readingSections.title: Age
readingSections.content:
Age is defined as a period of time that a person has lived or a thing has existed. Age is calculated in decades, years, months, days and so on.

Age-related problems typically involve data about the ages of two or more individuals and a correlation between their ages in the past, present, or future. Using the information, it is asked to calculate the ages of one or more persons in present/future/past.

readingSections.title: Things to remember
readingSections.content:
- (i) Hence (Later) = It shows the age of person in future.
- (ii) Thence (Ago) = It shows the age of person in past.
- (iii) If the present average age of a family or a group of persons is 'x' years then 'n' years ago the average age of a family or group of persons was $(x - n)$ years.
- (iv) If the present average age of a family or a group of persons is 'x' years then 'n' years later the average age of a family or a group of persons will be $(x + n)$ years.
- (v) Difference between ages of two person remains same at any point of time.
- (vi) When a child is born in the family then average age of the family is calculated by including the newly born child in the number of members of the family.

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content: If the ratio of present ages of M and N is x: y and n years ago, the ratio of their ages was p: q then $\frac{kx - n}{ky - n} = \frac{p}{q}$, where k is a constant.

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
The ratio of ages of P and Q at present is 3: 1, Four years earlier, the ratio was 4: 1. Find the age of Q after 12 years.

### Solution

### Method 1

According to concept,

$$\frac{3 \times k - 4}{1 \times k - 4} = \frac{4}{1}$$

$$3k - 4 = 4k - 16$$

$$k = 16 - 4 = 12$$

Age of Q after 12 years = $1 \times 12 + 12 = 24$ years

### Method 2

$$P^0 : Q^0 = 3 : 1 \} \times 3 = 9 : 3$$

$$P^{-4} : Q^{-4} = 4 : 1 \} \times 2 = 8 : 2$$

$$Q^0 = \frac{4}{1} \times 3 = 12 \text{ years}$$

Age of Q after 12 years = $1 \times 12 + 12 = 24$ years

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content: If the ratio of present ages of M and N is x: y and after n years, the ratio of their ages will be p: q then $\frac{kx + n}{ky + n} = \frac{p}{q}$, where k is a constant.

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
The ratio of ages of M and C at present is 6: 5, Fifteen years from now, the ratio will get changed to 9: 8. Find the age of M, 2 years ago.

### Solution

### Method 1

According to concept,

$$\frac{6 \times k + 15}{5 \times k + 15} = \frac{9}{8}$$

$$48k + 120 = 45k + 135$$

$$3k = 15; k = 5$$

Age of M, 2 years ago = $6 \times 5 - 2 = 28$ years

### Method 2

$$M^0 : C^0 = 6 : 5$$

$$M^{+15} : C^{+15} = 9 : 8$$

$$M^0 = \frac{15}{3} \times 6 = 30 \text{ years}$$

Age of M, 2 years ago = $30 - 2 = 28$ years

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
If 't' years after, age of one person is n times the age of another person and at present the age of first person is m times the age of another person, then

Age of first person = $$\operatorname{tm}\left(\frac{n-1}{m-n}\right)$$ years

Age of second person = $$t\left(\frac{n-1}{m-n}\right)$$ years

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
The present age of Komal is 5 times the age of Preeti. After 10 years, Komal will be 3 times as old as Preeti. What are the present ages of Komal and Preeti?

### Solution

### Method 1

Let the present age of Preeti = x years and present age of Komal = 5x years

According to question,

$$(5x + 10) = 3 \times (x + 10)$$

$$2x = 20$$

$$x = 10$$

Present age of Preeti = x years = 10 years

Present age of Komal = 5x years = 50 years

### Method 2

According to concept,

Komal's present age = $$\operatorname{tm}\left(\frac{n-1}{m-n}\right)$$ years

$$= 10 \times 5\left(\frac{3-1}{5-3}\right) = 50 \text{ years}$$

Preeti's present age = $$t\left(\frac{n-1}{m-n}\right)$$ years

$$= 10\left(\frac{3-1}{5-3}\right) = 10 \text{ years}$$

### Method 3

$$K^0 : P^0 = 5 : 1 \} \times 2 = 10 : 2$$

$$K^{+10} : P^{+10} = 3 : 1 \} \times 4 = 12 : 4$$

$$K^0 = \frac{10}{2} \times 10 = 50 \text{ years}$$

$$P^0 = \frac{10}{2} \times 2 = 10 \text{ years}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content:
If $$t_1$$ year before, age of a person was m times the age of another person. After $$t_2$$ year, age of a person will be n times the age of second person, then

Age of first person = $$\frac{t_2 m(n-1) + t_1 n(m-1)}{(m-n)}$$ years

Age of second person = $$\frac{t_2(n-1) + t_1(m-1)}{(m-n)}$$ years

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Manish told his granddaughter Mikki that five years earlier, he was seven times as old as she was. In 15 years, his age will be three times her age. What is the total of their current ages?

### Solution

### Method 1

Five years ago,

Let the age of Mikki = x - 5 years

and age of Manish = 7 (x - 5) years

According to question,

$$\{7(x - 5) + 20\} = (x - 5 + 20) \times 3$$

$$(7x - 35 + 20) = 3x + 45$$

$$7x - 15 = 3x + 45$$

$$4x = 60; x = 15$$

Present age of Mikki = x years = 15 years

Present age of Manish = $$\{7(x - 5) + 5\}$$ years = $$\{7(15 - 5) + 5\} = 75$$ years

Total of their present ages = 15 + 75 = 90 years

### Method 2

According to concept,

Age of first person = $$\frac{t_2 m(n-1) + t_1 n(m-1)}{(m-n)}$$ years

$$= \frac{15 \times 7(3-1) + 5 \times 3(7-1)}{(7-3)} \text{ years} = 75 \text{ years}$$

Age of second person = $$\frac{t_2(n-1) + t_1(m-1)}{(m-n)}$$ years

$$= \frac{15(3-1) + 5(7-1)}{(7-3)} = 15 \text{ years}$$

Sum of their present ages = 90 years

### Method 3

Manish$$^{-5}$$ : Mikki$$^{-5}$$ = 7 : 1 $$\} \times 2 = 14 : 2$$

Manish$$^{+15}$$ : Mikki$$^{+15}$$ = 3 : 1 $$\} \times 6 = 18 : 6$$

Manish$$^{-5}$$ = $$\frac{20}{4} \times 14 = 70$$ years

Mikki$$^{-5}$$ = $$\frac{20}{4} \times 2 = 10$$ years

Total of their present ages = 70 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 90 years

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
If M is as much elder to N as much he is younger to A and sum of ages of N and A is t years, N < M < A, then

M's age = $$\frac{\text{Sum of ages of N and A}}{2}$$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
If Shubhendra is as much elder as Navneet as he is younger to Shubham and sum of ages of Navneet and Shubham is 48 years, then find the age of Shubhendra.

### Solution

### Method 1

Shubhendra – Navneet = Shubham – Shubhendra

2 × Shubhendra = Navneet + Shubham

Shubhendra = ½ {Navneet + Shubham}

Shubhendra = ½ {48} = 24 years

### Method 2

According to concept,

Present age of Shubhendra =  $\frac{48}{2}$  = 24 years

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
4 years ago, N is four years younger than M. 6 years hence, ratio of ages of N to M will be 16 : 17. Find the sum of ages of both 4 years ago.

### Solution

Let age of N and M, 6 years hence be 16x & 17x respectively.

Difference of age of N & M remains same at any time.

So, 17x – 16x = 4

x = 4

Sum of ages of both, 4 years ago =  $(16 + 17) \times 4 - 10 \times 2 = 132 - 20 = 112$  years

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Average age of a family of three members 3 years ago is 22 years. A girl child was adopted in the family during this period. If average age of the family 42 months hence is 23.5 years then find the present age of the child.

### Solution

Sum of age of all members including child 3.5 years hence =  $23.5 \times 4 = 94$  years

Sum of age of all members excluding child 3.5 years hence =  $(22 + 3 + 3.5) \times 3 = 85.5$  years

Present age of child =  $94 - 85.5 - 3.5 = 5$  years

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Ratio of age of P and Q, 6 years ago was 3 : 4. Sum of the present age of Q and R is 80 years. R is 12 years elder to P. Find the difference of Q and R's age five years later?

### Solution

Let the present ages of P and Q be  $(3x + 6)$  years and  $(4x + 6)$  years respectively.

R's present age =  $(3x + 6 + 12)$  years =  $(3x + 18)$  years

According to the question,

Q + R = 80

4x + 6 + 3x + 18 = 80

7x + 24 = 80

7x = 56; x = 8

Required difference =  $(42 - 38)$  years = 4 years

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Ratio of present age of M and N is 3 : 2 and four years later age of N will be  $56\frac{1}{4}\%$  of age of A. If the average of the present age of M and A is 54 years, then find the present age of N.

### Solution

Let the present ages of M and N be 3x years and 2x years respectively.

4 years later,

N's age =  $(2x + 4)$  years

A's present age =  $\left[\frac{400}{225}\text{ of } (2x + 4) - 4\right] = \left[\frac{32x}{9} + \frac{28}{9}\right]$  years

According to the question,

$$\frac{\left[\frac{32x}{9} + \frac{28}{9} + 3x\right]}{2} = 54$$

x = 16

Present age of N =  $2 \times 16 = 32$  years

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
Three years ago, the average age of a family of 5 members was 17 years. A baby having been born, the average age of the family is the same today. The present age of the baby is:

### Solution

Total age of 5 members, 3 years ago =  $(17 \times 5) = 85$  years

Total age of 5 members, now =  $[85 + (3 \times 5)] = 85 + 15 = 100$  years

Total age of 6 members now =  $(17 \times 6) = 102$  years

The age of the baby =  $(102 - 100) = 2$  years.

chapters.content:
Chapter
7
PARTNERSHIP
A business partnership is a formal arrangement between
two or more individuals who have made investments in a
business, and these individuals are known as partners.
There are three types of business investments:
1. Monetary Investment (A)
2. Time Investment (T)
3. Work Investment (W)
To become a partner in a business, the main requirements
are monetary investment and time investment. The total
investment ‘I’ can be represented as I = A × T
Profits are distributed among partners according to the ratio
of their respective investments. This means that the ratio
of profit to investment remains constant. Therefore, we can
express this relationship as follows:
The ratio of profit (P) is equivalent to the ratio of investment (I).
Symbolically, this is represented as P ≡ I.
Concept:
If we denote the amount invested as A and the period of the
investment as T, we can derive the following relationships:
Case 1.
The profit (P) is equivalent to the product of the amount
invested (A) and the period (T).
Symbolically, P ≡ A × T.

Concept:
1. In a business partnership, if a partner withdraws a certain
amount, their share in the partnership is determined
by the remaining balance. On the other hand, if they
contribute additional funds, their share in the partnership
is considered to have increased.
2. The ratio of profit distribution is calculated based on the
product of the invested amount and the duration of the
investment.
Concept:
If the investment amounts are provided as fractions or percentages,
they can be directly incorporated into the calculations.
Alternatively, we can assign a suitable variable to represent
the investment amount as needed. This allows for flexibility in
handling various forms of investment representations.
Concept:
If an item is rented, the rent paid is proportional to its usage,
which is determined by the multiplication of several items
(N) used and the duration (T) of their use.
Rent paid = N × T

Concept:
An active partner often receives additional benefits in
the business or a fixed salary for their contributions to the
operational and managerial tasks.

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
PARTNERSHIP

A business partnership is a formal arrangement between two or more individuals who have made investments in a business, and these individuals are known as partners.

readingSections.title: There are three types of business investments
readingSections.content:
1. Monetary Investment (A)
2. Time Investment (T)
3. Work Investment (W)

To become a partner in a business, the main requirements are monetary investment and time investment. The total investment 'I' can be represented as I = A × T

Profits are distributed among partners according to the ratio of their respective investments. This means that the ratio of profit to investment remains constant. Therefore, we can express this relationship as follows:

The ratio of profit (P) is equivalent to the ratio of investment (I).

Symbolically, this is represented as P ≡ I.

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content: If we denote the amount invested as A and the period of the investment as T, we can derive the following relationships:

readingSections.title: Case 1.
readingSections.content:
The profit (P) is equivalent to the product of the amount invested (A) and the period (T).

Symbolically, P ≡ A × T.

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
In a business, A, B, and C invest Rs 9 crore for 2 years, Rs 4.5 crore for 1 year, and Rs 2.25 crore for 3 years respectively. At the end, A gets Rs 60 crore as profit. Then, find the total profit.

### Solution

Let's denote the profit as P which is proportional to the product of the amount invested (A) and the time period (T). So, P ≡ A × T.

Therefore, P_A : P_B : P_C = A_A × T_A : A_B × T_B : A_C × T_C
= 9,00,00,000 × 2 : 4,50,00,000 × 1 : 2,25,00,000 × 3 = 8 : 2 : 3

$$\text{Total profit} = \frac{60,00,00,000}{8} \times (8 + 2 + 3)$$
= 97,50,00,000
= Rs 97.5 crore.

readingSections.title: Case 2.
readingSections.content:
The amount invested (A) is equivalent to the profit (P) divided by the period (T).

$$\text{Symbolically, A} \equiv \frac{P}{T}.$$

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
A, B & C invested for 5 years, 3 years & 8 years respectively, if they earned profit in 5 : 4 : 3 then find the ratio of amount they invested.

### Solution

Given that A ≡ P/T, we have:

$$\text{Therefore, A}_A : A_B : A_C = \frac{P_A}{T_A} : \frac{P_B}{T_B} : \frac{P_C}{T_C} = \frac{5}{5} : \frac{4}{3} : \frac{3}{8} = 24 : 32 : 9$$

readingSections.title: Case 3.
readingSections.content:
The period (T) is equivalent to the profit (P) divided by the amount invested (A).

$$\text{Symbolically, T} \equiv \frac{P}{A}.$$

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
A, B & C invested in a business in 8 : 5 : 6, if profit distributed between them is 3 : 2 : 1, then find the ratio of time for which they invested.

### Solution

Given that T ≡ P/A, we have:

$$\text{Therefore, T}_A : T_B : T_C = \frac{P_A}{A_A} : \frac{P_B}{A_B} : \frac{P_C}{A_C} = \frac{3}{8} : \frac{2}{5} : \frac{1}{6} = 45 : 48 : 20$$

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
A, B & C invested in a business in 5:3:4, if profit distributed between them is 9:8:4, if A invested for 4.5 years then find the time of C.

### Solution

Given that $T \equiv \frac{P}{A}$ . we have:

Therefore, $T_A : T_B : T_C = \frac{P_A}{A_A} : \frac{P_B}{A_B} : \frac{P_C}{A_C} = \frac{9}{5} : \frac{8}{3} : \frac{4}{4} = 27 : 40 : 15$

Time of $C = \frac{4.5}{27} \times 15 = 2.5$ year

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If the period for the investment is not specified for each partner, it is assumed that all partners have invested for the same duration. This means that the time factor (T) is constant for all partners. Therefore, the distribution of profits will be based solely on the amount each partner has invested (A). In this case, the profit (P) for each partner is directly proportional to their investment amount.

Symbolically, $P \equiv A$.

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Amit, Sandeep, and Ritu started a business venture with investments of Rs 12,500, Rs 3,000, and Rs 8,000 respectively. Let's determine the profit ratio at the end of their business operations.

### Solution

Profit ratio of Amit: Sandeep: Ritu = 12500: 3000: 8000 = 25: 6: 16.

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
1. In a business partnership, if a partner withdraws a certain amount, their share in the partnership is determined by the remaining balance. On the other hand, if they contribute additional funds, their share in the partnership is considered to have increased.
2. The ratio of profit distribution is calculated based on the product of the invested amount and the duration of the investment.

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Mr. Sinha, along with his two friends, Mr. Ratan and Miss Supriya, embarked on a business venture. They invested amounts of Rs. 20,00,000, Rs. 15,00,000, and Rs. 30,00,000 respectively. However, after four months into the business, Mr. Sinha further invested an additional Rs. 5,00,000 while Miss Supriya withdrew Rs. 10,00,000 from the business. Calculate the ratio in which profit is distributed at the end of one year.

### Solution

The profit distribution ratio is calculated based on the amount of money invested and the duration of the investment. Here's how it's done:

- Mr. Sinha: $(20,00,000 \times 4 \text{ months}) + (25,00,000 \times 8 \text{ months}) = \text{Rs. } 2,80,00,000$

Mr. Ratan: \(15,00,000\times 12\) months \(=\) Rs.1,80,00,000
- Miss Supriya: \((30,00,000 \times 4\) months) + \((20,00,000 \times 8\) months) = Rs. 2,80,00,000

So the profit distribution ratio of Mr. Sinha : Mr. Ratan : Miss Supriya = 2,80,00,000 : 1,80,00,000 : 2,80,00,000 = 14 : 9 : 14

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content: If the investment amounts are provided as fractions or percentages, they can be directly incorporated into the calculations. Alternatively, we can assign a suitable variable to represent the investment amount as needed. This allows for flexibility in handling various forms of investment representations.

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Individuals A, B, and C initiated a business venture. A contributed 25% of the total investment for 6 months, while B invested one-third of the total amount for 9 months and C invested for a complete year. Calculate the profit distribution ratio among A, B, and C.

### Solution

The profit distribution ratio is calculated based on the amount of investment and the period for which the investment is made. Here's the calculation:

A's share: \(0.25 \times 6 = 1.5\)
B's share: \(\frac{1}{3} \times 9 = 3\)
C's share: \((1 - 0.25 - \frac{1}{3}) \times 12 = 5\)

So, the profit distribution ratio among A, B, and C is 1.5 : 3 : 5 = 3 : 6 : 10

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
If an item is rented, the rent paid is proportional to its usage, which is determined by the multiplication of several items (N) used and the duration (T) of their use.

Rent paid = N × T

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Rohit and Suman rent a pasture. Rohit uses the pasture for 5 cows for 4 months, with each cow grazing for 10 hours each day. On the other hand, Suman uses the pasture for 20 cows for 1 month, with each cow grazing for 5 hours each day. Calculate the ratio in which they pay the rent.

### Solution

Rohit's usage: 5 cows × 4 months × 10 hours/day = 200

Suman's usage: 20 cows × 1 month × 5 hours/day = 100

So, the rent ratio Rohit : Suman is 200 : 100 or simplified to 2 : 1.

readingSections.title: TYPE OF PARTNER
readingSections.content:
Partners in a business can be categorized primarily into two types: active partners and sleeping partners.

70

1. **Active partner:** An active partner is one who not only invests capital into the business but also actively participates in its day-to-day operations and management.
2. **Sleeping partner:** On the other hand, a sleeping partner is an investor who contributes capital to the business but does not participate in its daily affairs or decision-making processes.

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content: An active partner often receives additional benefits in the business or a fixed salary for their contributions to the operational and managerial tasks.

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Akhil and Bipin have formed a partnership in which Akhil is the active partner. They have invested Rs 48,000 and Rs 72,000 respectively. As compensation for managing the business, Akhil receives 10% of the profit. Find out how profit should be distributed.

### Solution

Given total profit = 100%, time = T

Akhil's share = Rs 48000 × T

Bipin's share = Rs 72000 × T

The profit ratio is then calculated as follows: Akhil: Bipin = Rs 48000 × T: Rs 72000 × T = 2:3

Akhil's % share = 10% + (90% × $\frac{2}{5}$) = 46%

Bipin's % share = 54%

Final profit ratio = 23:27

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A and B invested Rs 39 lakhs and Rs 65 lakhs respectively. At the end of the year, A claimed $\frac{3}{5}$ of the total profit. For how many days did B invest? (Assuming that each month has 30 days.)

### Solution

A claimed 3 unit profit out of 5 so the ratio of profit of A and B = 3 : 2 and time of A will be 12 months = 12 × 30 = 360 days

Therefore,  $T_A : T_B = \frac{P_A}{A_A} : \frac{P_B}{A_B}$

$$= \frac{3}{3900000} : \frac{2}{6500000} = 5 : 2$$

Time of B = $\frac{360}{5} \times 2 = 144$ days

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
A, B and C are partners in a business, A receives $\frac{3}{7}$ of profit while B and C shares remaining profit equally. A's income is increased by 1260 Rs when profit rises from 5% to 12%. Find the profit of B.

### Solution

Ratio of Profit of A, B and C = 3 : 2 : 2

Total income of A = $\frac{1260}{7\%} \times 100\% = 18000$

Time of all are equal so time of everyone is taken T so Amount is directly proportional to profit distributed

Therefore ratio of amount invested,  $A_A : A_B : A_C = P_A : P_B : P_C = 3 : 2 : 2$

Profit of B = $\frac{18000}{3} \times 2 = 12000$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
In a business, A and B invested Rs 16,000 and Rs 12,000 respectively. The government applied a flat tax of 20% on the total profit. After 10 years of operation, what will be the profit earned by A if they also donate 10% to an organization for the education of students and the total amount earned is Rs 35000?

### Solution

Ratio of Profit of A and B for equal time = 16000 : 12000 = 4 : 3

Let's consider total profit = 100%

After deduction of Government tax and donation = (100 - 20 - 10)% = 70%

Amount gets by A = $\frac{70\%}{7} \times 4 = 40\%$

Amount gets by B = $\frac{70\%}{7} \times 3 = 30\%$

Profit of A = $\frac{35,000}{100\%} \times 40\% = Rs 14,000$

MIXTURE
“Mixtures and Alligations” is a mathematical concept that involves
the combination of different elements to achieve specific levels,
percentages, or concentrations. This concept is used to simplify
questions, in which two or more substances are mixed, or when a
mixture already exists and we need to alligate it.
If two substances are mixed, with values “c” and “d” respectively,
and after mixing they create a substance with a new value, which
is called its mean value “m”, then the difference between “c” and
“m” and the difference between “d” and “m” will give the ratio of
the quantities of “d” and “c” respectively.
Some points to remember:

number altogether.

readingSections.title: The alligation rule
readingSections.content:
“Mixtures and Alligations” is a mathematical concept that involves the combination of different elements to achieve specific levels, percentages, or concentrations. This concept is used to simplify questions, in which two or more substances are mixed, or when a mixture already exists and we need to alligate it.

If two substances are mixed, with values “c” and “d” respectively, and after mixing they create a substance with a new value, which is called its mean value “m”, then the difference between “c” and “m” and the difference between “d” and “m” will give the ratio of the quantities of “d” and “c” respectively.

![Book diagram, page 75](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p75-img-14.jpeg)

Some points to remember:

1. The units of c, d, and m are always the same. Since these are in ratio, we can multiply or divide c, d, and m by any number altogether.
2. Values of (d ~ m) and (c ~ m) will always be taken as positive.
3. (d ~ m) and (c ~ m) represent the ratios of quantities of c and d respectively. So we can say that

$$\frac{\text{Quantity of } c}{\text{Quantity of } d} = \frac{d \sim m}{c \sim m}$$

readingSections.title: Example 1 · Wheat prices
readingSections.content:
In what proportion should wheat at Rs. 45.50/kg be mixed with wheat at Rs.40.50/kg so that the mixture is worth Rs.44/kg?

### Solution

Method 1: The ratio of the quantity of wheat priced at Rs 45.50 to the quantity of wheat priced at Rs 40.50 is calculated as follows: 40.5~44 : 45.5~44 = 3.5 : 1.5 = 7 : 3

### Method 2

![Book diagram, page 75](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p75-img-15.jpeg)

The ratio of wheat of Rs 45.5 per kg to Rs 40.5 per kg = 3.5 : 1.5=7 : 3

readingSections.title: Example 2 · Population growth
readingSections.content:
The current population of a city is 8000. If the number of men increases by 12% and the number of women increases by 18%, the total population becomes 9200. What was the original number of men in the city?

### Solution

The “mixture” is the total population increase, which is $$\frac{(9200 - 8000)}{8000} \times 100\% = 15\%$$

So, we have:

Men: 12% increase, Women: 18% increase, Total: 15% increase

![Book diagram, page 75](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p75-img-16.jpeg)

the ratio of men: the ratio of women = 18% ~ 15% : 12% ~ 15% = 3% : 3% = 1 : 1

So, the ratio of men to women in the original population is 1 : 1.

Therefore, the original number of men in the city was half of the total population,

$$\text{Which is } \frac{8000}{2} = 4000$$

readingSections.title: Example 3 · Coffee and profit
readingSections.content:
How many kg of coffee costing Rs 75 per kg must be mixed with 50 kg of coffee costing Rs 120 per kg, so that a seller makes a profit of 20% by selling the mixture at the rate of Rs 100 per kg?

### Solution

Because 75 Rs /kg and 120 Rs/kg are the cost price so mean value should also be the cost price

$$\text{So, Mean value } m = 100 \times \frac{100}{120} = \frac{250}{3}$$

![Book diagram, page 76](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p76-img-17.jpeg)

$$\text{The ratio of the 75 per kg to 120 per kg} = \frac{110}{3} : \frac{25}{3} = 22 : 5$$

$$\text{Quantity of Rs 75 per kg coffee} = 50 \times \frac{22}{5} = 220 \text{ kg}$$

readingSections.title: Mixing containers of different volumes
readingSections.content:
If the mixture of two liquids, for example milk and water in two containers is a:b and c:d and the ratio of volume of container is x: y then if these are mixed in a third container then the ratio of quantity of milk and water is

$$[ax(c+d)+cy(a+b)] : [bx(c+d)+dy(a+b)]$$

readingSections.title: Example 4 · Combining two vessels
readingSections.content:
Two vessels, A and B, have volumes in the ratio of 3 : 2. They contain milk and water in the ratios of 1 : 2 and 3 : 2 respectively. If these liquids are poured into a third container, C, then what is the ratio of milk to water in C?

### Solution

The ratio of the quantity of milk and water is $[ax(c+d)+cy(a+b)] : [bx(c+d)+dy(a+b)]$.

For vessel A (milk:water = a:b = 1:2, volume = x = 3), and for vessel B (milk:water = c:d = 3:2, volume = y = 2)

$$\text{Milk quantity in C} = ax(c+d) + cy(a+b) = 1 \times 3(3+2) + 3 \times 2(1+2) = 15 + 18 = 33 \text{ units}$$

$$\text{Water quantity in C} = bx(c+d) + dy(a+b) = 2 \times 3(3+2) + 2 \times 2(1+2) = 30 + 12 = 42 \text{ units}$$

So, according to formula, the ratio of milk to water in container C would be 33:42 = 11:14

readingSections.title: Mixing equal volumes
readingSections.content:
If the mixture of two liquids for example milk and water in two containers is a:b and c:d and the volume of both container is equal then if these are mixed in a third container then the ratio of quantity of milk and water is

$$[a(c+d)+c(a+b)] : [b(c+d)+d(a+b)]$$

readingSections.title: Example 5 · Equal-capacity containers
readingSections.content:
Two containers, X and Y, of equal capacities contain juice and water in the ratios of 2:3 and 1:4 respectively. If these liquids are poured into a third container, Z, then what is the ratio of juice to water in Z?

### Solution

Given that the ratio of juice to water in container X is 2 : 3 (a : b) and in container Y is 1 : 4 (c : d).

According to the given concept, the ratio of juice to water in container Z will be $[a(c+d)+c(a+b)] : [b(c+d)+d(a+b)]$.

$$\text{Juice in Z} = [2 \times (1+4)+1 \times (2+3)] = [2 \times 5 + 1 \times 5] = 15 \text{ units}$$

$$\text{Water in Z} = [3 \times (1+4)+4 \times (2+3)] = [3 \times 5 + 4 \times 5] = 35 \text{ units}$$

So, the ratio of juice to water in container Z is 15:35=3:7

readingSections.title: Example 6 · Profit by adding water
readingSections.content:
If a person sells milk at the same price as he bought it, but adds some water to it, what ratio of milk to water he will add to get a profit of 25%?

### Solution

**Method 1:** He will not receive profit from just selling milk. However, if he adds water, we can consider the milk to be 100% and the profit to be 25%. This implies that the water is 25%, so the ratio of milk to water is 100%:25%=4:1

**Method 2:** Let the cost price of milk = Rs 125

So the selling price of the mixture = Rs 125

$$\text{So, cost price of mixture} = 125 \times 100/125 = \text{Rs } 100$$

Cost price of water = 0

![Book diagram, page 76](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p76-img-18.jpeg)

The ratio of milk to water is 100 : 25 = 4 : 1

readingSections.title: Adding one liquid to a mixture
readingSections.content:
In a mixture of milk and water in a container, the ratio is a : b. If x liters of milk is added, then the new ratio of milk and water changes to c : d.

The quantity of milk in the original mixture is given =  $$\frac{x}{cb - ad} \times ad$$

Similarly, the quantity of water in the original mixture is given =  $$\frac{x}{cb - ad} \times bd$$

Also, make sure that 'cb' is not equal to 'ad' to avoid division by zero.

readingSections.title: Example 7 · Adding water to juice
readingSections.content:
A solution contains juice and water in a ratio of 4 : 1. On adding 25 liters of water, the ratio of juice to water becomes 2 : 3. What is the quantity of juice in the solution?

### Solution

From the problem, we have:

- a = 4, b = 1 (from the original ratio)
- c = 2, d = 3 (from the final ratio)
- x = 25 (amount of water added)

According to your concept,

The quantity of juice in the original mixture is given

$$= \frac{x}{cb - ad} \times ac = \frac{25}{(2 \times 1) - (4 \times 3)} \times 4 \times 2 = 20 \text{ liter}$$

readingSections.title: Mixing three ingredients
readingSections.content: If three gradients are mixed, the mean value can be achieved by combining two different gradients twice and adding the common gradient in both to achieve the ratio.

readingSections.title: Example 8 · Three varieties of rice
readingSections.content:
Three varieties of wheat, priced at Rs 1.35, Rs 1.38, and Rs 1.41 per kg, are combined to be sold at Rs 1.39 per kg. What should be the ratio in which these varieties of wheat are mixed?

### Solution

![Book diagram, page 77](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p77-img-19.jpeg)

Now the ratio of the quantity of wheat of price 1.35 , 1.38, 1.41 = 0.02 : 0.02 : (0.04 + 0.01) = 0.02 : 0.02 : 0.05 = 2 : 2 : 5

readingSections.title: Head-and-leg problems
readingSections.content:
If the total head and total leg are given H & L of two animal A and B particularly has a and b leg respectively then

The Quantity of animal A =  $$\frac{L - (H \times b)}{a - b}$$

Quantity of animal B =  $$\frac{(H \times a) - L}{a - b}$$



> **Correction:** The source reverses the numerator for animal A. From A + B = H and aA + bB = L, A = (L − bH)/(a − b). The corrected formula is shown above.

readingSections.title: Example 9 · Cows and hens
readingSections.content:
A farmer has a mix of ducks and horses on his farm. When he counts the heads, he finds there are 60 in total. However, when he counts the legs, he finds there are 200 in total. How many ducks the farmer has?

### Solution

For ducks (A) and horses (B), we know that a duck has 2 legs (a=2) and a horse has 4 legs (b=4). The total number of heads (H) is 60 and the total number of legs (L) is 200.

Quantity of ducks A =  $$\frac{(H \times b) - L}{a - b} = \frac{(60 \times 4) - 200}{4 - 2} = 20$$

So, the farmer has 20 ducks.

readingSections.title: Repeated replacement
readingSections.content:
In a mixture, if we substitute x liters of a pure substance A with substance B, and repeat this process n times, the quantity of A that remains in the mixture can be calculated using the following formula:

$$F = I \left( 1 - \frac{x}{I} \right)^n$$

In this formula:

- F represents the final quantity of substance A
- I stand for the initial quantity of substance A
- x is the volume that has been replaced
- n is the number of times the replacement occurred

readingSections.title: Example 10 · Replacing juice four times
readingSections.content:
A tank holds 100 liters of juice. 10 liters of juice is removed and replaced with water. This operation is performed four times. How much juice remains in the tank?

### Solution

The formula is:  $$F = I \left( 1 - \frac{x}{I} \right)^n$$

- I = 100 liters (initial quantity of juice)
- x = 10 liters (volume of juice that is replaced each time)

• n = 4 (number of times the replacement occurred)

Substituting these values into the formula, we get:

$$F = I \left( 1 - \frac{x}{I} \right)^n = 100 \times \left( 1 - \frac{10}{100} \right)^4 = 65.61 \text{ liter}$$



> **Transcription correction:** The denominator in the replacement formula is I (initial volume), not the digit 1. The numerical substitution and result are unchanged.

readingSections.title: Example 11 · Finding the original volume
readingSections.content:
A crafty juice vendor has removed 20 L of juice from a jug and replaced it with the same amount of water. This process was repeated 4 times. As a result, the ratio of juice to water became 625: 671. Can you determine the initial volume of juice in the jug?

### Solution

Let's assume initial juice I = 625x + 671x = 1296 x

Final juice F = 625x

The formula is: $$F = I \left( 1 - \frac{x}{I} \right)^n$$

$$625x = 1296x \left( 1 - \frac{20}{I} \right)^4$$

I = 120 liter

The concept of “percentage” comes from the Latin term “per
centum,” which means “for every hundred.” It’s a way to
express a number or ratio as a fraction of 100, represented by
the symbol “%”.
For example, 50% is the same as 50 out of 100, or half.
The percentage difference between two numbers is
calculated by subtracting the smaller number from the larger
one, dividing the result by the original number, and then
multiplying by 100 to convert it into a percentage.

week you scored 90 out of 100. The percentage difference

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
The concept of “percentage” comes from the Latin term “per centum,” which means “for every hundred.” It’s a way to express a number or ratio as a fraction of 100, represented by the symbol “%”.

For example, 50% is the same as 50 out of 100, or half.

The percentage difference between two numbers is calculated by subtracting the smaller number from the larger one, dividing the result by the original number, and then multiplying by 100 to convert it into a percentage.

Let’s say you scored 80 out of 100 on a test last week and this week you scored 90 out of 100. The percentage difference would be calculated as

$$\frac{90-80}{80} \times 100 = 12.5\%.$$ This indicates that your score has increased by 12.5% from last week to this week.

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Two students Aman and Sohan score 150 and 240 in different exams whose total marks of exams are 200 and 300 then find whose performance is better?

### Solution

readingSections.title: Conversion from Percentage to Fraction
readingSections.content:
The process of converting a percentage into a fraction involves two steps:

Express the percentage as a fraction of 100.

Reduce the fraction to its simplest form.

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
Let's take 45 as an example:

### Solution

We first write 45% as a fraction of 100 = $\frac{45}{100}$.

So we get $\frac{9}{20}$.

Therefore, 45% is equivalent to the fraction of $\frac{9}{20}$

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
Convert 166.66% to a fraction.

### Solution

The fraction value of 66.66% is $\frac{2}{3}$.

100% = 1

So, 166.66% (100%+66.66%) = $1 + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{5}{3}$

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Convert 387.5% to a fraction.

### Solution

The fraction value of 87.5% is $\frac{7}{8}$.

100% = 1 & 300% = 3

So, 387.5% (300% + 87.5%) = $3 + \frac{7}{8} = \frac{31}{8}$

readingSections.title: Conversion from Fraction to Percentage
readingSections.content: To transform a fraction into a percentage, you first do the division operation that the fraction represents (i.e., numerator divided by denominator), then multiply fraction by 100.

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Convert $\frac{3}{4}$ to percentage.

### Solution

Multiply by 100: $\frac{3}{4} \times 100\% = 75\%$.

So, when expressed as a percentage, $\frac{3}{4}$ becomes 75%.

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Convert 375% into fraction.

### Solution

So, 375% becomes $\frac{375}{100}$.

Next, simplify this fraction.

When you divide both the numerator and denominator by 25, you get $\frac{15}{4}$.

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Find the value of 60% of 25% of 83.33% of 21600.

### Solution

60% of 25% of 83.33% of 21600

$= \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{5}{6} \times 21600 = 2700$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Find the value of 360% of 233.33% of 8100.

### Solution

360% of 233.33% of 8100 = $\left(3 + \frac{3}{5}\right) \times \left(2 + \frac{1}{3}\right) \times 8100$

$= \frac{18}{5} \times \frac{7}{3} \times 8100 = 68040$

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
If 66.66% of a number is added itself then it becomes 75 then find the original number.

### Solution

66.66% = $\frac{2}{3}$

By unit original number is 3 unit

Final number = $3 + 2 = 5$ unit

Then original number = $\frac{75}{5} \times 3 = 45$

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
If a number is decreased by 62.5% then it decreases 39 then find the number after decrement.

### Solution

62.5% = $\frac{5}{8}$

Original number = 8 unit, Final number = 5 unit, Reduction in number = $8 - 5 = 3$ unit

Number after decrement = $\frac{39}{3} \times 5 = 65$

readingSections.title: Formula for Calculating a Percentage
readingSections.content:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{\text{TARGET VALUE}}{\text{BASE VALUE}} \times 100\%$$

Here, the 'Target Value' is the value whose percentage we are seeking to determine,

The 'Base Value' is the value that serves as a reference point or standard for comparison.

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
54 days is what percent of 27 weeks?

### Solution

To find out what percent 54 days is of 27 weeks, we first need to convert the weeks into days. Since there are 7 days in a week, 27 weeks would be $27 \times 7 = 189$ days.

The formula to calculate the percentage is:

$$\frac{\text{TARGET VALUE}}{\text{BASE VALUE}} \times 100\% = \frac{54}{189} \times 100 \approx 28.57\%$$

readingSections.title: For Percentage Change in Value, We Can Use the Formula Given Below
readingSections.content:
The formulas given are used to calculate percentage change. The decreased percentage formula calculates the percentage decrease between two numbers, using the larger value as the base. The increased percentage formula calculates the percentage increase, using the smaller value as the base.

1. **Decreased percentage** = $\frac{\text{Difference of the number}}{\text{Larg er value}} \times 100\%$
2. **Increased percentage** = $\frac{\text{Difference of the number}}{\text{Smaller value}} \times 100\%$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
Ram weighs 65 kg and Raman weighs 39 kg. Determine the percentage by which Raman's weight is less than Ram's weight.

### Solution

To find the percentage by which Raman's weight is less than Ram's weight, we can use the formula for the percentage difference:

Percentage Difference

$$= \frac{\text{Difference in Weight}}{\text{Weight of Ram}} \times 100\%$$

Difference in Weight

= Weight of Ram - Weight of Raman = 65 kg - 39 kg = 26 kg
So, Percentage Difference = $\frac{26}{65} \times 100 = 40\%$

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
In a race between Radha and Vasudha, Vasudha travels 150 meters at the same time while Radha travels 250 meters. Find out how much more percentage Radha travels than Vasudha.

### Solution

Increased percentage

$$= \frac{\text{Difference of the number}}{\text{Smaller value}} \times 100\%$$

Here, the difference in the number is Radha's distance - Vasudha's distance

=250 meters - 150 meters = 100 meters

The smaller value is Vasudha's distance =150 meters

$$\text{Increased percentage} = \frac{100}{150} \times 100\% = 66.67\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
The price of a product was $50 last year. This year, the price has increased to $65. Find out how much percentage the price has increased.

### Solution

The increased percentage can be calculated using the formula:

Increased percentage

$$= \frac{\text{Difference of the number}}{\text{Smaller value}} \times 100$$

Here, the difference in the number is this year's price minus last year's price, which equals $65 - $50 = $15.

The smaller value is last year's price, which is $50.

$$\text{Increased percentage} = \frac{15}{50} \times 100\% = 30\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
If 33.33% of (2A+B) =83.33% of (A-B), then what % of B is equal to A?

### Solution

If 33.33% of (2A+B) =83.33% of (A-B)

$$\frac{1}{3} \times (2A + B) = \frac{5}{6} \times (A - B)$$

$$2 \times (2A + B) = 5 \times (A - B)$$

$$4A + 2B = 5A - 5B$$

$$A = 7B$$

$$A : B = 7 : 1$$

$$\% = \frac{A}{B} \times 100\% = \frac{7}{1} \times 100\% = 700\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 16
readingSections.content:
If the price of kerosene is increased by 75%, by what percentage should a person reduce his consumption to keep his expenditure unchanged?

### Solution

Assume the initial price and initial expenditure = Rs 100.

The final price of kerosene after a 75% increase = 100 × 175% = Rs 175.

The percentage reduction in consumption can be calculated using the formula:

$$\frac{\text{Final Price} - \text{Initial Price}}{\text{Final Price}} \times 100\%$$

Substituting the values, we get: $\frac{175-100}{175} \times 100\% = 42.86\%$

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
If A is 20% more than B, and B is 20% less than C, then A is what percentage more or less than C?

### Solution

Let's assume C = 100.

B is 20% less than C, which means B = 80% of C

$$= \frac{80}{100} \times 100 = 80.$$

A is 20% more than B, which means A = 120% of B

$$= \frac{120}{100} \times 80 = 96.$$

Now, A is less than C by percentage calculated as follows:

$$\frac{100-96}{100} \times 100\% = 4\%.$$

Therefore, A is 4% less than C.

readingSections.title: Example 18
readingSections.content:
In an examination that consists of questions from Hindi, English, Maths, and Computer subjects. If Maths contains 35% of the questions, English contains 15%, Hindi contains 10%, and Computers contain 120 questions, then how many more questions are there in Maths than in Hindi?

### Solution

The total percentage of questions asked in Computer is 100% - (35% + 15% + 10%) = 40%.

In Maths, there are 35% - 10% = 25% more questions asked than in Hindi.

Now, More question in Maths than Hindi = $\frac{120}{40\%} \times 25\% = 75$

readingSections.title: For Any Error, We Can Use the Formula Given Below
readingSections.content: The Percentage Error formula is a statistical tool used to measure the discrepancy between an observed value and the actual value. It's calculated by subtracting the observed value from the actual value, dividing by the actual value, and multiplying by 100%.

readingSections.title: Percentage Error
readingSections.content: $$= \frac{\text{Actual Value} - \text{Observed Value}}{\text{Actual Value}} \times 100\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 19
readingSections.content:
If a number is divided by 25 instead of multiplied by 25 then what % error will occur in the result?

### Solution

Let's solve this problem step by step:

1. If a number is multiplied by 25, the result is $100 \times 25 = 2500$.
2. If the same number is divided by 25 instead, the result is $100 / 25 = 4$.

Now, Percentage Error

$$= \frac{\text{Actual Value} - \text{Observed Value}}{\text{Actual Value}} \times 100\%$$

Substituting the actual value (2500) and the observed value (4) into the formula, we get:

$$\text{Percentage Error} = \frac{2500-4}{2500} \times 100\% = 99.84\% \text{ error}$$

readingSections.title: Example 20
readingSections.content:
If a shopkeeper sells his 30% article and remains with 630 articles then how many articles did he have originally?

### Solution

30% articles sold,

so remaining articles = 100% - 30% = 70%

According to question, 70% = 630

$$1\% = \frac{630}{70} = 9$$

Original articles 100% = 9 × 100 = 900

readingSections.title: Example 21
readingSections.content:
In a town, 20% of males, 25% of females, and 40% of children died due to COVID-19. If the previous population of males, females, and children was 5000, 8000, and 12000 respectively, find the percentage of the population that died in the town.

### Solution

Let's calculate the number of people who died in each group:

- Males: 20% of 5000 = 1000
- Females: 25% of 8000 = 2000
- Children: 40% of 12000 = 4800

So, the total number of people who died is 1000 + 2000 + 4800 = 7800.

The total population of the town was 5000 + 8000 + 12000 = 25000.

Therefore, the percentage of the population that died

$$= \frac{7800}{25000} \times 100\% = 31.2\%.$$

readingSections.title: Example 22
readingSections.content:
If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 20% and its denominator is decreased by 30% then the fraction becomes $\frac{3}{14}$ then find the original fraction.

### Solution

Let the original fraction is $\frac{a}{b}$

$$\text{New fraction} = \frac{120\% \text{ of } a}{70\% \text{ of } b} = \frac{3}{14}$$

On solving this

$$\text{Original fraction} = \frac{a}{b} = \frac{1}{8}$$

readingSections.title: Example 23
readingSections.content:
If the flat income tax rate is increased by 0.5%, then a woman has to pay an extra Rs 2000. What is her income?

### Solution

Increased tax percentage = extra tax

$$0.5\% = 2000$$

$$\text{Income} = \frac{2000}{0.5} \times 100 = 400000$$

readingSections.title: Example 24
readingSections.content:
A company offers a 12% commission on the total sales made by a salesman, along with a bonus of 4% on sales exceeding Rs 30000. If his total sales amount to Rs 50000, calculate his income.

### Solution

The commission is 12% of the total sales. So, for a total sale of Rs 50000, the commission = $\frac{12}{100} \times 50000 = \text{Rs } 6000$

The salesman gets a bonus of 4% on the sales over Rs 30000 = 4% of $(50000 - 30000) = \frac{4}{100} \times 20000 = 800$

Therefore, his income $6000 + 800 = \text{Rs } 6800$

readingSections.content:
A man spends 60% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure also increases by 60%, what is the net percentage change in his savings?

### Solution

Let the initial income of man = Rs 100

readingSections.title: Marks is divided into two parts
readingSections.content:
1. **Aggregate Score:** This is the cumulative score that can be achieved in an examination, which is equivalent to 100%. It represents the maximum score a student can obtain in the given examination. This is also known as **maximum marks**.
2. **Passing Score:** Commonly referred to as passing marks, these are the least number of marks a student needs to secure to pass the examination. The requirement for these marks can vary based on the specific regulations of each examination. This is also known as **minimum marks**.

readingSections.title: Example 27
readingSections.content:
A student scores 32% marks and fails by 32 marks while another student gets 48% marks and gets 48 marks more than the passing marks. Find the maximum marks of the examination.

### Solution

Let's denote the maximum marks as 100%.

- The first student scored 32% of the maximum marks and failed by 32 marks. So, the passing marks are $32\% + 32$.
- The second student scored 48% of the maximum marks, which is 48 marks more than the passing marks. So, the passing marks are also $48\% - 48$.

Setting these two equations equal to each other gives us:

$$32\% + 32 = 48\% - 48$$

Solving this equation:

$$48\% - 32\% = 32 + 48$$

$$16\% = 80$$

$$\text{So, } 100\% = \frac{80}{16} \times 100\% = 500$$

readingSections.title: Example 28
readingSections.content:
In an exam, 18% of students failed in English 24% failed in Math and 11% of students failed in both subjects. Then find % of students who passed in both subjects.

### Solution

Add the percentages of students who failed in English and Math, which is 18% + 24% = 42%.

- Then, subtract the percentage of students who failed in both subjects, because they were counted twice in the previous step. So, 42% - 11% = 31%.
- The percentage of students who passed both subjects. So, 100% - 31% = 69%.

readingSections.title: Net Change
readingSections.content: When a value is continuously increased or decreased by a certain percentage, and each time the new result becomes the base value for the next calculation, this process is known as **successive change**. The total effect of this process is referred to as the **net change**. For example, if a value increases by 10% and then decreases by 10%, the net change will not be zero due to the successive change effect.

readingSections.title: Here are the formulas for net change
readingSections.content:
- For two successive changes, the formula
  $$= \left( a + b + \frac{ab}{100} \right) \%$$
- For three successive changes, the formula
  $$= \left( a + b + c + \frac{ab}{100} + \frac{bc}{100} + \frac{ca}{100} + \frac{abc}{100^2} \right) \%$$

**Note:** For a percentage increase, use a positive value in the formula. In case of a decrease in percentage, use a negative value in the formula.

readingSections.title: Example 29
readingSections.content:
If the population of a village is increased by 25% and 40% per year respectively then what will be the % change in population after 2 years?

### Solution

### Method 1

Let's assume we have two percentages, a and b, where a = 25% and b = 40%.

$$\left( a + b + \frac{ab}{100} \right) \%$$

Applying our values to this formula, we get:

$$= \left( 25 + 40 + \frac{25 \times 40}{100} \right) \% = 75\%$$

### Method 2

Let's assume the present population of the village is 100.

After the first year, the population increases by 25%, so it becomes 100 + 25% of 100 = 100 $\left( 1 + \frac{25}{100} \right) = 125$.

After the second year, this population further increases by 40%, so it becomes 125 + 40% of 125 = 125

$$\left( 1 + \frac{40}{100} \right) = 175.$$

So, population increased from 100 to 175,

Hence 75% increment in population.

### Method 3

Let initial population be 100

In first year 25% population increase = $\frac{1}{4}$ i.e $\frac{5}{4}$

In second year 40% population increase = $\frac{2}{5}$ i.e. $\frac{7}{5}$

Population after 2 years = $100 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{7}{5} = 175$

So percentage increase = $\frac{175 - 100}{100} \times 100 = 75\%$

readingSections.title: Example 30
readingSections.content:
If the length of a rectangle is increased by 83.33% and its width is decreased by 62.5% then what percentage change will occur in its area?

### Solution

The fraction value of an 83.33% increase is $\frac{5}{6}$.

6 represents the original length

New length becomes 6 + 5 = 11.

The fraction value of a 62.5% decrease is $\frac{5}{8}$. Here, 8 represent the original width

New width becomes 8 - 5 = 3.

The original area = 6 × 8 = 48.

The new area = 11 × 3 = 33.

The percentage decrease in area =

$$\frac{\text{Original Area} - \text{New Area}}{\text{Original Area}} \times 100\%$$

$$= \frac{48 - 33}{48} \times 100\% = \frac{15}{48} \times 100\% \approx 31.25\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 31
readingSections.content:
Ram spends 25% of his salary on food, on remaining 20% on rent, on the remaining 60% on travel and remains with Rs 2160/-, Then Find his salary.

### Solution

Let's assume the salary of Ram = a.

The remaining salary after deductions are given by the formula: a × (100-25)% × (100-20)% × (100-60)%

Substituting the given value into the formula, we get:

$$a \times 75\% \times 80\% \times 40\% = \text{Rs } 2160$$

Solving for 'a', we get: a = Rs 9000

So, Ram's salary is Rs 9000

readingSections.title: If Person Reduce His Consumption Because of Increment In Price
readingSections.content:
**Case 1.** If person did not change his expense due to increment in price x% then

$$\text{Percentage reduction in consumption} = \frac{x}{100 + x} \times 100\%$$

**Case 2.** If person changes his expense y% due to increment in price x% then

$$\text{Percentage reduction in consumption} = \frac{x - y}{100 + x} \times 100\%$$

readingSections.title: Example 32
readingSections.content:
Due to the increase in the price of flour 40%, by what percentage should Raman reduce his consumption if

- a) He does not want to change his expenses
- b) He increases his expense by 8%
- c) He decreases his expense by 20%

### Solution

**a) Method 1:** If price increment = x%

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Reduction in consumption in \%} &= \frac{x}{100 + x} \times 100\% \\ &= \frac{40}{100 + 40} \times 100\% = 28.56\% \end{aligned}$$

**Method 2 : Short trick:** Fraction value of 40% = $\frac{2}{5}$

$$\text{The percentage value of fraction} = \frac{2}{5 + 2} \times 100\% = 28.56\%$$

**b)** If price increment = x% and expense increase y%

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage reduction in consumption} &= \frac{x - y}{100 + x} \times 100\% \\ &= \frac{40 - 8}{100 + 40} \times 100\% = 22.85\% \text{ (Approx)} \end{aligned}$$

**c)** If price increment = x% and expense decrease (-y%)

Percentage reduction in consumption

$$\begin{aligned} &= \frac{x - (-y)}{100 + x} \times 100\% \\ &= \frac{40 - (-20)}{100 + 40} \times 100\% = \frac{60}{140} \times 100\% \\ &= 42.85\% \text{ (Approx)} \end{aligned}$$

readingSections.title: Example 33
readingSections.content:
Fresh fruit that is composed of 52% water, and you want to convert it into dry fruit, which contains only 22% water. If you have 65 kg of fresh fruit. How much dry fruit can you get from this?

### Solution

Let's denote the weight of the dry fruit obtained as 'x' kg.

The weight of the actual fruit in the fresh fruit is (100 - 52)% of 65 kg, which equals 48% of 65 kg.

Similarly, the weight of the actual fruit in the dry fruit is (100 - 22)% of 'x', which equals 78% of 'x'.

We can equate these two quantities:

$$48\% \text{ of } 65 \text{ kg} = 78\% \text{ of 'x'}$$

$$\text{'x'} = 40 \text{ kg}$$

readingSections.title: Example 34
readingSections.content:
The price of rice has been reduced by 25%. How many kilograms of rice can now be bought with the money that was previously sufficient to buy 30 kg of rice?

### Solution

If the price is reduced by 25%, then 30 kg can be bought for 75% of the original price. So, the total amount of rice that can now be purchased is calculated as follows:

So now in total amount rice can be purchased

$$= \frac{30}{75\%} \times 100\% = 40 \text{ kg}$$
