readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
Interest:

Simple interest is a concept in finance that describes the calculation of interest on a principal amount, where the interest is computed solely on the original sum of money that was deposited or borrowed. The formula used for this calculation is

$$I = \frac{PRT}{100}$$

Amount:

The amount is the final figure you get after adding the interest to the principal.

$$A = P + I$$

$$A = P \left[ 1 + \frac{RT}{100} \right]$$

Where:

- I stand for Simple Interest
- P represents the Principal amount (the initial sum of money)
- R denotes the Rate of interest yearly
- T signifies the Period for which the money is lent or invested
- A stands for amount

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Amount earned Rs. 960 as interest from a simple interest scheme with an annual rate of 12% over 4 years. Find the principal that was invested.

### Solution

The formula for calculating simple interest is given by

$$I = \frac{PRT}{100}, \text{ where:}$$

- I represents the interest = Rs. 960

- R is the annual interest rate = 12%
- T is the period in years = 4 years

Now rearrange this formula to find the principal (P):

$$P = \frac{100I}{RT} = \frac{100 \times 960}{12 \times 4} = \text{Rs } 2000$$

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
If you receive an interest of Rs. 900 after 2 years at a simple interest rate of 10% per annum, what is the total amount you will receive?

### Solution

$$I = \frac{PRT}{100}$$

Rearranging for P gives us:

$$P = \frac{100I}{RT} = \frac{100 \times 900}{10 \times 2} = \text{Rs. } 4500$$

So, the total amount you will receive (principal + interest) = 4500 + 900 = Rs. 5400

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content:
If the rate of interest is not yearly but given n times in a year, then the value of T will be n times the given year.

Case 1: If the rate of interest is half-yearly, then it will be received 2 times in a year, so the time will be 2 times the given year. For example, if given R = 12% half-yearly and time = 2 years, then it will be used in the formula R = 12% and time 2 × 2 = 4.

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
Ram invested Rs 90000 in a fixed deposit for 3 years. The bank offers an interest rate of 7% semi-annually. What is the total interest that Ram will earn at the end of 3 years?

### Solution

Principal, P = Rs 90000, Rate of interest, R = 7%, Time period, T = 3 × 2 = 6 (as it's compounded semi-annually)

$$I = \frac{PRT}{100} = \frac{90000 \times 7 \times 6}{100} = \text{Rs. } 37800$$

Case 2: If the rate of interest is quarterly, then it will be received 4 times in a year, so the time will be 4 times the given year. For example, if given R = 12% quarterly and time = 2 years, then it will be used in the formula R = 12% and Time = 2 × 4 = 8.

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Raman invested Rs 60000 for 2 years in a bank that offers a 5% interest rate quarterly. What is the interest he will receive at the end of the term?

### Solution

Principal, P = Rs 60000, Interest rate per period, r = 5%, Number of periods, t = 2 × 4 = 8 (since it's compounded quarterly, we have four periods per year)

$$I = \frac{PRT}{100} = \frac{60000 \times 5 \times 8}{100} = \text{Rs. } 24000$$

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If the value of R is given in months, then the formula for interest will be

$$I = \frac{PRT}{12 \times 100}$$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Ramesh put Rs 81000 into a savings account that offers a monthly interest rate of 3.5% for 5 years. What will be the interest accrued at the end of this period?

### Solution

Principal amount (P) = Rs 81000, Monthly interest rate (R) = 3.5%, Time period in years (T) = 5 years

$$I = \frac{PRT}{12 \times 100} = \frac{81000 \times 3.5 \times 5}{12 \times 100} = \text{Rs } 1181.25$$

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
If the value of R is given in days, then the formula for interest will be

$$I = \frac{PRT}{365 \times 100}$$

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Priya invested Rs 50000 for 73 days in a bank that offers an annual interest rate of 4%. What is the interest she will receive at the end of this term?

### Solution

Principal (P) = Rs 50000, Rate of interest (R) = 4% per annum, Time (T) = 73 days

$$I = \frac{PRT}{365 \times 100} = \frac{50000 \times 4 \times 73}{365 \times 100} = \text{Rs } 400$$

So, Priya will receive an interest of Rs 400 at the end of her term.

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content: We can also solve the question using the percentage method. For that, assuming that P is 100%, we can express the interest percent as I% = (RT) %, and the amount as (100+I) % or (100+RT) %.

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
If the interest received at 10% per annum simple interest after 2 years is Rs. 500, what was the principal (in Rs)?

### Solution

We know that the interest percent can be expressed as I% = (RT) % = (10 × 2) % = 20%

This means Rs. 500 received as interest is 20% of the principal amount.

So, if 20% corresponds to Rs. 500, we can find the principal (P), which is 100%, using the unitary method:

$$P = \frac{500}{20} \times 100 = \text{Rs } 2500$$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Ramesh invests an unknown sum of money in a scheme that offers varying interest rates over time. The interest rate is 5% per annum for the first 2 years, 7% per annum for the subsequent 4 years, and 10% per annum for any years beyond the sixth year. After a total of 9 years, Ramesh receives Rs. 61,200 as interest. Find out how much money Ramesh initially invested.

### Solution

We can start by understanding that the principal amount, P, is considered as 100%.

For the first 2 years, an interest of 2×5% = 10%

For the next 4 years, an interest of 4×7% = 28%

For the final 3 years (since the total duration is 9 years), an interest of 3×10% = 30%

Total payable interest of 10% + 28% + 30% = 68%.

Given that the total interest received = Rs. 61,200 (which corresponds to the total payable interest of 68%).

$$P = \frac{61200 \times 100}{68} = \text{Rs } 90,000$$

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Rahul invests a sum of money in a scheme that offers 5% interest per annum, with an increase of 1% per annum each year. If at the end of 3 years, he receives Rs. 12,960 as interest, what is the amount of money invested by Rahul?

116

### Solution

Let's assume the invested amount is 100%.

The scheme offers an interest rate of 5% per annum, which increases by 1% each year. So, the interest rates for the three years would be 5%, 6%, and 7%, respectively.

Therefore, the total interest = 5% + 6% + 7% = 18%.

So, the amount invested = $\frac{12960}{18} \times 100 = R_s$ 72,000

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
Ankit borrows a sum of money at the rate of 4% p.a. for the first 3 years, 8% p.a. for the next 2 years, and 10% p.a. beyond 5 years. At the end of 8 years, he pays a total amount of Rs. 18960. Find the amount of loan taken by Ankit.

### Solution

The invested money, P, is 100%.

The interest for the first 3 years at 4% per annum is given by $3 \times 4\% = 12\%$.

The interest for the next 2 years at 8% per annum is $2 \times 8\% = 16\%$.

The interest for the last 3 years at 10% per annum is $3 \times 10\% = 30\%$.

So, the total payable interest = 12% + 16% + 30% = 58%.

Amount = 100% + 58% = 158%

Therefore, $P = \frac{18960}{158} \times 100 = R_s$ 12,000

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content: If the rate of interest is increased by r%, then for t years the increased interest will be rt% of the principle.

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
A sum of Rs. 3,000 amounts to Rs. 4,200 in 5 years at a certain rate of simple interest. If the rate of interest is increased by 2%, how much the same sum amounts in the same time.

### Solution

The sum will be increased by 2% for 5 years, so it will be $5 \times 2\% = 10\%$.

Therefore, the increased amount is 10% of Rs. 3,000 = Rs. 300.

So, the new amount is Rs. 4,200 + Rs. 300 = Rs. 4,500.

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content:
If the interest from different principals a, b, c, ... is equal and the rate of interest are $r_1, r_2, r_3, \dots$, and the time periods are $t_1, t_2, t_3, \dots$, then:

$$a \times (r_1 \times t_1)\% = b \times (r_2 \times t_2)\% = c \times (r_3 \times t_3)\% = \dots$$

OR

$$a : b : c : \dots = \frac{1}{r_1 \times t_1} : \frac{1}{r_2 \times t_2} : \frac{1}{r_3 \times t_3} \dots$$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
A woman invests a sum of money in three different schemes that offer 5% p.a., 8% p.a., and 12% p.a. for 8 years, 10 years, and 5 years respectively. She divides her investment into three different parts such that in each scheme, she receives an equal amount of interest. If the smallest part of her investment is Rs 5400, what is the total amount she invested?

### Solution

According to the problem,

$$a \times r_1 \times t_1 = b \times r_2 \times t_2 = c \times r_3 \times t_3$$

Given that, $r_1 = 5\%$, $r_2 = 8\%$, $r_3 = 12\%$, $t_1 = 8$ years, $t_2 = 10$ years, $t_3 = 5$ years.

$$a \times 5\% \times 8 = b \times 8\% \times 10 = c \times 12\% \times 5$$

From this, we get:

$$2a = 4b = 3c$$

So, the ratio of a : b : c = 6 : 3 : 4

The total investment is represented by $6 + 3 + 4 = 13$ units, where the smallest amount is 3 units.

Therefore, the total amount invested

$$= \frac{5400 \times 13}{3} = R_s \text{ 23400}$$

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
If Ramu has Rs 520,000 and invests it in 3 companies, the amounts in company X, company Y, and company Z for 4 years, 5 years, and 10 years respectively, at 8%, 12%, and 16% rates of interest respectively, and earns an equal interest from all parts, then find the amount that is invested at 8%.

### Solution

$P = R_s$ 520,000, $r_1 = 8\%$, $r_2 = 12\%$, $r_3 = 16\%$, $t_1 = 4$ years, $t_2 = 5$ years, and $t_3 = 10$ years.

$$a : b : c : \dots = \frac{1}{r_1 \times t_1} : \frac{1}{r_2 \times t_2} : \frac{1}{r_3 \times t_3} \dots$$

$$a : b : c = \frac{1}{8 \times 4} : \frac{1}{12 \times 5} : \frac{1}{16 \times 10}$$

$$a : b : c = 15 : 8 : 3$$

Now, the amount that is invested at 8%

$$= \frac{520000}{(15 + 8 + 3)} \times 15 = R_s \text{ 300000}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 7
readingSections.content:
If the amount from different principals a, b, c, ... is equal and the rates of interest are $r_1, r_2, r_3, \dots$, and the time periods are $t_1, t_2, t_3, \dots$, then:

$$a \times (100 + r_1 \times t_1)\% = b \times (100 + r_2 \times t_2)\% = c \times (100 + r_3 \times t_3)\% = \dots$$

OR

$$a : b : c : \dots = \frac{1}{(100 + r_1 \times t_1)} : \frac{1}{(100 + r_2 \times t_2)} : \frac{1}{(100 + r_3 \times t_3)} \dots$$

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
A woman invests a certain amount of money in three different schemes for 3 years, 5 years, and 7 years. The schemes offer an interest rate of 6%. The interest is paid in such a way that at the end of each scheme, she receives an equal amount of money. What is the ratio between her investments in these schemes?

### Solution

Let's denote the three parts of the investment as a, b, and c. According to the question, we have:

$$a \times (100 + r_1 \times t_1)\% = b \times (100 + r_2 \times t_2)\% = c \times (100 + r_3 \times t_3)\%$$

Given that $r_1 = r_2 = r_3 = 6\%$, $t_1 = 3$ years, $t_2 = 5$ years, and $t_3 = 7$ years,

$$a \times (100 + 6\% \times 3) = b \times (100 + 6\% \times 5) = c \times (100 + 6\% \times 7)$$

118% of a = 130% of b = 142% of c

So, the ratio of a : b : c = 4615 : 4189 : 3835

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
Amit has Rs 103,050 and invests it in 3 companies, the amounts in company X, company Y, and company Z for 1 years, 2 years, and 5 years respectively, at 25%, 20%, and 10% rates of interest respectively, and earns an equal amount from all parts, then find the amount that is invested at 10%.

### Solution

P = Rs 103,050, $r_1 = 25\%$, $r_2 = 20\%$, $r_3 = 10\%$, $t_1 = 1$ years, $t_2 = 2$ years, and $t_3 = 5$ years.

Let the parts are a, b, c then

$$a : b : c = \frac{1}{(100 + 25 \times 1)} : \frac{1}{(100 + 20 \times 2)} : \frac{1}{(100 + 10 \times 5)}$$

a : b : c = 84 : 75 : 70

Now, the amount that is invested at 10%

$$= \frac{103050}{(84 + 75 + 70)} \times 70 = \text{Rs } 31500$$

readingSections.title: Concept 8
readingSections.content:
If an amount P is divided into the fraction of $\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}$,

...and the rate of interest is $r_1, r_2, r_3, \dots$ and received total I interest for $t_1, t_2, t_3, \dots$, then

$$P = \frac{100I}{\left( \frac{r_1 \times t_1}{a} + \frac{r_2 \times t_2}{b} + \frac{r_3 \times t_3}{c} + \dots \right)}$$

readingSections.title: Example 16
readingSections.content:
Raj invests one fourth of his capital in the State Bank of India, one third of his capital in the Bank of Baroda, and the remaining amount in the Central Bank of India at yearly interest rates of 5%, 8%, and 10% for 5 years, 3 years, and 4 years respectively. He receives a total interest amount of Rs 37100. Find his total capital.

### Solution

Given the data, the total interest I is Rs 37100, the interest rates $r_1, r_2$, and $r_3$ are 5%, 8%, and 10% respectively, and the time periods $t_1, t_2$, and $t_3$ are 5 years, 3 years, and 4 years

respectively and $\frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{c} = 1 - \left( \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} \right) = 1 -$

$$\left( \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3} \right) = \frac{5}{12}$$

$$\text{Now, } P = \frac{100I}{\left( \frac{r_1 \times t_1}{a} + \frac{r_2 \times t_2}{b} + \frac{r_3 \times t_3}{c} \right)}$$

$$= \frac{100 \times 37100}{\left( \frac{5 \times 5}{4} + \frac{8 \times 3}{3} + \frac{10 \times 4}{\frac{12}{5}} \right)} = \text{Rs } 120000$$

readingSections.title: Concept 9
readingSections.content:
If person B borrows an amount P from A at an interest rate of x% and lends it to C at an interest rate of y%, while also adding an amount Q, then the profit of B in this process will be for $t_1$ time

$$(y-x) \times t_1\% \text{ of } P + y \times t_1\% \text{ of } Q$$

If the person did not add any amount then Q = 0 then Profit will be

$$(y-x) \times t_1\% \text{ of } P$$

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
A person borrows Rs 10,000 for 3 years at 5% per annum simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at 7.5% per annum simple interest for 3 years after adding Rs 5000. What is his gain in the transaction?

### Solution

### Method 1

$$\text{Interest paid} = \frac{(\text{Principle} \times \text{Rate} \times \text{Time})}{100}$$

$$= \frac{10000 \times 5 \times 3}{100} = \text{Rs } 1,500$$

Interest the person earns by lending Rs 15,000 (Rs 10,000 + Rs 5,000) at 7.5% per annum for 3 years is calculated as follows:

118

$$\text{Interest earned} = \frac{(\text{Principle} \times \text{Rate} \times \text{Time})}{100}$$

$$= \frac{15000 \times 7.5 \times 3}{100} = \text{Rs } 3,375$$

Gain = Interest Earned - Interest Paid = Rs (3,375 - 1,500) = Rs 1,875

### Method 2

The profit of person B in this process can be calculated using the formula you provided:

$$(y - x) \times t_1\% \text{ of } P + y \times t_1\% \text{ of } Q$$

- P (the amount borrowed) = Rs 10,000
- x (the interest rate of A) = 5%
- y (the interest rate of C) = 7.5%
- t₁ (the time period) = 3 years
- Q (the additional amount) = Rs 5,000

we get:  $(7.5 - 5) \times 3\%$  of Rs 10,000 + 7.5  $\times 3\%$  of Rs 5,000 = 2.5  $\times 3\%$  of Rs 10,000 + 22.5% of Rs 5,000 = Rs (750 + 1,125) = Rs 1,875

So, the gain in the transaction for the person who borrowed the money is Rs 1,875.

readingSections.title: Concept 10
readingSections.content: **If an amount becomes n times in any time then principle will be 1 unit and interest will be (n-1) unit so the ratio of principle and interest will be 1 : (n-1)**

readingSections.title: Example 18
readingSections.content:
In a small town, a local farmer invested some money in a new agricultural technology. The investment was so successful that it became 4 times the original amount in just a few years. If the rate of interest was 8% per annum, can you calculate how many years it took for the farmer's investment to grow to this extent?

### Solution

Because the amount becomes 4 times so interest will be (4 - 1 = 3) units and the principle will be 1 unit

$$\text{So, Interest} = \frac{PRT}{100}$$

$$\text{Time} = \frac{100 \times I}{P \times R} = \frac{100 \times 3}{1 \times 8} = 37.5 \text{ years}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 11
readingSections.content:
**If an amount becomes n₁ times in t₁ years due to simple interest, and becomes n₂ times in t₂ years, then the relation between them is given by the equation**

$$\frac{t_1}{t_2} = \frac{n_1 - 1}{n_2 - 1}$$

readingSections.title: Example 19
readingSections.content:
Entrepreneur who decides to invest some money in a bank. If the money becomes 7 times of its original amount in 36 years due to simple interest, how many years it will take for the money to become 3 times its original amount?

### Solution

n₁ = 7 (the money becomes 7 times its original amount),

t₁ = 36 years, n₂ = 3 (we want to find out when the money becomes 3 times its original amount) We need to find t₂. The formula is:

$$\frac{t_1}{t_2} = \frac{n_1 - 1}{n_2 - 1}$$

$$\frac{36}{t_2} = \frac{7 - 1}{3 - 1}$$

t₂ = 12 years.

readingSections.title: Concept 12
readingSections.content:
**If an amount becomes n₁ times by r₁ rate of interest and n₂ times by r₂ rate of interest then the relation between them is given by the equation.**

$$\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{n_1 - 1}{n_2 - 1}$$

readingSections.title: Example 20
readingSections.content:
If an amount becomes 5 times by 8% rate of interest then by 10% rate of interest how many times it will be in same time.

### Solution

n₁ = 5 (the money becomes 5 times its original amount), r₁ = 8%, r₂ = 10%

We need to find n₂. The formula is:

$$\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{n_1 - 1}{n_2 - 1}$$

$$\frac{8\%}{10\%} = \frac{5 - 1}{n_2 - 1}$$

n₂ = 6 times

readingSections.title: Example 21
readingSections.content:
A girl aged 10 years inherits Rs. 200,000 from her grandmother's will. The money is placed in a trust that invests the funds at an interest rate of 5% per annum. The young girl receives Rs. 4000 as an allowance at the end of each year. The trust's expenses amount to Rs. 1000 per annum. Determine the amount that will be given to the girl when she reaches the age of 16 years.

### Solution

The girl is 10 years old and she will receive the money when she is 16 years old. So, the money will be invested for 16 - 10 = 6 years

The girl receives Rs. 4000 as an allowance at the end of each year. So, the total allowance for 6 years is $4000 \times 6 = \text{Rs. } 24,000$

The trust's expenses amount to Rs. 1000 per annum. So, the total expenses for 6 years are $1000 \times 6 = \text{Rs. } 6,000$

The total amount that will be deducted from the initial amount is the sum of the allowance and the expenses, which is Rs. $24,000 + \text{Rs. } 6,000 = \text{Rs. } 30,000$

The trust invests the funds at an interest rate of $5\%$ per annum. The total interest earned over 6 years

$$
= \frac{200000 \times 5 \times 6}{100} = \text{Rs. } 60,000
$$

Therefore, the amount that will be given to the girl when she reaches the age of 16 years is the initial amount plus the total interest earned minus the total deductions: Rs. $200,000 + \text{Rs. } 60,000 - \text{Rs. } 30,000 = \text{Rs. } 230,000$

So, when she turns 16 years old, she will receive Rs.230,000.

readingSections.title: Concept 13
readingSections.content:
If an amount $\mathbf{P}$ becomes $\mathbf{A}_1$ in $\mathbf{T}_1$ year and becomes $\mathbf{A}_2$ in $\mathbf{T}_2$ year then

$$
\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{P} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{T}_1} \\
\mathrm{R} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_1 - \mathrm{A}_2}{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{T}_1} \times 100\%
\end{array}
$$

readingSections.title: Example 22
readingSections.content:
Rahul deposited some amount in Bank of Baroda which becomes Rs 2500 in 5 years and Rs 3100 in 8 years then find the amount deposited and the rate of interest that is given by the bank.

### Solution

Give that $\mathrm{A}_1 = \text{Rs } 2500, \mathrm{A}_2 = 3100, \mathrm{T}_1 = 5$ year, $\mathrm{T}_2 = 8$ year

Amounted deposited by Rahul $= \frac{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{T}_1}$

$$
= \frac{2500 \times 8 - 3100 \times 5}{8 - 5} = \text{Rs. } 1500
$$

Rate of Interest $= \frac{\mathrm{A}_1 - \mathrm{A}_2}{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{T}_1} \times 100\%$

$$
= \frac{2500 - 3100}{2500 \times 8 - 3100 \times 5} \times 100\% = 13.33\%
$$

readingSections.title: Concept 14
readingSections.content:
If a certain sum $\mathbf{P}$ amounts to $\mathbf{A}_1$ by $\mathbf{R}_1\%$ rate of interest and becomes $\mathbf{A}_2$ by $\mathbf{R}_2\%$ rate of interest in $\mathbf{T}$ time then

$$
\mathrm{P} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{R}_1 - \mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1 - \mathrm{R}_2}
$$

$$
\mathrm{T} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_2 - \mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{R}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{R}_1} \times 100
$$

readingSections.title: Example 23
readingSections.content:
If a certain sum becomes Rs 1000 at a $6\%$ rate of interest and becomes Rs 1200 at an $8\%$ rate of interest, then find the principal and time.

### Solution

Given that a certain sum becomes Rs 1000 at a $6\%$ rate of interest ($\mathrm{A}_1 = \text{Rs. } 1000, \mathrm{R}_1 = 6\%$) and becomes Rs 1200 at an $8\%$ rate of interest ($\mathrm{A}_2 = \text{Rs. } 1200, \mathrm{R}_2 = 8\%$)

Principle $\mathrm{P} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{R}_1 - \mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1 - \mathrm{R}_2}$

$$
\mathrm{P} = \frac{1200 \times 6 - 1000 \times 8}{6 - 8} = \text{Rs. } 400
$$

Time $\mathrm{T} = \frac{\mathrm{A}_2 - \mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{R}_2 - \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{R}_1} \times 100$

$$
= \frac{1200 - 1000}{1000 \times 8 - 1200 \times 6} \times 100 = 25 \text{ year}
$$

readingSections.title: Installment Based in Simple Interest
readingSections.content:
$$
\text{Installment} = \frac{100A}{100T + RT \times \frac{(T - 1)}{2}}
$$

A: Loan amount, T: time in year, R: Rate of interest yearly

readingSections.title: Example 24
readingSections.content:
What annual installment will discharge a debt of Rs 990 due in 3 years at an interest rate of $10\%$ per year?

### Solution

$$
\text{Installment} = \frac{100A}{100T + RT \times \frac{(T - 1)}{2}}
$$

$\mathrm{A} = \text{Rs } 990, \mathrm{T} = 3$ years, $\mathrm{R} = 10\%$

$$
\text{Installment} = \frac{100 \times 990}{100 \times 3 + 10 \times 3 \times \frac{(3 - 1)}{2}}
$$

$$
= \text{Rs } 300
$$

Compound interest is a method of computing interest
where the interest is added to the principal sum after each
compounding period. The interest for the subsequent
period is then calculated on this new, larger principal,
resulting in exponential growth in the total sum over time.

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
Compound interest is a method of computing interest where the interest is added to the principal sum after each compounding period. The interest for the subsequent period is then calculated on this new, larger principal, resulting in exponential growth in the total sum over time.

$$A = P \left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{n}$$

$$I = A - P$$

In this equation:

- A represents the total amount of money accumulated after n compounding periods, including interest.
- P refers to the principal sum, which is the initial amount of money deposited or loaned.
- R represents the interest rate for each compounding period, expressed as a percentage.
- n indicates the total number of compounding periods
- t represents that how many times interest is credited per year
- I indicate compound interest

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
John invested Rs 1000 in a bank that offers a 12% annual interest rate, compounded annually. How much interest will he earn after 5 years?

### Solution

From the above chart for 5 years and a 12% interest rate, the amount will be 1.76 times the principal, because the principal is 1 times itself.

So, Compound interest = Principal × (n-1) = 1000 × (1.76-1) = Rs 760 (Approximately).

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
Sarah invests Rs 5000 in a savings account that offers a 3% annual interest rate, compounded annually. How much will her investment be worth after 10 years?

### Solution

From the above chart for 10 years and a 3% interest rate, the amount will be 1.34 times the principal.

So, Amount = Principal × n = 5000 × 1.34 = Rs 6700 (Approximately).

readingSections.content:
We know that in compound interest, interest is earned on total previous amount that will be principle as well as interest for example if principle is Rs 1000 and rate of interest is 10% then

First year interest $= 10\%$ of $1000 = 100$

Second year interest $= 10\%$ of $(1000 + 100) = 100 + 10$

Third year interest $= 10\%$ of $(1000 + 100 + 100 + 10)$

= 100 + 10 + 10 + 1

readingSections.title: Ratio Method
readingSections.content:
Case 1: We can also solve compound interest questions using ratios. If the fractional value of the rate of interest for different years is $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \frac{a_3}{b_3}, \ldots$ then the ratio of principle to amount will be

$$
\frac {\mathrm {P}}{\mathrm {A}} = \frac {\mathrm {b} _ {1} \times \mathrm {b} _ {2} \times \mathrm {b} _ {3} \times \dots}{(\mathrm {a} _ {1} + \mathrm {b} _ {1}) \times (\mathrm {a} _ {2} + \mathrm {b} _ {2}) \times (\mathrm {a} _ {3} + \mathrm {b} _ {3}) \times \dots}
$$

Case 2: If the rate of interest is equal in all cases and the fractional value for $n$ times is $a / b$ , then the ratio of principle to amount will be

$$
\frac {P}{A} = \frac {b ^ {n}}{(a + b) ^ {n}}
$$

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Calculate the compound interest on an amount of Rs 80,000 for 3 years if the rate of interest is $5\%$ annually.

### Solution

Method 1: Let's denote the principal amount as $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{Rs}$ 80,000, the number of years as $n = 3$ , and the rate of interest per year as $\mathrm{R} = 5\%$ . We'll assume $t = 1$ because the interest is credited annually.

The formula for compound interest is

$$
A = P \left(1 + \frac {R}{1 0 0}\right) ^ {n t} = 8 0 0 0 0 \times \left(1 + \frac {5}{1 0 0}\right) ^ {3 + 1} = R s 9 2, 6 1 0
$$

The interest I is calculated as $\mathrm{I} = \mathrm{A} - \mathrm{P}$ .

Substituting the values we have, $\mathrm{I} = \mathrm{Rs} 92,610 - \mathrm{Rs} 80,000 = \mathrm{Rs} 12,610$ .

So, the compound interest is Rs 12,610

Method 2: The rate of interest is $5\%$ , which is $1/20$ .

Since the interest is compounded yearly, $n = 3$

$$
\frac {\text {P r i n c i p l e}}{\text {A m o u n t}} = \frac {2 0 ^ {3}}{(1 + 2 0) ^ {3}} = \frac {2 0 ^ {3}}{2 1 ^ {3}} = \frac {8 0 0 0}{9 2 6 1}
$$

Interest $= 9261 - 8000 = 1261$ unit

So, interest $= \frac{80000}{8000} \times 1261 = Rs12610$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Rajesh deposited Rs 50,000 in a bank that offers an annual interest rate of $6\%$ compounded semi-annually. What total amount will be in his account after 2 years?

### Solution

Method 1: Let's denote the principal amount as $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{Rs}$ 50,000,

the interest rate as $r = 6\%$ per annum,

the number of times interest is compounded per year as $n = 2$ (since it's compounded semi-annually),

and the time the money is invested for as $t = 2$ years.

$$
A = P \left(1 + \frac {R}{1 0 0}\right) ^ {n t} = 5 0 0 0 0 \times \left(1 + \frac {6}{2 \times 1 0 0}\right) ^ {2 + 2} = R s 5 6 2 7 5. 4 4
$$

So, the total amount in Rajesh's account after 2 years will be Rs 56,275.44.

124

Method 2: Since the interest is compounded semi-annually, n = 2×2 = 4.

The rate of interest is 6%, but for semi-annually it will be 6/2 = 3% = 3/100. The ratio of Principle to Amount is 100⁴ : (3+100)⁴ = 100⁴ : 103⁴

Therefore, the Amount

$$= \frac{50000}{100^4} \times 103^4 = \text{Rs}56,275.44$$

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If the amount for years n₁ and n₂ is given, where n₁ is the starting year and n₂ is the ending year, then we will use n = n₂ - n₁ in the formula for the amount. The starting amount will be considered the principal and the new amount will be the total amount. The formula is:

$$A = P \left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{(n_2 - n_1)t}$$

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
If an amount increases to Rs 51,200 at the end of 7 years and further increases to Rs 72,900 at the end of 9 years, what is the annual rate of interest if the amount is compounded every 8 months?

### Solution

Method 1: Let's denote the initial amount as P = Rs 51,200 and the final amount as A = Rs 72,900. The time period for compounding is t = 12/8 = 1.5. The difference in the number of years is n₂ - n₁ = 9 - 7 = 2 years.

$$A = P \left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{(n_2 - n_1)t}$$

$$72900 = 51200 \left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{2 \times 1.5}$$

$$R = 12.5\%$$

12.5% interest in 8 months so annually rate of interest

$$= \frac{12.5 \times 12}{8} = 18.75\%$$

Method 2: Let's assume the fraction value of the rate of interest is 1/r for 8 months. Because it is compounded after 8 months, from 7 years to 9 years, it will be calculated 3 times

$$\left( \frac{2 \times 12}{8} = 3 \right), \text{ so } n = 3$$

Now,

$$\frac{P}{A} = \frac{r^3}{(1+r)^3}$$

$$\frac{51200}{72900} = \frac{r^3}{(1+r)^3}$$

$$\frac{8}{9} = \frac{r}{1+r}$$

Therefore, $$\frac{8}{9} = \frac{r}{1+r}$$, Which implies that r=8.

So, $$R = \frac{1}{r} = \frac{1}{8}$$ (For 8 months).

But for 1 year, it will be $$R = \frac{\frac{1}{8} \times 12}{8} \times 100\% = 18.75\%$$

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
If the rate of interest change per time then the formula of amount will be

$$A = P \left( 1 + \frac{R_1}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{R_2}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{R_3}{100} \right) \times \dots$$

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
You have inherited a sum of Rs. 20,000 from a distant relative. You decide to invest this money in a savings account that offers a varying rate of interest: 3% per annum for the first year, 4% per annum for the second year, and 5% per annum for the third year. What would be the compound interest accrued on your inheritance after 3 years? Remember, compound interest is calculated annually.

### Solution

### Method 1

$$A = P \left( 1 + \frac{R_1}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{R_2}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{R_3}{100} \right) \times \dots$$

A is the amount after 3 years is the principal amount (Rs. 20,000), R₁ is the rate of interest for the first year (3%), R₂ is the rate of interest for the second year (4%), R₃ is the rate of interest for the third year (5%)

Substituting the values, we get:

$$A = 20000 \left( 1 + \frac{3}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{4}{100} \right) \times \left( 1 + \frac{5}{100} \right)$$

$$= \text{Rs. } 22,495.2$$

So, the compound interest = Rs. 22,495.2 - Rs. 20,000 = Rs. 2,495.2.

Method 2: Because the rate of interest per year is different, we use the fraction value where 3% = 3/100, 4% = 1/25, and 5% = 1/20.

The principle amount is calculated as follows:

125

Amount = 100 × 25 × 20 : (100+3) × (1+25) × (1+20) = 100 × 25 × 20 : 103 × 26 × 21.

$$\text{Amount} = 20000 \times \frac{103 \times 26 \times 21}{100 \times 25 \times 20} = \text{Rs. } 22,495.28$$

So, the compound interest after 3 years would be Rs. 22,495.2 - Rs. 20,000 = **Rs. 2,495.2**

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content:
If in $t_1$ time an amount becomes $n_1$ times of principle and in $t_2$ time it becomes $n_2$ times then the relation of $t_1 t_2$, $n_1$ and $n_2$ will be

$$n_2 = n_1^{\left(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\right)}$$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
In the bustling city of Bhopal, there's a famous sweet shop owned by Mr. Sharma. He decided to invest some of his savings in a scheme that offered compound interest. He noticed that his investment doubled in 12 years. Find in how many years his investment would quadruple?

### Solution

Given that Mr. Sharma's investment doubles ($n_1 = 2$) in 12 years ($t_1 = 12$), he wants to find out how long it will take for his investment to quadruple ($n_2 = 4$).

We can use the formula: $n_2 = n_1^{\left(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\right)}$

$$4 = 2^{\left(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\right)}$$

By comparing,

we get $\frac{t_2}{t_1} = 2$ Therefore, $t_2 = t_1 \times 2 = 12 \times 2 = 24$ years.

So, it will take 24 years for Mr. Sharma's investment to quadruple.

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
A certain amount of money becomes 16 times its original value in 64 years due to compound interest. How many years will it take for it to become 4 times its original value?

### Solution

An amount becomes 16 times its original value in 64 years.

So, $n_1 = 16$, $t_1 = 64$ and we want to find out when it will be $n_2 = 4$ times its original value. So, we have

$$n_2 = n_1^{\left(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\right)}$$

$$4 = 16^{\frac{t_2}{64}}$$

$$4^1 = 4^{2\left(\frac{t_2}{64}\right)}$$

$$1 = 2^{\left(\frac{t_2}{64}\right)}$$

Solving for $t_2$, we get $t_2 = \frac{64}{2} = 32$ years.

So, the amount will become 4 times its original value in 32 years.

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content: If an amount is initially A and it becomes B in time t, then in the next time period t, B will be multiplied by B/A

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A sum of money becomes amount to Rs.33000 at the end of 3 years and Rs 39600 at the end of 6 years. If interest is compounded annually. Then find the amount at the end of 9 years?

### Solution

Given that a sum of money becomes Rs. 33000 at the end of 3 years and Rs. 39600 at the end of 6 years, we can see that the amount is compounded annually.

$$\text{Amount after 9 years} = \text{Rs. } 39600 \times \frac{\text{Rs. } 39600}{\text{Rs. } 33000} = \text{Rs. } 47520$$

If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest for a period of 2 years is Rs. 800 and the rate of interest is 10% per annum, what is the principal amount?

### Solution

P = 80000

readingSections.title: BOX METHOD
readingSections.content:
In this method, if the principal is given and the fraction value of the rate is 1/r, then for the first box, multiply the principal by 1/r. For the second box, multiply the value of the first box by 1/r. After the second box, we should multiply the value of the previous box by 1/r and add the value of the previous box as well. The time will be multiplied in decreasing order by 1 from the start.

For example, if the principal is 1024 and the rate of interest is 50% (which equals 1/2), and we want to calculate it for 4 years, then we will continuously multiply 1024 by ½ for the first two boxes. After that, we will also add the value of the previous box.

$$4 \times (512) + 3 \times (256) + 2 \times (384) + 1 \times (576)$$

If for n years, the box is:

$$n \times (a) + (n-1) \times (b) + (n-2) \times (c) + (n-3) \times (d) + \dots \dots \dots$$

Then:

The first box will show Simple Interest \(= \mathrm{n}\times (\mathrm{a})\)
The total of all boxes will show Compound Interest \(= \mathrm{n}\) \(\times (\mathrm{a}) + (\mathrm{n - 1})\times (\mathrm{b}) + (\mathrm{n - 2})\times (\mathrm{c}) + (\mathrm{n - 3})\times (\mathrm{d}) + \dots\)
Leaving out the first box for difference between Simple and Compound Interest \(= (\mathrm{n - 1})\times (\mathrm{b}) + (\mathrm{n - 2})\times (\mathrm{c}) + (\mathrm{n - 3})\) \(\times (\mathrm{d}) + \dots\)

- Leaving out the first box and constant value of n for all boxes will give difference between Simple and Compound Interest for nth year = b + c + d + ...

### Solution

16.66% = 1/6 , n=4, now multiply by 1/6 with Rs 46656 for value of boxes

\(4 \times (7776) + 3 \times (1296) + 2 \times (1512) + 1 \times (1764)\)
1) Simple Interest for 4 year \(= 4\times (7776) = \mathbf{Rs}31104\)
2) Compound interest for 4 year \(= 4\times (7776) + 3\times\) (1296) \(+2\times (1512) + 1\times (1764) = \mathbf{Rs}39780\)
3) Difference between simple and compound interest for 4 year \(= 3\times (1296) + 2\times (1512) + 1\times (1764)\) \(= \mathbf{Rs}8676\)
4) Difference between simple and compound interest for \(4^{\text{th}} = (1296) + (1512) + (1764) = \mathbf{Rs}4572\)

Given that the simple interest for 2 years is Rs 16000 with a rate of interest of 12% per year,

we can use the ratio of Simple Interest (SI) to Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years, which is SI : CI = 200 : (200 + r).

In this case, the relationship between the loan amount and the installment can be expressed as:

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
A businessman takes a loan of Rs. 120000 at an annual compound interest rate of 15%. If he plans to repay the loan

in three equal annual installments, what would be the amount of each installment?

### Solution

Given that the loan amount X is Rs. 120000, the rate of interest R is 15%, and the loan is to be repaid in three equal annual installments, we can use the formula you provided to calculate the amount of each installment.

First, we calculate $K = \left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right) = \left(1 + \frac{15}{100}\right) = \frac{23}{20}$

$$\frac{X}{a} = \frac{1}{K} + \frac{1}{K^2} + \frac{1}{K^3} + \dots$$

$$\frac{120000}{a} = \frac{20}{23} + \left(\frac{20}{23}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{20}{23}\right)^3$$

$$= \frac{20}{23} + \frac{400}{529} + \frac{8000}{12167}$$

$$\frac{120000}{a} = \frac{27780}{12167}$$

a= Rs 52560 (approx)

examples.label: Example
examples.text: A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 9 days and 15 days respectively. If they work for a day alternately, with A beginning, then the work will be completed in? Solution: Method 1: Let’s assume that the total work is 45 units (LCM of 9 and 15). In one day, A can complete 5 units of work and B can complete 3 units of work. If they work alternately, then in two days, they can complete 8 units of work (5 + 3). Therefore, they can complete 40 units of work in 10 days (5 cycles of 2 days each). On the 11th day, A will work and complete 5 units of work, thus completing the total work. Therefore, the work will be completed in 11 days. Method 2: Let Total Work = 45 unit (LCM of 9 and 15) 1 st day A work = 5 unit, 2 nd day B work = 3 unit, So, in every 2 days work done = 5+3 = 8 unit So, in (2×5)10 days work done = (8×5) 40 unit Remaining work 45 – 40 = 5 unit And now it’s A’s turn A will come and in 1 day he does 5 work. Hence, In (10+1) 11 days total work (40+5) 45 will be completed.

readingSections.title: Work and Person
readingSections.content: The work is directly proportional to number of persons engaged in doing that particular work (more work, more men and conversely less work, less men).

readingSections.title: Time and Person
readingSections.content:
These two terms are inversely proportional to each other (more men, less time and conversely more time, less men).

The work is directly proportional to time. It directly means that if a particular person works on a project or work for more time, then more work will be done by that person. On the contrary, if a particular person works on a project or work for less time, then less work will be done by that person.

readingSections.title: Concept of Efficiency
readingSections.content: Suppose a person can complete a particular work in '4' days, then we can say he does 25% work each day. Thus it is clear that his efficiency is 25% per day.

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content: If a person can do a piece of work in 'n' days (or hours), then the person's 1 day's (hour's) work =  $\frac{1}{n}$

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Anshika completes a work in 59 days. How much work will she accomplish in a single day?

### Solution

According to above concept,

Required work done by Anshika in 1 day =  $\frac{1}{59}$

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content: If a person's 1 day's (hour's) work =  $\frac{1}{n}$ , then person will complete the work in 'n' days (or hours).

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
Komal completes  $\frac{1}{13}$  part of a certain work in 1 day. In how many days, will she complete the whole work?

### Solution

According to above concept,

Required number of days = 13

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
Maneesh can do a work 3 times faster than Vishesh and therefore takes 40 days less than Vishesh. Find the time in which Maneesh and Vishesh can complete the work individually.

### Solution

According to above concept,

(Maneesh : Vishesh)  Efficiency = 3 : 1

Time taken to complete the work by Maneesh : Vishesh = 1 : 3

According to Question,

Time taken by Vishesh – Time taken by Maneesh = 40

3k – k = 40

2k = 40

k = 20

Number of days, required by Maneesh = 20

Number of days, required by Vishesh = 20 × 3 = 60

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content: If ratio of number of men required to complete a work is  $p : q$ , then the ratio of time taken by them will be  $q : p$ .

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
If a task can be completed by 12 men in 20 days, how many days will it take for 15 men to finish the same task?

### Solution

According to above concept,

Ratio of number of men in two groups =  $12 : 15 = 4 : 5$

Ratio of time taken by the two groups =  $5 : 4$

According to question,

$$5 = 20$$

$$4 = 16$$

Required number of days by 15 men = 16

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
(I) If  $P$  can do a piece of work in  $x$  days and  $Q$  can do the same work in  $y$  days, then

$$(P + Q)'s 1 \text{ day's work} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{x+y}{xy}$$

Time taken by  $(P + Q)$  to complete the work =  $\frac{xy}{x+y}$

(II) If  $P$  can do a piece of work in  $x$  days,  $Q$  can do the same work in  $y$  days and  $R$  can do the same work in  $z$  days, then

$$(P + Q + R)'s 1 \text{ day's work} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} = \frac{yz + xz + xy}{xyz}$$

Time taken by  $(P + Q + R)$  to complete the work

$$= \frac{xyz}{yz + xz + xy}$$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Manish can do a piece of work in 10 days and Shubhendra can do the same work in 12 days. What is the duration required for the completion of the task when both collaborate?

### Solution

### Method 1

Manish's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{10}$  and Shubhendra's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{12}$

(Manish + Shubhendra)'s 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{6+5}{60} = \frac{11}{60}$$

(Manish + Shubhendra) complete the whole work in

$$\frac{60}{11} = 5 \frac{5}{11} \text{ days}$$

According to above concept,

Number of days taken to complete the work by Manish and

$$\text{Shubhendra} = \frac{10 \times 12}{10+12} = 5 \frac{5}{11} \text{ days}$$

### Method 2

Let Total Work = 60 unit (LCM of 10 and 12)

![Book diagram, page 130](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p130-img-34.jpeg)

Work done by  $M + S$  in one day =  $6 + 5 = 11$  unit/day

Time taken to complete work

$$= \frac{\text{total work}}{\text{work done in one day}} = \frac{60}{11} = 5 \frac{5}{11} \text{ days.}$$

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Abhishek can do a piece of work in 16 days, Maneesh can do the same work in 32 days and Naimish can do the same work in 48 days. What is the duration required for the completion of the task when they collaborate?

### Solution

### Method 1

Abhishek's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{16}$ , Maneesh's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{32}$  and Naimish's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{48}$

(Abhishek + Maneesh + Naimish)'s 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{32} + \frac{1}{48} = \frac{6+3+2}{96} = \frac{11}{96}$$

(Abhishek + Maneesh + Naimish) complete the whole work in  $\frac{96}{11} = 8 \frac{8}{11}$  days

According to above concept,

Number of days taken to complete the work by Abhishek, Maneesh and Naimish

$$= \frac{16 \times 32 \times 48}{16 \times 32 + 32 \times 48 + 48 \times 16} = 8 \frac{8}{11} \text{ days}$$

### Method 2

Let Total Work = 96 unit (LCM of 16, 32 and 48)

![Book diagram, page 130](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p130-img-35.jpeg)

Work done by A + M + N in one day = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 unit/day
Time taken to complete work

$$= \frac{\text{total work}}{\text{work done in one day}} = \frac{96}{11} = 8\frac{8}{11} \text{ days.}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content: If P + Q can complete a work in x days and P alone can complete that work in y days, then the number of days required to complete the work by Q alone = $\frac{\text{xy}}{\text{y} - \text{x}}$ days

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Radhika and Mansi can complete a piece of work in 12 days and Radhika alone can complete that work in 18 days. In how many days can Mansi alone complete it?

### Solution

### Method 1

(Radhika + Mansi)'s 1 day's work = $\frac{1}{12}$ and Radhika's 1 day's work = $\frac{1}{18}$

Mansi's 1 day's work = (Radhika + Mansi)'s 1 day's work - Radhika's 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3 - 2}{36} = \frac{1}{36}$$

Time taken by Mansi to complete the work alone = 36 days

According to above concept,

Number of days taken to complete the work by Mansi

$$= \frac{12 \times 18}{18 - 12} = 36 \text{ days}$$

### Method 2

Let Total Work = 36 unit (LCM of 12 and 18)

![Book diagram, page 131](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p131-img-36.jpeg)

Efficiency of Mansi = 3 - 2 = 1 unit/day

Number of days to complete work by Mansi Alone

$$= \frac{36}{1} = 36 \text{ days.}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 7
readingSections.content:
If $m_1$ persons can do $w_1$ work in $d_1$ days working $t_1$ hours in a day and $m_2$ persons can do $w_2$ work in $d_2$ days working $t_2$ hours in a day, then the following can be deduced

$$\frac{m_1 d_1 t_1}{w_1} = \frac{m_2 d_2 t_2}{w_2}$$

$$\text{i.e. } m_1 d_1 t_1 w_2 = m_2 d_2 t_2 w_1$$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
If 20 persons can make 40 toys in 12 days working 12 hours per day. Then, in how many days can 24 persons make 30 toys working 15 hours per day?

### Solution

According to above concept,

$$m_1 d_1 t_1 w_2 = m_2 d_2 t_2 w_1$$

$$20 \times 12 \times 12 \times 30 = 24 \times d_2 \times 15 \times 40$$

$$d_2 = \frac{20 \times 12 \times 12 \times 30}{24 \times 15 \times 40} = 6 \text{ days}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 8
readingSections.content: If P and Q can do a piece of work in x days, Q and R can do the same work in y days and R and P can do the same work in z days, then working together P, Q and R can do that work in = $\frac{2xyz}{yz + xz + xy}$ days

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Manish and Ratnesh can do a piece of work in 3 days, Ratnesh and Nitesh can do the same work in 9 days, while Nitesh and Manish can do the same work in 12 days. What is the duration required for the completion of the task when they collaborate?

### Solution

### Method 1

Here, (Manish + Ratnesh)'s 1 day's work = $\frac{1}{3}$, (Ratnesh + Nitesh)'s 1 day's work = $\frac{1}{9}$

and (Nitesh + Manish)'s 1 day's work = $\frac{1}{12}$

Now, 2 (Manish + Ratnesh + Nitesh)'s 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{12 + 4 + 3}{36} = \frac{19}{36}$$

(Manish + Ratnesh + Nitesh)'s 1 day's work = $\frac{19}{36 \times 2} = \frac{19}{72}$
Hence, (Manish + Ratnesh + Nitesh) complete the whole work in $\frac{72}{19} = 3\frac{15}{19}$ days

According to above concept,

Number of days taken to complete the work by Manish and Ratnesh and Nitesh

$$= \frac{2 \times 3 \times 9 \times 12}{3 \times 9 + 9 \times 12 + 12 \times 3} = 3\frac{15}{19} \text{ days}$$

### Method 2

Let Total Work $= 36$ unit (LCM of 3,9 and 12)

![Book diagram, page 132](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p132-img-37.jpeg)

One day work $= \mathrm{M} + \mathrm{R} + \mathrm{R} + \mathrm{N} + \mathrm{N} + \mathrm{M} = 12 + 4 + 3$

$$
2 (\mathrm {M} + \mathrm {R} + \mathrm {N}) = 1 9 \Rightarrow \mathrm {M} + \mathrm {R} + \mathrm {N} = \frac {1 9}{2} \text {u n i t / d a y}
$$

Number of days in which $\mathrm{M} + \mathrm{R} + \mathrm{N}$ can complete work

$$
= \frac {3 6}{1 9 / 2} = \frac {7 2}{1 9} = 3 \frac {1 5}{1 9} \text {d a y s}.
$$

readingSections.title: Concept 9
readingSections.content: If $\mathfrak{m}_1$ men or $\mathbf{w}_1$ women can finish a work in D days, then time taken by $\mathfrak{m}_2$ men and $\mathbf{w}_2$ women to complete the work in $\frac{\mathrm{D}(\mathfrak{m}_1\mathbf{w}_1)}{(\mathfrak{m}_2\mathbf{w}_1 + \mathfrak{m}_1\mathbf{w}_2)}$ days.

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
If 12 men or 16 women can reap a field in 86 days, how long will 14 men and 10 women taken to reap it?

### Solution

12 men = 16 women; 1 man = $\frac{4}{3}$ women

14 men + 10 women = 14 × $\frac{4}{3}$ women + 10 women = $\frac{56}{3}$

women + 10 women = $\frac{86}{3}$ women

According to the formula,

$$
\mathrm {m} _ {1} \mathrm {d} _ {1} \mathrm {w} _ {2} = \mathrm {m} _ {2} \mathrm {d} _ {2} \mathrm {w} _ {1}
$$

$$
1 6 \times 8 6 \times 1 = (8 6 / 3) \times d _ {2} \times 1
$$

$\mathrm{d}2 = 48$ days

According to above concept,

Required number of days $= \frac{86(16\times 12)}{(14\times 16 + 12\times 10)} = 48$ days

readingSections.title: Concept 10
readingSections.content: If $\mathrm{P}$ can do a work in $\mathbf{x}$ days and $\mathrm{Q}$ can do $\mathrm{y}\%$ faster than $\mathrm{P}$ , then $\mathrm{Q}$ will complete the work in $\frac{100\mathrm{x}}{100 + \mathrm{y}}$ days.

Shruti can do a work in 15 days and Shivi is $50\%$ more expert than Shruti to complete the same work, then find the total time taken by Shivi to complete the work.

### Solution

### Method 1

Number of days in which Shivi complete work

$$

readingSections.title: Concept 11
readingSections.content: If $\mathrm{m}_1$ men can do a piece of work in x days and $\mathrm{b}_1$ boys can do the same work in y days, then time taken to complete the same work by $\mathrm{m}_2$ men and $\mathrm{b}_2$ boys will be $\frac{1}{\frac{\mathrm{m}_2}{\mathrm{m}_1\mathrm{x}} + \frac{\mathrm{b}_2}{\mathrm{b}_1\mathrm{y}}}$ days.

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
If 5 men can do a piece of work in 2 days and 3 boys can do the same work in 5 days, then find time taken to complete the same work by 10 men and 3 boys.

### Solution

1 day work of $5\mathrm{men} = \frac{1}{2}$

1 day work of $1\mathrm{man} = \frac{1}{2\times 5} = \frac{1}{10}$

1 day work of 3 boys $= \frac{1}{5}$

$\therefore 1$ day work of 1 boy $= \frac{1}{3\times 5} = \frac{1}{15}$

Hence, 1 day work of 10 men and 3 boys

134

$$= 10 \times \frac{1}{10} + 3 \times \frac{1}{15} = 1 + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{6}{5}$$

∴ Time taken to complete the work by 10 men and 3 boys

$$= \frac{5}{6} \text{ days}$$

According to above concept,

Required number of days

$$= \frac{1}{\frac{10}{5 \times 2} + \frac{3}{3 \times 5}} = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{1}{5}} = \frac{1}{\frac{6}{5}} = \frac{5}{6} \text{ days}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 12
readingSections.content:
If 'm$_{1}$' men and 'b$_{1}$' boys can do a piece of work in x days and 'm$_{2}$' men and 'b$_{2}$' boys can do the same work in y days, then

$$\frac{1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ man}}{1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ boy}} = \frac{(y_{b_2} - x_{b_1})}{(x_{m_1} - y_{m_2})}$$

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
If 12 men and 16 boys can complete a piece of work in 5 days, while 13 men and 24 boys can complete the same work in 4 days. Compare the 1 day's work of 1 man and 1 boy.

### Solution

$$1 \text{ day work of } 12 \text{ M} + 16 \text{ B} = \frac{1}{5} \quad \dots (i)$$

$$\text{and } 1 \text{ day work of } 13 \text{ M} + 24 \text{ B} = \frac{1}{4} \quad \dots (ii)$$

On solving above two equations, we get

$$1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ man} = \frac{1}{100} \text{ and } 1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ boy} = \frac{1}{200}$$

$$\text{Required comparison} = \frac{1}{100} : \frac{1}{200} = 2 : 1$$

According to above concept,

$$\frac{1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ man}}{1 \text{ day work of } 1 \text{ boy}} = \frac{(4 \times 24 - 5 \times 16)}{(5 \times 12 - 4 \times 13)}$$

$$= \frac{96 - 80}{60 - 52} = \frac{16}{8} = \frac{2}{1}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 13
readingSections.content: If P takes x days more to complete a work than the time taken by (P + Q) to do same work and Q takes y days more than the time taken by (P + Q) to do the same work, then (P + Q) do the work in $\sqrt{\text{xy}}$ days.

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
When Pawan alone does a piece of work, he takes 16 days more than the time taken by (Pawan + Amit) complete the work, while Amit alone takes 9 days more than the time taken

by (Pawan + Amit) to finish the work. What time Pawan and Amit together will take to complete the work?

### Solution

Let time taken by Pawan and Amit to complete the work = x days

According to question,

$$\frac{1}{16 + x} + \frac{1}{9 + x} = \frac{1}{x}$$

$$x(16 + x + 9 + x) = (16 + x)(9 + x)$$

$$25x + 2x^2 = 144 + 16x + 9x + x^2$$

$$x^2 = 144$$

x = 12 (Taking only positive value)

Hence, time taken by Pawan and Amit to complete the work = 12 days

According to above concept,

Required time taken by Pawan and Amit to complete the work = $\sqrt{16 \times 9} = 12$ days

readingSections.title: Concept 14
readingSections.content:
P and Q, each alone can do a piece of work in 'm' and 'n' days, respectively. Both begin together and if

(i) P leaves the work x days before its completion, then total time taken for completion of work will be given as

$$T = \frac{(m + x)n}{(m + n)} \text{ days}$$

(ii) Q leaves the work y days before its completion, then total time taken for completion of work will be given as

$$T = \frac{(n + y)m}{(m + n)} \text{ days}$$

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
Prashant can do a piece of work in 10 days while Sonu can do it in 20 days. They begin together but 2 days before the completion of the work, Prashant leaves off. Determine the overall duration (in days) needed for the completion of the work.

### Solution

### Method 1

Sonu's 2 day's work = $\frac{2}{20} = \frac{1}{10}$, then remaining work

$$= 1 - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{9}{10}$$

(Prashant + Sonu)'s 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{1 + 2}{20} = \frac{3}{20}$$

(Prashant + Sonu) finish $\frac{3}{20}$ work in 1 day.

So, (Prashant + Sonu) will finish $\frac{9}{10}$ work in $\frac{9}{10} \times \frac{20}{3} = 6$ days.

Required total time $= 6 + 2 = 8$ days

According to above concept,

Required time $= \frac{(10 + 2)20}{(10 + 20)} = \frac{240}{30} = 8$ days

### Method 2

Let Total Work $= 20$ unit (LCM of 10 and 20)

![Book diagram, page 134](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p134-img-39.jpeg)

Prashant leaves 2 days before, work done in 2 days alone by Sonu $= 2 \times 1 = 2$ unit

Rest all work done by Prashant and Sonu both $= 20 - 2 = 18$ unit

Number of days taken by Prashant and Sonu both

$$= \frac{18}{3} = 6 \text{ days.}$$

Total number of days $= 6 + 2 = 8$ days.

readingSections.title: Example 16
readingSections.content:
Pragun can do a piece of work in 10 days while Saurabh can do it in 15 days. They begin together but 5 days before the completion of the work, Saurabh leaves off. Determine the overall duration (in days) needed for the completion of the work.

### Solution

### Method 1

Pragun's 5 day's work $= \frac{5}{10} = \frac{1}{2}$, then remaining work

$$= 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

(Pragun + Saurabh)'s 1 day's work

$$= \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{3 + 2}{30} = \frac{5}{30} = \frac{1}{6}$$

(Pragun + Saurabh) finish $\frac{1}{6}$ work in 1 day.

So, (Pragun + Saurabh) will finish $\frac{1}{2}$ work in $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3$ days.

Required total time $= 5 + 3 = 8$ days

According to above concept,

Required time $= \frac{(15 + 5)10}{(15 + 10)} = \frac{200}{25} = 8$ days

### Method 2

Let Total Work $= 30$ unit (LCM of 10 and 15)

![Book diagram, page 134](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p134-img-40.jpeg)

Saurabh leaves 5 days before, work done in 5 days alone by Pargun $= 3 \times 5 = 15$ unit

Rest all work done by Pargun and Saurabh both $= 30 - 10 = 15$ unit

Number of days taken by Pargun and Saurabh both $= \frac{15}{5} = 3$ days.

Total number of days $= 3 + 5 = 8$ days.

readingSections.title: Concept 15
readingSections.content:
P and Q do a piece of work in 'm' and 'n' days, respectively. Both begin together but after some days, P leaves off and the remaining work is completed by Q in x days. Then, the time after which P left, is given by

$$T = \frac{(n - x)m}{m + n} \text{ days}$$

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
P and Q do a piece of work in 40 days and 50 days, respectively. Both begin together but after a certain time, P leaves off. In this case, Q finishes the remaining work in 20 days. After how many days did P leave?

### Solution

### Method 1

Q's 20 day's work $= \frac{20}{50} = \frac{2}{5}$, then remaining work

$$= 1 - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5}$$

(P + Q)'s 1 day's work $= \frac{1}{40} + \frac{1}{50} = \frac{5 + 4}{200} = \frac{9}{200}$

(P + Q) did $\frac{9}{200}$ work in 1 day.

So, (P + Q) will do $\frac{3}{5}$ work in

$$\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{200}{9} = \frac{40}{3} = 13\frac{1}{3} \text{ days}$$

According to above concept,

Required time $= \frac{(50 - 20)40}{(40 + 50)} = \frac{1200}{90} = \frac{40}{3} = 13\frac{1}{3}$ days

### Method 2

Let Total Work = 200 unit (LCM of 40 and 50)

![Book diagram, page 135](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p135-img-41.jpeg)

Work done by Q alone in 20 days = 20 × 4 = 80 units

Remaining work done by P and Q together in

$$= \frac{200 - 80}{5 + 4} = \frac{120}{9} = 13\frac{1}{3} \text{ days.}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 16
readingSections.content: When two people A and B work alternately i.e. on alternate days/hours. Either A or B starting the work. Then we have to calculate how many work will be completed in how many days.

readingSections.title: Example 18
readingSections.content:
A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 9 days and 15 days respectively. If they work for a day alternately, with A beginning, then the work will be completed in?

### Solution

### Method 1

Let's assume that the total work is 45 units (LCM of 9 and 15).

In one day, A can complete 5 units of work and B can complete 3 units of work.

If they work alternately, then in two days, they can complete 8 units of work (5 + 3).

Therefore, they can complete 40 units of work in 10 days (5 cycles of 2 days each).

On the 11th day, A will work and complete 5 units of work, thus completing the total work. Therefore, the work will be completed in 11 days.

### Method 2

Let Total Work = 45 unit (LCM of 9 and 15)

![Book diagram, page 135](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p135-img-42.jpeg)

1$^{st}$ day A work = 5 unit, 2$^{nd}$ day B work = 3 unit,

So, in every 2 days work done = 5+3 = 8 unit

So, in (2×5)10 days work done = (8×5) 40 unit

Remaining work 45 – 40 = 5 unit

And now it's A's turn A will come and in 1 day he does 5 work.

Hence, In (10+1) 11 days total work (40+5) 45 will be completed.

![Book diagram, page 136](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p136-img-43.jpeg)

Work and Wages
Work refers to tasks or activities that require physical exertion
and are undertaken to accomplish a specific outcome.
Money received by a person for a certain work is called the
Wages of the person for that particular work.
Entire Wages = Total number of days × Wages of 1 day

implies that the compensation received is directly
proportional to the amount of work done; higher the

(ii) The compensation received by a person is inversely
related to the duration of time spent on the task.
(iii) The remuneration received is directly linked to the
amount of work done in a single day by an individual.

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
WORK AND WAGES

Work refers to tasks or activities that require physical exertion and are undertaken to accomplish a specific outcome.

Money received by a person for a certain work is called the Wages of the person for that particular work.

Entire Wages = Total number of days × Wages of 1 day of a person

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
If Puneet's monthly wages is ₹ 4200 and he worked for all 30 days, then his daily wages will be calculated as

$$\text{Total wages} = \text{Number of days} \times \text{Daily wages}$$

$$4200 = 30 \times \text{Daily wages}$$

$$\text{Daily wages} = 4200 \div 30 = ₹ 140$$

Some Important Points:

- (i) Wages is directly proportional to the work done. This implies that the compensation received is directly proportional to the amount of work done; higher the work, greater the pay, and vice versa.
- (ii) The compensation received by a person is inversely related to the duration of time spent on the task.
- (iii) The remuneration received is directly linked to the amount of work done in a single day by an individual.

For Example:

If Kapil can do a piece of work in 10 days and Arjun can do the same piece of work in 15 days. Then, ratio of Kapil and Arjun's wages will be 15: 10, i.e. 3: 2.

- (iv) If P, Q and R can do a piece of work in d₁, d₂ and d₃ days respectively, then ratio of their shares is d₂d₃ : d₃d₁ : d₁d₂

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content:
If P and Q can do a piece of work in x and y days respectively, the ratio of their wages will be y: x. Then, the wages earned by P and Q will be

$$\text{P's wages} = \frac{\text{Total wages}}{x + y} \times y;$$

$$\text{Q's wages} = \frac{\text{Total wages}}{x + y} \times x$$

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
Anushika can do a piece of work in 6 days, while Vandana can do the same work in 5 days. If the total amount to be given for his work is ₹ 6600, then what will be the share of Vandana, if both work together?

### Solution

Time taken by Anushika = 6 days

$$\therefore 1 \text{ day's work of Anushika} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Time taken by Vandana = 5 days

$$\therefore 1 \text{ day's work of Vandana} = \frac{1}{5}$$

$$\text{Ratio of their incomes} = \frac{1}{6} : \frac{1}{5} = 5 : 6$$

Give, total amount earned = ₹ 6600

$$\text{Vandana's share} = \frac{6}{5 + 6} \times 6600 = ₹ 3600$$

LCM Method:

![Book diagram, page 140](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p140-img-44.jpeg)

Ratio of their incomes = Ratio of their efficiencies = 5 : 6

Given, total amount earned = ₹ 6600

$$\text{Vandana's share} = \frac{6}{5 + 6} \times 6600 = ₹ 3600$$

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If P, Q and R can do a piece of work in x, y and z days respectively, the ratio of their wages will be yz:

xz: xy. Then, the wages earned by P, Q and R will be

$$P\text{'s wages} = \frac{\text{Total wages}}{(yz + xz + xy)} \times yz;$$

$$Q\text{'s wages} = \frac{\text{Total wages}}{(yz + xz + xy)} \times xz$$

$$R\text{'s wages} = \frac{\text{Total wages}}{(yz + xz + xy)} \times xy$$

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
Tushar, Anushika and Maahi take ₹ 5350 for doing a piece of work together. If working alone, each takes 5 days, 6 days and 7 days respectively, then find the share of each.

### Solution

According to above concept,

Tushar's share

$$= \frac{5350}{(6 \times 7 + 5 \times 7 + 5 \times 6)} \times (6 \times 7) = \frac{5350 \times 42}{107}$$
$$= ₹ 2100$$

Anushika's share

$$= \frac{5350}{(6 \times 7 + 5 \times 7 + 5 \times 6)} \times (5 \times 7) = \frac{5350 \times 35}{107}$$
$$= ₹ 1750$$

Maahi's share

$$= \frac{5350}{(6 \times 7 + 5 \times 7 + 5 \times 6)} \times (5 \times 6) = \frac{5350 \times 30}{107}$$
$$= ₹ 1500$$

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
Total wages earned by certain persons in doing certain work

= (1 person's 1 day wages) × (Number of persons) × (Number of days)

Required number of persons

$$= \frac{\text{Total wages}}{\text{Number of days} + 1 \text{ person's 1 day wages}}$$

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Wages of 45 women for 48 days amount to ₹ 31050. How many men must work for 16 days to receive ₹ 11500, if daily wages of a man being double of a woman?

### Solution

According to above concept,

$$1 \text{ day's wages of a woman} = \frac{31050}{45 \times 48} = ₹ \frac{115}{8}$$

$$1 \text{ day's wages of a man} = ₹ \frac{115}{8} \times 2 = ₹ \frac{115}{4}$$

$$\text{Required number of men} = \frac{11500}{16 \times \frac{115}{4}} = 25$$

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content:
P can do a piece of work in x days. With the help of Q, P can do the same piece of work in y days. If they get ₹ R for that work, then

$$\text{Share of P} = ₹ \left( \frac{Ry}{x} \right); \quad \text{and share of Q} = ₹ \left[ \frac{R(x - y)}{x} \right]$$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Dinesh can do a piece of work in 20 days. Dinesh and Suresh together do the same work in 15 days. If they got ₹ 6400 for that work, then find the share of Dinesh and Suresh.

### Solution

$$\begin{array}{ccc} D & 20 & 3 \\ D + S & 15 & 60 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Ratio of their incomes = Ratio of their efficiencies = 3 : 1

Given, total amount earned = ₹ 6400

$$\text{Dinesh's share} = \frac{3}{3 + 1} \times 6400 = ₹ 4800$$

$$\text{Suresh's share} = \frac{1}{3 + 1} \times 6400 = ₹ 1600$$

According to above concept,

$$\text{Share of P} = ₹ \left( \frac{6400 \times 15}{20} \right) = ₹ 4800 \text{ and share of Q} = ₹$$

$$\left[ \frac{6400(20 - 15)}{20} \right] = ₹ 1600$$

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
P, Q and R undertake to do a work for ₹ M. If P and Q together do only (p/q) of the work and rest is done by R alone, then the share of R is given by

$$M \left( 1 - \frac{p}{q} \right)$$

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
P, Q and R undertake to do a work for ₹ 4800. If P and Q together do only (1/4) of the work and rest is done by R alone. How much should R get?

### Solution

According to above concept,

$$\text{Share of } R = M \left( 1 - \frac{p}{q} \right) = 4800 \left( 1 - \frac{1}{4} \right) = 4800 \times \frac{3}{4} = ₹\ 3600$$

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Vijayshree and Poorna contracted a piece of work for ₹ 3200. Vijayshree alone can do it in 6 days, while Poorna can do that work in 8 days. They completed the work in 3 days taking help of Kshma. Find the share of Kshma.

### Solution

$$\text{Vijayshree's 1 day's work} = \frac{1}{6}$$

$$\text{Poorna's 1 day's work} = \frac{1}{8}$$

Let Kshma can do the work in 'n' days, then Kshma's 1 day's work =  $\frac{1}{n}$

According to the question,

(Vijayshree + Poorna + Kshma) complete the work in 3 days.

Vijayshree's 3 day's work + Poorna's 3 day's work + Kshma's 3 day's work = 1

$$\frac{3}{6} + \frac{3}{8} + \frac{3}{n} = 1$$

on solving above, we get;  $n = 24$

$$\text{Vijayshree's share : Poorna's share : Kshma's share} = \frac{1}{6} : \frac{1}{8} : \frac{1}{24} = 4 : 3 : 1$$

$$\text{Kshma's share} = \frac{1}{(4+3+1)} \times 3200 = 400$$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Bhumika can do a piece of work in 10 days, while Gayatri can do it in 15 days. They work together for 5 days and rest

of the work is done by Anjali in 2 days. If they get ₹ 18000, then how much should they divide the money?

### Solution

Time taken by Bhumika = 10 days; then Bhumika's 1 day's

$$\text{work} = \frac{1}{10}$$

and time taken by Gayatri = 15 days;

$$\text{then Gayatri's 1 day's work} = \frac{1}{15}$$

Now, (Bhumika + Gayatri)'s 5 day's work

$$= 5 \left( \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} \right) = 5 \left( \frac{3+2}{30} \right) = 5 \times \frac{5}{30} = \frac{5}{6}$$

Remaining work =  $1 - (5/6) = 1/6$

$$\text{Anjali's 2 day's work} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Now, required ratio between shares = Bhumika's 5 day's work : Gayatri's 5 day's work : Anjali's 2 day's work

$$= \frac{5}{10} : \frac{5}{15} : \frac{1}{6}$$

$$= 15 : 10 : 5 = 3 : 2 : 1$$

$$\text{Bhumika's share} = \frac{18000}{(3+2+1)} \times 3 = 18000 \div 2 = ₹\ 9000;$$

$$\text{Gayatri's share} = \frac{18000}{(3+2+1)} \times 2 = 18000 \div 3 = ₹\ 6000$$

$$\text{Anjali's share} = \frac{18000}{(3+2+1)} \times 1 = 18000 \div 6 = ₹\ 3000$$
