readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
PIPE AND CISTERN

In the context of pipes and cisterns, pipes serve as channels that can either add to or deplete the volume of a tank or cistern. The operation of these pipes, whether it's filling or draining, constitutes the work performed.

**Inlet Pipe:** It fills a tank/cistern/reservoir.

**Outlet Pipe:** It empties a tank/cistern/reservoir.

readingSections.title: Important Facts Related to Pipes and Cisterns
readingSections.content:
(i) If a pipe can fill/empty a tank in 'x' hours, then the part of tank filled/emptied in 1 hour = $\frac{1}{x}$

**For Example:** If a pipe can fill the tank in 13 hours, then the volume of tank filled in 1 hour = $\frac{1}{13}$

(ii) If a pipe can fill/empty '1/x' part of a tank in 1 hour, then it can fill/empty the whole tank in 'x' hours.

**For Example:** If a pipe can fill $\frac{1}{13}$ part of the tank in 1 hour, then it can fill the whole tank in 13 hours.

(iii) Time taken to fill a tank is taken positive (+) ve and time taken to empty a tank is taken negative (-) ve.

(iv) If a pipe fills a tank in 'x' hours and another pipe fills in 'y' hours. Then, part filled by both pipes in 1 hour = $\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y}$

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
An outlet pipe can empty a cistern in 25 hours. What time it takes for a pipe to empty $\frac{2}{5}$ portion of a cistern?

### Solution

Time taken to empty full cistern = 25 hours

Time taken to empty $\frac{2}{5}$ part of the cistern

$$= \frac{2}{5} \times 25 = 10 \text{ hours}$$

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
If a pipe can fill a tank in 4 hours and another pipe can fill the same tank in 12 hours, then what part of a tank will be filled by both the piped in 1 hour, if they are opened simultaneously.

### Solution

In 1 hour, part filled by 1$^{st}$ pipe = $\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{4}$

In 1 hour, part filled by 2$^{nd}$ pipe = $\frac{1}{y} = \frac{1}{12}$

$\therefore$ In 1 hour, part filled by both the pipes together

$$= \left( \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} \right) = \left( \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{12} \right)$$
$$= \left( \frac{3+1}{12} \right) = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3} \text{ part}$$

readingSections.title: L.C.M. Method
readingSections.content:
![Book diagram, page 145](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p145-img-46.jpeg)

In 1 hour, tank filled = 4 units

Required answer = $\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
If a pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours and another pipe can empty the same tank in 30 hours, then what part of a tank will be filled by both the piped in 1 hour, if they are opened simultaneously.

### Solution

In 1 hour, part filled by 1$^{st}$ pipe = $\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{15}$

In 1 hour, part emptied by 2$^{nd}$ pipe = $\frac{1}{y} = \frac{1}{30}$

$\therefore$ In 1 hour, part filled by both the pipes together

$$= \left( \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{y} \right) = \left( \frac{1}{15} - \frac{1}{30} \right)$$

$$
= \left(\frac {2 - 1}{3 0}\right) = \frac {1}{3 0} \text { part}
$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
![Book diagram, page 146](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p146-img-47.jpeg)

In 1 hour, tank filled $= 1$ units

Required answer $= \frac{1}{30}$

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content:
A pipe can fill/empty a tank in 'x' hours and another pipe can fill/empty the same tank in 'y' hours.

(i) If both pipes either fill or empty the tank, then the time taken to fill or empty the tank when both pipes are opened, is

$$
T = \frac {x y}{x + y}
$$

(ii) If first pipe fills the tank and second pipe empties the tank, then the time taken to fill the tank when both pipes are opened, is

$$
T = \frac {x y}{x - y}, \text { where } x > y
$$

(iii) If first pipe fills the tank and second pipe empties the tank, then the time taken to empty the tank when both pipes are opened, is

$$
T = \frac {x y}{y - x}, \text { where } y > x
$$

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 18 hours and 12 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then how much time will be taken to fill the tank?

### Solution

According to concept,

Time taken to fill the tank (T)

$$
= \frac {x y}{x + y} = \frac {1 8 \times 1 2}{1 8 + 1 2} = \frac {2 1 6}{3 0} = \frac {3 6}{5} = 7 \frac {1}{5} \text { hours}
$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
![Book diagram, page 146](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p146-img-48.jpeg)

In 1 hour, tank filled $= 5$ units

Required answer $= \frac{36}{5} = 7\frac{1}{5}$

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours while another pipe can empty it in 12 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then how much time will be taken to fill the tank?

### Solution

According to concept,

Time taken to fill the tank (T)

$$
= \frac {x y}{x - y} = \frac {1 2 \times 1 0}{1 2 - 1 0} = \frac {1 2 0}{2} = 6 0 \text { hours}
$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
![Book diagram, page 146](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p146-img-49.jpeg)

In 1 hour, tank filled $= 1$ units

Required answer $= \frac{60}{1} = 60$ hours

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. Due to a leak in the bottom, it fills the tank in 20 hours. How long would it take for the leak to drain the tank completely if it's full?

### Solution

According to concept,

Time taken to fill the tank (T)

$$
= \frac {x y}{y - x} = \frac {1 0 \times 2 0}{2 0 - 1 0} = \frac {2 0 0}{1 0} = 2 0 \text { hours}
$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
![Book diagram, page 146](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p146-img-50.jpeg)

In 1 hour, tank being emptied by leak $= 1$ units

Required answer $= \frac{20}{1} = 20$ hours

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If three pipes can fill a tank separately in $x$ , $y$ and $z$ hours respectively, then part of the tank filled in 1 hour by all the three pipes is given by $\left(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z}\right)$ and total time taken to fill

the tank is given by $\frac{\mathrm{xyz}}{(\mathrm{xy} + \mathrm{yz} + \mathrm{zx})}$ hours.

150

If a single pipe from the three is employed to drain the tank, then the time that specific pipe takes will be represented as a negative value. Suppose, third pipe is used to empty the tank. Then, the above formulae takes the form as $$\left(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} - \frac{1}{z}\right)$$ and $$\frac{xyz}{(yz + zx - xy)}$$ hours

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Three pipes P, Q and R can fill a tank separately in 4, 5 and 6 hours respectively. Determine the duration required for all three pipes to fill the tank when they are simultaneously opened.

### Solution

According to concept,

Total time taken to fill the tank

$$= \frac{4 \times 5 \times 6}{(4 \times 5 + 5 \times 6 + 6 \times 4)} = \frac{120}{74} = 1\frac{23}{37} \text{ hours}$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
$$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{cc} P & 4 \\ Q & 5 \end{array} \begin{array}{c} 60 \\ 10 \end{array} \begin{array}{c} 15 \\ 12 \end{array} \\ R & 6 \end{array}$$

In 1 hour, tank filled = 37 units

Required answer = $$\frac{60}{37} = 1\frac{23}{37}$$ hours

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Pipe P can fill a tank in 20 hours while pipe Q alone can fill it in 10 hours and pipe R can empty the full tank in 30 hours. If all the pipes are opened together, then how much time will be needed to make the tank full?

### Solution

According to concept,

Total time taken to fill the tank

$$= \frac{20 \times 10 \times 30}{(10 \times 30 + 20 \times 30 - 20 \times 10)} = \frac{6000}{700} = 8\frac{4}{7} \text{ hours}$$

readingSections.title: LCM Method
readingSections.content:
$$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{cc} P & 20 \\ Q & 10 \end{array} \begin{array}{c} 60 \\ 2 \end{array} \begin{array}{c} 3 \\ 6 \end{array} \\ R & -30 \end{array} \begin{array}{c} 60 \\ -2 \end{array}$$

In 1 hour, part of the tank filled = 7 units

Required answer = $$\frac{60}{7} = 8\frac{4}{7}$$ hours

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content: Two pipes P and Q together can fill a tank in time T. If time taken by P alone is more than T by 'x' and time taken by Q alone is more than T by 'y', then $$T = \sqrt{xy}$$

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Two pipes P and Q are opened together to fill a tank. The tank is filled by both pipes in a duration of T. If P separately takes 16 minutes more time than T to fill the tank and Q takes 25 minutes more than T to fill the tank, then find the value of T.

### Solution

According to concept,

$$T = \sqrt{25 \times 16} = 20 \text{ hours}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content:
A full tank gets emptied in 'x' hours due to presence of a leak in it. If a tap which fills it at a rate of 'y' Litre/hours, is opened, then it gets emptied in 'z' hours. Therefore,

Volume of the tank = $$\frac{xyz}{z - x}$$

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A full tank gets emptied in 6 minutes due to presence of an orifice in it. On opening a tap which can fill the tank at the rate of 8 Litre/minutes, the tank gets emptied in 10 minutes. Find the capacity of tank.

### Solution

According to concept,

Capacity of the tank = $$\frac{6 \times 8 \times 10}{10 - 6} = 120 \text{ Litres}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
If two taps P and Q, which can fill a tank, such that efficiency of P is 'n' times of Q and takes T minutes less/more than Q to fill the tank, then

- (i) Time taken to fill the tank by both taps together = $$\frac{nT}{n^2 - 1}$$
- (ii) Time taken to fill the tank by faster tap = $$\frac{T}{n - 1}$$ minutes
- (iii) Time taken to fill the tank by slower tap = $$\frac{nT}{n - 1}$$ minutes

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
Pipe P can fill a tank 3 times faster than pipe Q and takes 14 minutes less than pipe Q to fill the tank. If we open both pipes at the same time, how long will it take to fill the tank?

### Solution

Ratio between Efficiency of pipes P and Q = 3 : 1

Ratio between Time taken by pipes P and Q to fill the tank = 1 : 3

According to question,

$$(3 - 1) = 14$$

$$2 = 14$$

$$1 = 7$$

Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank =  $1 \times 7 = 7$  minutes

Time taken by pipe Q to fill the tank =  $3 \times 7 = 21$  minutes

Required time to fill the tank when both pipes are open =

$$\frac{21 \times 7}{(21+7)} = \frac{147}{28} = (21/4) \text{ minutes}$$

readingSections.title: According to concept,
readingSections.content:
Required time to fill the tank when both pipes are open =

$$\frac{3 \times 14}{3^2 - 1} = (21/4) \text{ minutes}$$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
Pipe P is 3 times slower than the pipe Q and takes 32 minutes less than pipe Q to fill the tank. How much time will pipe Q take to fill the tank?

### Solution

Ratio between Efficiency of pipes P and Q = 1 : 3

Ratio between Time taken by pipes P and Q to fill the tank = 3 : 1

According to question,

$$(3 - 1) = 32$$

$$2 = 32$$

$$1 = 16$$

Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank =  $3 \times 16 = 48$  minutes

Time taken by pipe Q to fill the tank =  $1 \times 16 = 16$  minutes

readingSections.title: According to concept,
readingSections.content: Required time to fill the tank by faster pipe =  $\frac{32}{3-1} = 16$  minutes

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
Pipe P is 2 times slower than pipe Q and takes 18 minutes more time than the pipe Q to fill the tank. How much time will pipe P take to fill the tank?

### Solution

Ratio between Efficiency of pipes P and Q = 1 : 2

Ratio between Time taken by pipes P and Q to fill the tank = 2 : 1

According to question,

$$(2 - 1) = 18$$

$$1 = 18$$

Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank =  $2 \times 18 = 36$  minutes

readingSections.title: According to concept,
readingSections.content:
Required time to fill the tank by slower tap

$$= \frac{2 \times 18}{2 - 1} = 36 \text{ minutes}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content:
Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in x minutes and y minutes respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously,

then the time after which pipe Q should be closed, so that the tank is full in T minutes, is  $\left[ y \left( 1 - \frac{T}{x} \right) \right]$  minutes.

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 12 hours and 16 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then after how much time should Q be closed so that the tank is full in 9 minutes?

### Solution

In 1 minute, part filled by pipe A =  $\frac{1}{12}$

and part filled by pipe B =  $\frac{1}{16}$

Let the pipe Q closed after n minutes.

According to the question,

$$n \left( \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{16} \right) + (9 - n) \left( \frac{1}{12} \right) = 1$$

$$n \left( \frac{4+3}{48} \right) + (9 - n) \left( \frac{1}{12} \right) = 1$$

$$7n + 36 - 4n = 48$$

$$3n = 12$$

$$n = 4$$

Hence, pipe Q should be closed after 4 minutes.

readingSections.title: According to concept,
readingSections.content:
Required time to fill the tank when both pipes are open

$$= 16 \left( 1 - \frac{9}{12} \right) = 4 \text{ minutes}$$

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
A cistern is provided with two pipes A and B. A can fill it in 40 minutes and B can empty it in 60 minutes. If they are opened alternately for one minute each how soon will the cistern be filled?

### Solution

$$\begin{array}{ccc} \text{A} & 40 & +3 \\ \text{B} & 60 & -2 \end{array}$$

Part of the tank is filled in 2 minutes by Pipes A and B each for 1 minute =  $3 - 2 = 1$

117 units of tank is filled in  $117 \times 2 = 234$  minutes

Remaining part of the tank =  $120 - 117 = 3$  units

3 units of tank is being filled by pipe A in 1 minute.

Total time to fill the tank =  $234 + 1 = 235$  minute

The concept of ratio can generally be applied to problems involving

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content: SPEED, TIME & DISTANCE

readingSections.title: Speed
readingSections.content:
In the context of motion, speed is defined as the measure of how quickly an object moves. It's determined by the total distance (D) an object travels divided by the time (T) it takes to travel that distance. The mathematical representation of speed (S) is:

$$S = \frac{D}{T}$$

readingSections.title: Time
readingSections.content:
Time (T) can be calculated by dividing the total distance covered (D) by the speed (S). The formula for time is:

$$T = \frac{D}{S}$$

readingSections.title: Distance
readingSections.content:
Distance (D) can be calculated by multiplying the speed (S) by the time (T). The distance formula is:

$$D = S \times T$$

readingSections.title: Units
readingSections.content:
The standard units used for these measurements are as follows:

- **Time:** seconds (sec), minutes (min), hours (hr), etc.
  - 1 minute = 60 seconds
  - 1 hour = 60 minutes = 3600 seconds
- **Distance:** meter (m), kilometer (km), feet (ft), miles (mi), etc.
  - 1 kilometer = 1000 meters
- **Speed:** meters per second (m/sec), kilometers per hour (km/hr), etc.

readingSections.title: Conversion
readingSections.content:
To convert speed from km/hr to m/sec, multiply by $\left(\frac{1000}{60 \times 60}\right) = \frac{5}{18}$ and to convert from m/sec to km/hr, do the reverse.

- We can express the conversion ratio between kilometers per hour (Km/hr) and meters per second (m/s) as 18 : 5.

$$(\text{Km/hr}): (\text{m/s}) = 18 : 5$$

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Convert 72 km/hr into meter/sec.

### Solution

**Method 1:** To convert speed from km/hr to m/sec, we multiply by 5/18. So,

$$72 \text{ km/hr} \times \frac{5}{18} = 20 \text{ m/sec}$$

**Method 2:** (Km/hr): (m/s) = 18:5

$$\frac{72}{\text{m/sec}} = \frac{18}{5}$$

In, m/sec = 20 m/sec

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
A cyclist travels at a speed of 24 km/h. How many meters does she cover in 5 minutes?

### Solution

Convert speed from km/h to m/min: Speed in m/min

$$= 24 \text{ km/h} = \frac{24 \times 1000}{60} = 400 \text{ m/min}$$

Distance = Speed $\times$ Time = 400 m/min $\times$ 5 min = 2000 meters

readingSections.title: Average Speed Based
readingSections.content:
Average speed is a measure of the total distance covered by an object during a specific time. The formula of average speed is:

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}$$

$$S_A = \frac{D_s}{T_s}$$

For instance, if a vehicle covers a distance of 80 kilometers in 1 hour, its average speed would be 80 kilometers per hour.

Case 1: When time and distance are given

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {D _ {1} + D _ {2} + D _ {3} + \dots}{T _ {1} + T _ {2} + T _ {3} + \dots}
$$

"Where $\mathrm{D}_1, \mathrm{D}_2, \mathrm{D}_3, \ldots$ are the distances traveled partially, and $\mathrm{T}_1, \mathrm{T}_2, \mathrm{T}_3, \ldots$ are the times taken for those partial distances."

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
Arjun embarks on a voyage where he covers three separate distances. He initially covers a distance of $14\mathrm{km}$ in 20 minutes and then travels $25\mathrm{km}$ in 30 minutes, and finally, he traverses $60\mathrm{km}$ in an hour. What is his Average speed for the entire voyage?

### Solution

Let's calculate the total distance D that Arjun has covered, which is the sum of the three distances:

$$
\mathrm {D} = \mathrm {D} _ {1} + \mathrm {D} _ {2} + \mathrm {D} _ {3} = 1 4 \mathrm {k m} + 2 5 \mathrm {k m} + 6 0 \mathrm {k m} = 9 9 \mathrm {k m}
$$

Next, we calculate the total time T taken by Arjun. We convert all times to hours for consistency:

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathrm {T} = \mathrm {T} _ {1} + \mathrm {T} _ {2} + \mathrm {T} _ {3} \\ = \frac {2 0 \min}{6 0} + \frac {3 0 \min}{6 0} + 1 \text {h o u r} = \frac {1 1}{6} \text {h o u r s} \\ \end{array}
$$

Finally, we calculate the average speed $S_{\mathrm{A}}$ as the total distance divided by the total time:

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {D}{T} = \frac {9 9 k m}{\frac {1 1}{6} h o u r s} = 5 4 k m / h r
$$

Case 2: When time and speed are given

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {D _ {1} + D _ {2} + D _ {3} + \dots}{T _ {1} + T _ {2} + T _ {3} + \dots}
$$

Replace $\mathrm{D}_1 + \mathrm{D}_2 + \mathrm{D}_3 + \ldots = (\mathrm{S}_1\times \mathrm{T}_1) + (\mathrm{S}_2\times \mathrm{T}_2) + (\mathrm{S}_3\times \mathrm{T}_3)$ $+\ldots$

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {\left(S _ {1} \times T _ {1}\right) + \left(S _ {2} \times T _ {2}\right) + \left(S _ {3} \times T _ {3}\right) + \dots}{T _ {1} + T _ {2} + T _ {3} + \dots}

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
In the course of his trip, Rohan spends a quarter of an hour moving at a pace of $40\mathrm{km / h}$ , followed by 25 minutes at $60\mathrm{km / h}$ , and concludes with an hour at $70\mathrm{km / h}$ . Can you determine his average speed over the entire trip?

### Solution

Total distance travelled $= \mathrm{D}_1 + \mathrm{D}_2 + \mathrm{D}_3$

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \mathrm {S} _ {1} \times \mathrm {T} _ {1} + \mathrm {S} _ {2} \times \mathrm {T} _ {2} + \mathrm {S} _ {3} \times \mathrm {T} _ {3} \\ = 4 0 \times \frac {1 5}{6 0} + 6 0 \times \frac {2 5}{6 0} + 7 0 \times 1 = 1 0 + 2 5 + 7 0 = 1 0 5 \mathrm {k m} \\ \end{array}
$$

Total time $= \mathrm{T}_{1} + \mathrm{T}_{2} + \mathrm{T}_{3} = \frac{(15 + 25 + 60)}{60}$ hour $= 5 / 3$ hour

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {1 0 5}{\left(\frac {5}{3}\right)} = 6 3 k m / h r
$$

Case 3: When distance and speed is given

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {D _ {1} + D _ {2} + D _ {3} + \dots}{T _ {1} + T _ {2} + T _ {3} + \dots}
$$

Replace $\mathrm{T}_1 + \mathrm{T}_2 + \mathrm{T}_3 + \dots$

$$
= \left(\frac {D _ {1}}{S _ {1}}\right) + \left(\frac {D _ {2}}{S _ {2}}\right) + \left(\frac {D _ {3}}{S _ {3}}\right) + \dots
$$

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {D _ {1} + D _ {2} + D _ {3} + \dots}{\left(\frac {D _ {1}}{S _ {1}} + \frac {D _ {2}}{S _ {2}} + \frac {D _ {3}}{S _ {3}} \dots\right)}

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
A person travels a distance of $150\mathrm{km}$ by train at a speed of $50~\mathrm{km / h}$ , then covers another $140\mathrm{km}$ by bus moving at a speed of $35\mathrm{km / h}$ , and finally completes the last $40\mathrm{km}$ of the journey by auto, moving at a speed of $20\mathrm{km / h}$ . We are tasked with determining the average speed for the entire journey.

### Solution

Total distance traveled $= \mathrm{D}_1 + \mathrm{D}_2 + \mathrm{D}_3 = 150 + 140 + 40 = 330\mathrm{km}$

Total time $= \mathrm{T}_{1} + \mathrm{T}_{2} + \mathrm{T}_{3} = \left(\frac{D_{1}}{S_{1}}\right) + \left(\frac{D_{2}}{S_{2}}\right) + \left(\frac{D_{3}}{S_{3}}\right)$

$$
= \left(\frac {1 5 0}{5 0}\right) + \left(\frac {1 4 0}{3 5}\right) + \left(\frac {4 0}{2 0}\right) = 9 \mathrm {h r}
$$

$$
S _ {A} = \frac {3 3 0}{9} = 3 6. 6 6 k m / h r
$$

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
On a straight track, a locomotive covers half the distance at a pace of $40\mathrm{km / h}$ , a third of what's left at $45\mathrm{km / h}$ , and completes the journey at $50\mathrm{km / h}$ . Can you calculate the locomotive's average speed throughout the trip?

### Solution

The total distance covered by the locomotive is assumed to be $600\mathrm{km}$

The locomotive covers half the distance at a speed of 40 km/h, which is $600 / 2 = 300$ km.

A third of what's left $(600 - 300 = 300\mathrm{km})$ is covered at a speed of $45~\mathrm{km / h}$ , which is $300 / 3 = 100\mathrm{km}$ .

156

The remaining distance (600 - 300 - 100 = 200 km) is covered at a speed of 50 km/h. which is = 200 km.

Total distance traveled= $D_1 + D_2 + D_3 = 600$ km

$$\text{Total time} = T_1 + T_2 + T_3 = \left(\frac{D_1}{S_1}\right) + \left(\frac{D_2}{S_2}\right) + \left(\frac{D_3}{S_3}\right)$$

$$= \left(\frac{300}{40}\right) + \left(\frac{100}{45}\right) + \left(\frac{200}{50}\right) = 13.72 \text{ hr}$$

$$S_A = \frac{600}{13.72} = 43.72 \text{ km/hr (Approximately)}$$

**Case 4:** When distances are equal

- ○ **When a journey involves covering the same distance at two different speeds, the formula to compute the average speed is as follows:**

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{2XY}{X+Y}$$

Here, X and Y denote the two different speeds.

- ○ **When the same distance is travelled at three different speeds, the formula to calculate the average speed is:**

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{3XYZ}{XY+YZ+ZX}$$

Here, X, Y, and Z denote the three different speeds.

- ○ Another method for average speed if speed is given: If two or more speeds are given for the same distance, then take the number of given speeds and multiply it by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the speeds. Then, divide this by the sum of the division value of the LCM for each speed. For example, if the 'n' number of speeds is given and the speeds are X, Y, Z, etc., and the LCM is K, then the average speed can be calculated as follows:

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{nK}{\left(\frac{K}{X} + \frac{K}{Y} + \frac{K}{Z} + \dots\right)}$$

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Rahul covers a distance from his house to coaching at the speed of 75 km/hr and returns at the speed of 50 km/hr, what is his average speed?

### Solution

### Method 1

X = 75 km/hr, Y = 50 km/hr

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{2XY}{X+Y}$$

$$= \frac{2 \times 75 \times 50}{75+50} = 60 \text{ km/hr}$$

### Method 2

So, 'n' is 2 (the number of given speeds), 'X' is 75 km/hr (the speed to the coaching), and 'Y' is 50 km/hr (the speed back). The LCM of 75 and 50 is K=150.

readingSections.title: Let's substitute these values into the formula
readingSections.content: $$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{2 \times 150}{\left(\frac{150}{75} + \frac{150}{50}\right)} = \frac{2 \times 150}{(2+3)} = 60 \text{ km/hr}$$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Anuj walks around a rhombus plot and covers the distance of each side at the speeds of 6 km/hr, 18 km/hr, 12 km/hr, and 24 km/hr respectively. What is the average speed of walking?

### Solution

Given the speeds of 6 km/hr, 18 km/hr, 12 km/hr, and 24 km/hr for the same distance

Here, n is the number of speeds given, which is 4 in this case.

The speeds are X=6, Y=18, Z=12, and W=24. The least common multiple (LCM) of these speeds is 72.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Average Speed} &= \frac{nK}{\left(\frac{K}{X} + \frac{K}{Y} + \frac{K}{Z} + \frac{K}{W}\right)} \\ &= \frac{4 \times 72}{\left(\frac{72}{6} + \frac{72}{18} + \frac{72}{12} + \frac{72}{24}\right)} \\ &= \frac{288}{(12+4+6+3)} = \frac{288}{25} = 11.52 \text{ km/hr} \end{aligned}$$

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
A train travels at a speed of 60 km/h without any interruptions. However, due to periodic stops, the average speed of the journey decreases to 50 km/h. How many total minutes per hour does the train stop?

### Solution

Because the speed is reduced from 60 km/hr to 50 km/hr, it means that the speed is reduced by 10 km/hr.

Therefore, we can say that the train stops for the amount of time it would normally take to travel 10 km at its original speed of 60km/hr. So, the stoppage time is calculated as

$$\text{follows: } \frac{10}{60} = \frac{1}{6} \text{ hr per hour}$$

$$\Rightarrow 60 \times \frac{1}{6} = 10 \text{ minutes per hour}$$

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A train moves at an average speed of $100\mathrm{km / h}$ , stopping for 5 minutes after every $80\mathrm{km}$ . What is the total time taken by the train to cover a distance of $800\mathrm{km}$ ?

### Solution

Travel Time: The train is moving at an average speed of 100

$\mathrm{km / h}$ . So, to cover a distance of $800\mathrm{km}$ , it would take: $\mathrm{T}_{1} = \frac{800km}{100km / hr} = 8$ hours.

Stoppage Time: The train stops for 5 minutes after every 80

km. So, for a distance of $800\mathrm{km}$ , it would make $\left(\frac{800}{80} - 1\right) = 9$ stops.

Since each stop is 5 minutes long, the total stoppage time would be $\mathrm{T}_2 = 9$ stops $\times 5$ min/stop $= 45$ minutes.

Therefore, the total time taken by the train to cover a distance of $800\mathrm{km}$ , including stoppages, $\mathrm{T}_1 + \mathrm{T}_2 = 8$ hours and 45 minutes

readingSections.title: Ratio Method
readingSections.content:
The concept of ratio can generally be applied to problems involving time and distance, provided that one of the three variables - time, distance, or speed - remains constant in two cases.

Case 1: If time is constant Speed is proportional to Distance $(\mathrm{S} \propto \mathrm{D})$ . So, the ratio of $\mathrm{S}_1$ to $\mathrm{S}_2$ equals the ratio of $\mathrm{D}_1$ to $\mathrm{D}_2$ . So, $\mathrm{S}_1: \mathrm{S}_2 = \mathrm{D}_1: \mathrm{D}_2$

Case 2: If speed is constant Distance is proportional to Time $(\mathrm{D} \propto \mathrm{T})$ . So, the ratio of $\mathrm{D}_1$ to $\mathrm{D}_2$ equals the ratio of $\mathrm{T}_1$ to $\mathrm{T}_2$ . So, $\mathrm{D}_1: \mathrm{D}_2 = \mathrm{T}_1: \mathrm{T}_2$

Case 3: If distance is constant Speed is inversely proportional to Time $(\mathrm{S} \propto 1 / \mathrm{T})$ . So, the ratio of $\mathrm{S}_1$ to $\mathrm{S}_2$ equals the inverse ratio of $\mathrm{T}_1$ to $\mathrm{T}_2$

$$
\mathrm {S o}, \mathrm {S} _ {1}: \mathrm {S} _ {2} = \mathrm {T} _ {2}: \mathrm {T} _ {1}
$$

On his way back, he meets cyclist A at point R. Determine the distance from point P to point R?

According to question:

11 unit $= 66\mathrm{km}$

1 unit $= 6\mathrm{km}$

Distance from P to R is traveled by A so Distance $= 5$ unit $= 5 \times 6 = 30$ km

readingSections.title: When Given Time Difference Or Total Time For Two Different Speeds Covering The Same Distance
readingSections.content:
For the first formula, it calculates the distance (D) based on the difference in time $(\mathrm{T_d})$ and the speeds $(\mathrm{S_1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_2)$ . The formula is:

$$
D = \frac {S _ {1} \times S _ {2}}{S _ {1} \sim S _ {2}} \times T _ {d}
$$

The second formula calculates the distance (D) based on the total time $(\mathrm{T_t})$ and the speeds $(\mathrm{S_1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_2)$ . The formula is:

$$
D = \frac {S _ {1} \times S _ {2}}{S _ {1} + S _ {2}} \times T _ {t}
$$

If someone is early or late on two different occasions, then the total time difference will be the difference between the early and late times. For example, if Amit reaches the office 10 minutes early on the first day and 6 minutes early on the second day, then the total time difference is $10 - 6 = 4$ minutes.

158

If someone is late on the first occasion and early on the second, then the total time difference will be the sum of the late and early times. For example, if Amit reaches the office 10 minutes early on the first day and is 6 minutes late on the second day, then the total time difference is 10 + 6 = 16 minutes.

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
A woman travels from her home to her workplace at a speed of 45 km/h and arrives 15 minutes late. If she travels at a speed of 60 km/h, she arrives 5 minutes early. What is the distance from her home to her workplace?

### Solution

The total time difference (Td) is the sum of the late and early times, which is 15 minutes (late) + 5 minutes (early) = 20 minutes.

While, as the speeds are in km/h, we need to convert this time difference into hours. So, Td = 20/60 hr

$$D = \frac{S_1 \times S_2}{S_1 - S_2} \times T_d$$
$$= \frac{45 \times 60}{60 - 45} \times \frac{20}{60} = 60 \text{ km}$$

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
A girl traveled a certain distance by scooter from her home to her office at a speed of 35 km/h and walked back at the speed of 5 km/h. If the entire journey took 6 hours and 24 minutes, what was the distance from her home to her office?

### Solution

S1 is the speed of the scooter (35 km/h),

S2 is the walking speed (5 km/h), and

Tt is the total time (6 hours and 24 minutes = 6.4 hours).

$$D = \frac{S_1 \times S_2}{S_1 + S_2} \times T_t = \frac{35 \times 5}{35 + 5} \times 6.4 = 28 \text{ km}$$

readingSections.title: Race-Based
readingSections.content:
Case 1: If the gap between two members in a race is Dg, and the speeds of the two members are S1 and S2 respectively, then to find the time taken to cover the gap, we need to use the difference of speeds, Sd = S1 - S2. So,

$$\text{Time Taken} = \frac{\text{Distance of gapping}}{\text{Difference of speed}}$$
$$T = \frac{D_g}{S_d}$$

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
A thief spots a policeman at a distance of 200 meters. The thief immediately starts running at a speed of 15 km/h. At

the same time, the policeman starts chasing him at a speed of 18 km/h. How long will it take for the policeman to catch the thief?

### Solution

The gap between the thief and the policeman is 200 meters, Which is Dg = 200 meters.

The difference of speeds, Sd = S2 - S1 = 18 - 15 = 3 km /hr

$$= 3 \times \frac{5}{18} \text{ m/sec} = \frac{5}{6} \text{ m/sec}$$

Substituting these values in the formula

$$T = \frac{D_g}{S_d} = \frac{200}{\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)} = 240 \text{ seconds or } 4 \text{ minutes}$$

Case 2: If the term "hop" or "Leaps" is used in a question, then the product of the number of hops per unit time and the length per hop will give the distance. For example, if a cat cover 2 feet in one hop and runs 25 hops in a minute, then the speed of the cat is calculated as 2 × 25=50 feet/minute.

readingSections.title: Example 16
readingSections.content:
A dog spots a cat and estimates that the cat is 40 hops away. The cat sees the dog and starts running, with the dog not far behind. If in every minute the dog makes 4 hops and the cat makes 5 hops, and one hop of the dog is equal to 2 hops of the cat, how long will it take for the dog to catch up with the cat?

### Solution

One hop of the dog is equal to 2 hops of the cat. So, the ratio of the distance covered per hop by the dog and cat is 2:1.

When the dog spots the cat, the distance between them is equal to 40 hops of the dog.

Given that each hop of the dog covers a distance of 2 units, the total distance between the cat and dog is 40 × 2 = 80 units.

The speed of the dog, S1 = 4 × 2 = 8 units/min. The speed of the cat, S2 = 5 × 1 = 5 units/min.

The difference in their speeds, Sd, is S1 - S2 = 8 - 5 = 3 units/min.

Therefore, the time it takes for the dog to reach the cat,

$$T = \frac{D_g}{S_d} = \frac{80}{3} = 26.66 \text{ minutes}$$
$$= 26 \text{ minutes and } 40 \text{ seconds}$$

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
In a circular race of 2000 meters, A and B start running simultaneously with speeds of 30 km/h and 50 km/h from the same point and at the same time. After how much time will they meet at the starting point for the first time if their direction is the same?

### Solution

$$\text{Speed of A} = 30 \times \frac{5}{18} = 8.33 \text{ m/sec}$$

$$\text{Speed of B} = 50 \times \frac{5}{18} = 13.88 \text{ m/sec}$$

$$\text{Time taken by A to complete a round} = \frac{2000}{8.33} = 240 \text{ sec}$$

$$\text{Time taken by B to complete a round} = \frac{2000}{13.88} = 144 \text{ sec}$$

The least common multiple (LCM) of 240 and 144 is 720 sec

So, they will meet for the first time after 720 seconds or 12 minutes.

readingSections.title: Example 19
readingSections.content:
A train travels a distance of 50 km at a constant speed. Due to a mechanical issue, the train's speed decreases to 4/5 of its original speed and it reaches its destination 55 minutes late. If the mechanical issue had occurred after the train had traveled an additional 40 km, it would have arrived 40 minutes late. What is the total distance the train had to travel?

### Solution

The train's speed decreased to $\frac{4}{5}$ of its usual speed, causing it to arrive 55 minutes late. Therefore, the usual time from the point where the issue occurred is calculated as $\frac{55}{(5-4)} \times 4 = 220$ minutes.

If the incident had happened after the train had traveled an additional 40 km, it would have arrived 40 minutes late. So, from that point, the original time taken by the train is calculated as $\frac{40}{(5-4)} \times 4 = 160$ minutes.

This means that the train traveled 40 km in 220 - 160 = 60 minutes, which is equivalent to 1 hour.

Therefore, the speed of the train is $\frac{40}{1} = 40$ km/hr.

Knowing that the issue occurred after the train had traveled 50 km,

We can calculate the distance after 50 km as the speed of the train multiplied by the time taken from that point: $40 \times \frac{220}{60} =$ approximately 146.67 km.

So, the total distance traveled by the train is $50 + 146.67 =$ approximately 196.67 km.

readingSections.title: Example 20
readingSections.content:
Buses start from a bus terminal at the speed of 36 km/h at an Interval of 10 min. A man coming towards a Bus terminal meets the Buses at intervals of 8 min what is the speed of that man?

### Solution

The speed of the bus is 36 km/hr, and we'll denote the speed of the man as X.

The man travels for 8 minutes.

The same distance that the person traveled is covered by the bus in (10-8) = 2 minutes.

Since the distance is equal, we can set up the equation:

Speed of bus × Time taken by bus = Speed of man × Time taken by man.

This gives us $36 \times 2 = X \times 8$

Solving for X, we find that X = 9 km/hr.

19. A car travels a distance of 60 km at a uniform speed. If the speed of the car is 23 km/hr more, it takes 1 hour and 9 minutes less to cover the same distance. What was the original speed?
(a) 25 km/hr (b) 48 km/hr
(c) 21 km/hr (d) 32 km/hr
20. A man covers a certain distance by car. If he covers the distance at 2 km/h more speed, he takes 4 hr less, and if he covers at 2 km/h slower speed, he takes 8 hr more. What is the distance?
(a) 16 km (b) 1.6 km
(c) 48 km (d) 96 km
21. In covering a certain distance, the speeds of A and B are in the ratio of 5:11. A takes 24 minutes more than B to reach the destination. How much time does A take to reach the destination?
(a) 44 min (b) 20 min
(c) 24 min (d) 32 min
22. After covering a distance with a uniform speed, there is some defect in the train engine, and therefore its speed reduces to 8/11 of its original speed. The train reaches its destination 42 min late. Had it happened after 32 km more, the train would have reached 24 min late. What is the actual speed of the train?
(a) 45 km/hr (b) 40 km/hr
(c) 12 km/hr (d) 32 km/hr
23. Buses start from a bus terminal at the speed of 63 km/hr at intervals of 56 min. A man coming towards the bus terminal meets the buses at intervals of 49 min. What is the speed of the man?
(a) 15 km/hr (b) 9 km/hr
(c) 12 km/hr (d) 18 km/hr
24. Buses start from a bus terminal after every 12 min. A man going away from the bus terminal meets the buses after every 15 min. If the speed of the man is 30 km/hr, what is the speed of the buses?
(a) 145 km/hr (b) 190 km/hr
(c) 150 km/hr (d) 162 km/hr
25. Bullets are fired from a firing point at intervals of 24 min. A man coming towards the firing point in a car hears the sound of bullets at intervals of 22 min. If the speed of sound is 330 m/sec, what is the speed of the car?
(a) 33 m/sec (b) 30 m/sec
(c) 27 m/sec (d) 31 m/sec
26. Every day, Laxmi's husband meets her at the bus stand at 4:40 PM and drives her to their residence. One day, she left the office early and reached the bus stand at 4:20 PM. She started walking towards home and met her husband coming from the residence on the way. They reached home 12 minutes earlier than usual. For how long did she walk?
(a) 20 min (b) 18 min
(c) 16 min (d) 14 min
27. A thief saw a policeman at a distance of 25 meters and started running at a speed of 8 m/sec. At the same time, the policeman started to chase him at a speed of 9 m/sec. At what time will the policeman catch the thief?
(a) 25 min (b) 5/12 min
(c) 2.4 min (d) 0.4 min
28. A thief stole a car at 3 AM and drove at 45 km/hr. The theft was discovered at 4 AM and the owner of the car chased him in another car at a speed of 48 km/hr. At what time will the owner catch the thief?
(a) 7:00 AM (b) 5:00 AM
(c) 7:00 PM (d) 5:00 PM
29. Two trains started from Lucknow to Noida at 3:12 AM and 4:42 AM at speeds of 75 km/hr and 90 km/hr respectively. At what time will train B cross train A?
(a) 12:12 AM (b) 12:12 PM
(c) 10:42 AM (d) 10:42 PM
30. A dog chases a rabbit and takes 5.5 leaps for every 6 leaps of the rabbit, but 8 leaps of the dog are equal to 12 leaps of the rabbit. Compare the speed of the dog and the rabbit.
(a) 11:8 (b) 8:11
(c) 2:3 (d) 3:2
31. A dog chases a rabbit. It estimates that the rabbit is 90 leaps ahead of the dog's jump. The rabbit can jump 9 times in the time the dog can jump 5 times.

The distance covered by the rabbit and the dog in one jump is 3 feet and 6 feet respectively. In how many jumps will the dog catch the rabbit?

(a) 600 (b) 750
(c) 900 (d) 1080

32. Two trains start at the same time between Gonda and Basti and proceed towards each other at rates of 41 km/hr and 47.5 km/hr respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has traveled 26 km more than the other. What is the distance between the two stations?

(a) 333 km (b) 365 km
(c) 354 km (d) 355.5 km

33. In a flight of 800 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 80 km/h the time of flight increased by 30 min, the original time duration of the flight is-

(a) 1 hour (b) 2 hours

(c) 2.5 hours (d) 4 hours

34. A car crosses a man walking at 6 km/hr. the man can see the things upto 450 m. only in one direction due to fog. He observes the car moving in the same direction for a duration of 4.5 minutes. Find the speed of the car.

(a) 9 km/hr (b) 12 km/hr
(c) 18 km/hr (d) 20 km/hr

35. Pramod takes 4 hours 40 minutes in going to some place on foot and returns on a vehicle. Had he travelled both the sides on foot, he would have taken 2 hours more. How much time will he take in travelling both sides on a vehicle?

(a) 2 hours 10 minutes
(b) 2 hours 30 minutes
(c) 2 hours
(d) 2 hours 40 minutes

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
TRAINS

Problem based on trains are very close to the problems related to 'Time, Speed and Distance' and some of the concepts of 'Time, Speed and Distance' are also applicable to these problems. The only difference is that the length of the moving object (train) is taken into consideration in these types of problems.

readingSections.title: Concept 1
readingSections.content:
$$\text{Speed of train } (T_t) = \frac{\text{Distance covered (d)}}{\text{Time taken (t)}} \text{ or } S = \frac{D}{t}$$

Here, unit of speed is m/s or km/h.

$$(i) \text{ p km/hr} = \left( \text{p} \times \frac{5}{18} \right) \text{ m/s}$$

$$(ii) \text{ p m/s} = \left( \text{p} \times \frac{18}{5} \right) \text{ km/hr}$$

Objects whose length taken Zero = Pole, Tree, Man, Car, Post box, etc...

Objects whose length was never considered Zero = Train, Platform, Tunnel, Bridge, Post office etc...

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Convert 180 km/hr into m/s.

### Solution

According to the formula,

$$1 \text{ km/hr} = \frac{5}{18} \text{ m/s}$$

$$180 \text{ km/hr} = \frac{5}{18} \times 180 = 50 \text{ m/s}$$

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
Convert 75 m/s into km/hr.

### Solution

According to the formula,

$$1 \text{ m/s} = \frac{18}{5} \text{ km/hr}$$

$$75 \text{ m/s} = \frac{18}{5} \times 75 = 270 \text{ km/hr}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content: The distance covered by a train in passing a pole or a standing man or a signal post or any other object (of negligible length) is equal to the length of the train.

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
A train covers 165 m in passing a signal post. What is the length of the train?

### Solution

We know that the distance covered by a train in passing a pole or a standing man or a signal post or any other object (of negligible length) is equal to the length of the train. So, in this case, train covers 165 m to pass a signal post.

∴ Length of the train = 165 m

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content: If a train passes a stationary object (bridge, platform etc.) having some length, then the distance covered by train is equal to the sum of the length of train and that particular stationary object which it is passing

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
A 129 long train passes a platform which is 150 m long. What is the distance that the train travels while it crosses the platform?

### Solution

We know that when a train passes a stationary object having some length, then the distance covered by train is equal to the sum of the length of the train and that particular stationary object. In this case, stationary object is 100 m long platform.

Required distance = Length of train + Length of platform =  $(129 + 150) \text{ m} = 279 \text{ m}$

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content: If two trains are moving in opposite directions, then their relative speed is equal to the sum of the speeds of both the trains.

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
Two trains are moving in opposite directions with speeds of 16 m/s and 9 m/s, respectively. Find their relative speed.

### Solution

Given, speed of first train = 16 m/s and speed of second train = 9 m/s

We know that when two trains are moving in opposite directions, then their relative speed = Sum of speeds of both the trains

Required relative speed of trains

$$= (16 + 9) \text{ m/s} = 25 \text{ m/s}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content: If two trains are moving in same directions, then their relative speed is equal to the difference of the speeds of both the trains.

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Two trains are moving in same direction with speeds of 119 km/hr and 99 km/hr, respectively. What will be the relative speed of the train running at 119 km/hr in respect of the train running at 99 km/hr?

### Solution

Given, speed of first train = 119 km/hr and speed of second train = 99 km/hr

We know that when two trains are moving in same direction, then their relative speed = Difference of speeds of both the trains

Required relative speed of trains = $(119 - 99) \text{ km/hr} = 20 \text{ km/hr}$

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content: If two trains of lengths 'm' and 'n' are moving in opposite directions with speeds of 'x' and 'y' respectively, then time taken by the trains to cross each other is equal to $\frac{(m+n)}{(x+y)}$

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Two trains of length 250 m and 350 m are moving in opposite directions at 20 m/s and 30 m/s, respectively. Determine the duration required for the trains to cross one another.

### Solution

Here, $m = 250 \text{ m}$, $n = 350 \text{ m}$, $x = 20 \text{ m/s}$ and $y = 30 \text{ m/s}$

Both trains are moving in opposite directions.

According to the formula,

$$\text{Required time} = \frac{(m+n)}{(x+y)} = \frac{(250+350)}{(20+30)} = \frac{600}{50} = 12 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 7
readingSections.content:
If two trains of lengths 'm' and 'n' are moving in same directions with speeds of 'x' and 'y' respectively, then time

taken by the faster train to cross the slower train is equal to $\frac{(m+n)}{(x-y)}$

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Two trains of length 250 m and 350 m are moving in same directions at 30 m/s and 20 m/s, respectively. Determine the duration needed by the speedier train to overtake the slower one.

### Solution

Here, $m = 250 \text{ m}$, $n = 350 \text{ m}$, $x = 30 \text{ m/s}$ and $y = 20 \text{ m/s}$

Both trains are moving in same directions.

According to the formula,

$$\text{Required time} = \frac{(m+n)}{(x-y)} = \frac{(250+350)}{(30-20)} = \frac{600}{10} = 60 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
A train passes a standing man in 12 s and 240 m long platform in 32 s. Find the length and the speed of the train.

### Solution

### Method 1

Let length of the train be L m.

If the speed of the train remains same while crossing a standing man and platform.

Then, according to the question,

$$\frac{L}{12} = \frac{L+240}{32}$$

$$8L = 3L + 720 \Rightarrow 5L = 720 \Rightarrow L = \frac{720}{5} = 144 \text{ m}$$

$$\text{Speed of the train} = \frac{\text{Length of the train}}{\text{Time taken}} = \frac{144}{12} = 12 \text{ m/s}$$

### Method 2

Difference between the distance covered by train in passing the man and the train = length of platform = 240m

Difference between the time taken by train to cross the man and the platform = $32 - 12 = 20 \text{ s}$.

$$\text{Speed of train} = \frac{240}{20} = 12 \text{ m/s}$$

Length of train = Speed of train × Time taken to cross pole = $12 \text{ m/s} \times 12 \text{ s} = 144 \text{ m}$

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A 375 m long train is running at 196 km/hr. In what time, will it pass a man running at 16 km/hr in the same direction in which the train is moving?

### Solution

Given, length of the train = 375 m

Speed of the train = 196 kmph

and speed of the man = 16 kmph since, train and man are moving in same direction.

Speed of the train relative to man = Speed of the train – Speed of man

$$= 196 - 16 = 180 \text{ kmph} = 180 \times \frac{5}{18} = 50 \text{ m/s}$$

Time taken = Distance covered in passing the man ÷ Relative speed of the train

$$= \frac{375}{50} = 7.5 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
A 440 m long train is running at 125 km/hr. In what time, will it pass a man running in the direction opposite to that of the train at 19 km/hr?

### Solution

Given, length of the train = 440 m

Speed of the train = 125 kmph

and speed of the man = 19 kmph

since, train and man are moving in opposite direction.

Speed of the train relative to man = Speed of the train ÷ Speed of man

$$= 125 + 19 = 144 \text{ kmph} = 144 \times \frac{5}{18} = 40 \text{ m/s}$$

Time taken = Distance covered in passing the man ÷ Relative speed of the train

$$= \frac{440}{40} = 11 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 8
readingSections.content:
If a train of length 'L' m passes a platform of 'x' m in 'T' seconds, then time taken by the same train to pass a platform of length 'y' m is given as

$$T_2 = \left( \frac{L+y}{L+x} \right) T_1$$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
A train of length 250 m, passes a platform of 350 m length in 40 seconds. What time will this train take to pass the platform of 200 m length?

### Solution

Given, length of the train = 250 m;

length of platform = 350 m

and time taken to cover the distance = 40 s

So, to cross the platform, the train has to cover a distance = Length of train + Length of platform = 250 + 350 = 600 m

$$\text{Speed of the train} = \frac{\text{Distance covered}}{\text{Time taken}} = \frac{600}{40} = 15 \text{ m/s}$$

Now, the time taken to cross the platform of length 200 m

$$= \frac{\text{Total Distance covered}}{\text{Speed of Train}}$$

$$= \frac{\text{Length of train} + \text{Length of platform}}{\text{Speed of Train}}$$

$$= \frac{250 + 200}{15}$$

$$= 30 \text{ s}$$

According to the formula,

Here, L = 250 m, x = 350 m, T$_{1}$ = 50 s, y = 200 m and T$_{2}$ = ?

$$\text{Required time} = \left( \frac{250 + 200}{250 + 350} \right) \times 40 = 30 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 9
readingSections.content:
From stations A and B, two trains start moving towards each other with the speeds of 'x' and 'y', respectively. When they meet each other, it is found that one train covers the distance 'D' km more than that of another train. In such cases, distance between stations A and B is given as

$$\left( \frac{x+y}{x-y} \right) \times D \text{ km}$$

readingSections.title: Example 13
readingSections.content:
From stations Mathura and Ayodhya, two trains moving towards each other with the speeds of 150 km/hr and 130 km/hr, respectively. When the two trains meet each other, it is observed that one train travels an additional 20 km compared to the other. Find the distance between stations Mathura and Ayodhya.

### Solution

### Method 1

Let the trains meet after time 't' at a distance x from station B.

Then, another train coming from station Mathura covers a distance of (x + 20).

For station Mathura, distance covered by first train (x + 20) = 150t

$$x = 150t - 20 \quad \dots \quad (i)$$

For station Ayodhya, distance covered by second train,

$$x = 130t \quad \dots \quad (ii)$$

From eq. (i) and (ii), we get

$$130t = 150t - 20$$

$t = 1$ hour

Distance between stations Mathura and Ayodhya $= 150t + 130t = 280t = 280 \times 1 = 280\mathrm{km}$

According to the formula,

Here, $x = 150 \, \text{km/hr}$ , $y = 130 \, \text{km/hr}$ and $D = 20 \, \text{km}$

Distance between stations Mathura and Ayodhya

$$
= \left(\frac {1 5 0 + 1 3 0}{1 5 0 - 1 3 0}\right) \times 2 0 = \frac {2 8 0}{2 0} \times 2 0 = 2 8 0 \mathrm {k m}
$$

### Method 2

Time taken to meet the trains

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \frac {\text {d i f f e r e n c e b e t w e e n d i s t a n c e c o v e r e d}}{\text {d i f f e r e n c e b e t w e e n t h e i r s p e e d}} \\ = \frac {2 0}{1 5 0 - 1 3 0} = \frac {2 0}{2 0} = 1 \mathrm {h r s} \\ \end{array}
$$

Distance between Mathura and Ayodhya $=$ Relative speed $\times$ time taken to meet

$$
= (1 5 0 + 1 3 0) \times 1 = 2 8 0 \mathrm {k m}
$$

readingSections.title: Concept 10
readingSections.content:
If two trains leave A for B at time $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ and travel with speeds 'x' and 'y' respectively, then the distance 'd' from A, where the two trains meet, is given as

$$
d = \text {D i f f e r e n c e i n t i m e} \times \frac {\text {P r o d u c t o f s p e e d s}}{\text {D i f f e r e n c e i n s p e e d s}}
$$

$$
d = \left(T _ {1} - T _ {2}\right) \times \left(\frac {x \times y}{x - y}\right)
$$

readingSections.title: Example 14
readingSections.content:
Two train leave Lucknow for Delhi at 5:00 am and 5:30 am, respectively and travel at $120\mathrm{km / hr}$ and $150~\mathrm{km / hr}$ , respectively. Calculate the distance from Lucknow at which the two trains will meet.

### Solution

Speed of $1^{\mathrm{st}}$ train $= 120\mathrm{km / hr}$ and speed of $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ train $= 150\mathrm{km / hr}$

Relative speed of $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ train $= (150 - 120)\mathrm{km / hr} = 30\mathrm{km / hr}$

As $1^{\mathrm{st}}$ train leaves $(1/2)$ hour before, hence in $(1/2)$ hour, it will cover $60\mathrm{km}$ as it moves $120\mathrm{km}$ in 1 hour.

Time taken by $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ train to gain $60\mathrm{km} = \frac{60}{30} = 2$ hours

Actual distance covered by $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ train in 2 hours $= 2 \times 150 = 300\mathrm{km}$

According to the formula,

Here, $x = 120 \, \text{km/hr}$ , $y = 150 \, \text{km/hr}$ , $t_1 = 5:00 \, \text{am}$ and $t_2 = 5:30 \, \text{am}$

Required distance

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \left(T _ {1} - T _ {2}\right) \times \left(\frac {x \times y}{x - y}\right) = (5: 0 0 - 5: 3 0) \times \left(\frac {1 2 0 \times 1 5 0}{1 2 0 - 1 5 0}\right) \\ = \frac {1}{2} \times \left(\frac {1 2 0 \times 1 5 0}{3 0}\right) \\ = 3 0 0 \mathrm {k m} \\ \end{array}
$$

readingSections.title: Concept 11
readingSections.content:
If a train overtakes two persons who are walking with speeds of 'x' and 'y' respectively, in the same direction and passes the two persons completely in $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ time, respectively, then

$$
\text {L e n g t h o f t r a i n} = \frac {\text {D i f f e r e n c e i n s p e e d s} \times \mathrm {T} _ {1} \times \mathrm {T} _ {2}}{\left(\mathrm {T} _ {1} - \mathrm {T} _ {2}\right)}
$$

readingSections.title: Example 15
readingSections.content:
A train overtakes two persons who are walking at the rate of 2 km/hr and 4 km/hr in the same direction and passes completely in 18 and 20 seconds, respectively. Find the length of the train.

### Solution

### Method 1

Let speed of the train be $\mathrm{xm / s}$

Relative speed of train w.r.t first man $= (x - \frac{5}{9})\mathrm{m / s}$

Relative speed of train w.r.t. second man $= (x - \frac{10}{9})\mathrm{m / s}$

According to question,

Length of the train for $1^{\mathrm{st}}$ man = Length of the train for $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ man

$$
(x - \frac {5}{9}) \times 1 8 = (x - \frac {1 0}{9}) \times 2 0
$$

$$
8 1 x - 4 5 = 9 0 x - 1 0 0
$$

$$
9 x = 5 5
$$

$$
x = 5 5 / 9
$$

Length of the train $= \left(\frac{55}{9} -\frac{5}{9}\right)\times 18 = 100\mathrm{m}$

According to the formula,

Here, $\mathrm{T}_{1} = 18\mathrm{s}$ , $\mathrm{T}_{2} = 20\mathrm{s}$ , $\mathrm{x} = 2\mathrm{km / hr} = 2\times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{10}{18} = \frac{5}{9}$

and $y = 4 \, \text{km/hr} = 4 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{20}{18} = \frac{10}{9}$

Required Distance

$$
= \frac {\left(\frac {1 0}{9} - \frac {5}{9}\right) \times 1 8 \times 2 0}{(2 0 - 1 8)} = \frac {5}{9} \times 1 8 \times 2 0 \times \frac {1}{2} = 1 0 0 \mathrm {m}
$$

168

### Method 2

$$\left( \frac{\text{speed of } 1^{\text{st}} \text{ man} \times \text{Time taken by } 1^{\text{st}} \text{ man} - \text{speed of } 2^{\text{nd}} \text{ person} \times \text{Time taken by } 2^{\text{nd}} \text{ man}}{\text{difference between their time}} \right)$$

$$= \frac{18 \times 2 - 20 \times 4}{18 - 20} = \frac{36 - 80}{(-2)} = \left( \frac{-44}{-2} \right) = 22 \text{ km/h}$$

Length of train =  $(22 - 4) \times \frac{5}{18} \times 20 = 100 \text{ m}$

readingSections.title: Concept 12
readingSections.content:
If two trains P and Q start from stations/points A and B towards B and A, respectively and after passing each other, they take  $T_1$  and  $T_2$  time to reach B and A, respectively and speed of train P is given as  $x$  km/hr, then

Speed of train  $Q = x \sqrt{\frac{T_1}{T_2}}$

readingSections.title: Example 16
readingSections.content:
Two trains A and B start from Secundarabad and Mumbai towards Mumbai and Secundarabad, respectively. After passing each other, they take 12 hours 30 minutes and 8 hours to reach Mumbai and Secundarabad, respectively. If the train from Secundarabad is moving at 60 km/hr, then find the speed of the other train.

### Solution

According to the formula,

Here,  $T_1 = 12$  hours 30 minutes =  $12 + \frac{30}{60} = \frac{25}{2}$  hour and  $T_2 = 8$  hours

Speed of train  $B = 60 \times \sqrt{\frac{25}{2 \times 8}} = 60 \times \frac{5}{4} = 75$  kmph

readingSections.title: Concept 13
readingSections.content:
The distance between two stations A and B is  $D$  km. A train with  $x$  km/hr starts from station A towards B and after a difference of 't' hours another train with  $y$  km/hr starts from station B towards A, then both the trains will meet at a certain point after time 'T' hours. Then,

$$T = \left( \frac{D \pm ty}{x + y} \right)$$

If second train starts after the first train, then 't' is taken as positive.

If second train starts before the first train, then 't' is taken as negative.

readingSections.title: Example 17
readingSections.content:
The distance between two stations Patna and Haridwar is 1200 km. A train with speed of 120 km/hr leaves Patna

station at 8: 00 am towards station Haridwar. Another train with speed of 150 km/hr leaves station Haridwar at 9: 00 am towards station Patna. Then, at what time both trains meet?

### Solution

First train leaves at 8: 00 am and second at 9: 00 am.

So, first train i.e. from Patna to Haridwar has travelled 1 hour more.

Distance covered by first train in 1 hour =  $120 \times 1 = 120$  km  
[Distance = Speed  $\times$  Time]

So, distance, left between the station =  $1200 - 120 = 1080$  km

Now, trains are travelling in opposite directions.

So, relative speed =  $(120 + 150) = 270$  km/hr

Time taken to cover 1080 km

$$= \frac{\text{Distance Travelled}}{\text{Relative Speed}} = \frac{1080}{270} = 4 \text{ hours}$$

The time, at which the two trains will meet =  $09: 00 + 4$  hours = 1: 00 pm

According to the formula,

Here,  $D = 1200$  km,  $t = 9: 00 - 8: 00 = 1$  hour,  $x = 120$  km/hr and  $y = 150$  km/hr

Time taken by trains to meet,

$$T = \left( \frac{D + ty}{x + y} \right) = \left( \frac{1200 + 1 \times 150}{120 + 150} \right) = \frac{1350}{270} = 5 \text{ hours}$$

The two trains will meet = 8: 00 am + 5 hours = 1: 00 pm

readingSections.title: Concept 14
readingSections.content:
The distance between two stations A and B is  $D$  km. A train starts from A towards B and another train starts from B towards A at the same time and they meet at a certain point after 'T' hours. If train starting from A travels with a speed of  $x$  km/hr slower or faster than another train, then

(i) Speed of faster train =  $\left( \frac{D + Tx}{2T} \right)$  km/hr

(ii) Speed of slower train =  $\left( \frac{D - Tx}{2T} \right)$  km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 18
readingSections.content:
The distance between two stations Ghaziabad and Mussorie is 615 km. A train starts from Ghaziabad to Mussorie and another from Mussorie to Ghaziabad at the same time and they meet after 3 hours. The train travelling from Ghaziabad to Mussorie is slower by 7 km/hr compared to other train from Mussorie to Ghaziabad, then find the speed of both the trains.

### Solution

### Method 1

Let speed of slower train be x km/hr.

Then, speed of faster train = (x + 7) km/hr

As the trains are moving in opposite directions.

So, relative speed = x + (x + 7) = (2x + 7) km/hr

Time taken = Distance Travelled / Relative Speed

$$3 = \frac{615}{2x + 7}$$

$$2x + 7 = 205$$

$$x = 99 \text{ km/hr}$$

Hence, speed of slower train is 99 km/hr and speed of faster train is 106 km/hr

According to the formula,

Here, D = 615 km, T = 3 hours, x = 7 km/hr

(i) Speed of faster train

$$= \left(\frac{615 + 3 \times 7}{2 \times 3}\right) = \frac{615 + 21}{6} = \frac{636}{6} = 106 \text{ km/hr}$$

(ii) Speed of slower train

$$= \left(\frac{615 - 3 \times 7}{2 \times 3}\right) = \frac{615 - 21}{6} = \frac{594}{6} = 99 \text{ km/hr}$$

### Method 2

Relative speed

$$= \frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}} = \frac{615}{3} = 205 \text{ km/h}$$

Sum of speed of both train = x + y = 205

Difference between speed of trains x - y = 7

Hence x = 212/2 = 106 km/h

$$y = \frac{198}{2} = 99 \text{ km/h}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 15
readingSections.content:
A train covers distance 'D' between two stations A and B in T₁ hrs. If the speed of train is reduced by 'x' km/hr, then the same distance will be covered in T₂ hrs.

(i) Distance between A and B, D = x (T₁T₂ / (T₂ - T₁)) km

(ii) Speed of the train = (xT₂ / (T₂ - T₁)) km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 19
readingSections.content:
A train covers distance between two stations Agra and Ahmedabad in 8 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 24 km/hr, then it travels the same distance in 12 hours. Calculate the distance between the two stations and speed of the train.

### Solution

### Method 1

Let the initial speed of train be x km/hr and distance between stations Agra and Ahmedabad = d km

According to the question,

Distance covered with initial speed = Distance covered with decreased speed

$$8x = 12(x - 24)$$

$$4x = 12 \times 24$$

$$x = 72 \text{ km/hr}$$

Initial speed of the train = 72 km/hr and distance between stations Agra and Ahmedabad = 8 × 72 = 576 km

According to the formula,

Here, T₁ = 8 hours, T₂ = 12 hours, x = 24 km/hr

(i) Distance between Agra and Ahmedabad,

$$D = 24 \times \left(\frac{8 \times 12}{12 - 8}\right) = 24 \times \frac{96}{4} = 576 \text{ km}$$

(ii) Speed of the train = (24 × 12 / 12 - 8) = (24 × 12 / 4) = 72 km/hr

### Method 2

If distance covered in 24 km/h in 12 hours is same as old speed covers in 4hrs

So, old speed = (24 × 12 / 4) = 72 km/h

Distance = speed × time = 72 × 8 = 576 km

readingSections.title: Concept 16
readingSections.content:
Without stoppages, a train travels at an average speed of 'x' and with stoppage, it covers the same distance at an average speed of 'y', then stoppage time per hour

$$= \frac{\text{Difference in average speeds}}{\text{Speed without stoppage}} = \frac{x - y}{x}; \quad \text{where } x > y$$

readingSections.title: Example 20
readingSections.content:
Without stoppage, the speed of a train is 90 km/hr and with stoppage, it is 75 km/hr. What is the number of minutes the train halts every hour?

### Solution

Decrease in speed due to stoppage = 90 - 75 = 15 km/hr

Because of stoppage, train covers 15 km less per hour.

170

Time taken to cover 15 km

$$= \frac{15}{90} = \frac{1}{6} \text{ hours} = \frac{1}{6} \times 60 = 10 \text{ minutes}$$

According to the formula,

Here, $x = 90 \text{ km/hr}$, $y = 75 \text{ km/hr}$

Required rest time

$$= \frac{x-y}{x} = \frac{90-75}{90} = \frac{15}{90} = \frac{1}{6} \text{ hours} = \frac{1}{6} \times 60 = 10 \text{ minutes}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 17
readingSections.content:
If two trains of equal lengths and different speeds take $T_1$ and $T_2$ time to cross a pole (or some object with negligible length), then time taken by them to cross each other is

$$T = \frac{2T_1T_2}{T_2 \pm T_1}$$

Here, (+) ve sign is being used, when trains are moving in opposite directions and

(–) ve sign is being used, when trains are moving in same directions.

readingSections.title: Example 21
readingSections.content:
Two trains of equal lengths take 10 s and 12 s, respectively to cross a pole. If the trains are traveling in the same direction, what is the duration required for one to overtake the other?

### Solution

Let the length of the train be x m.

Then, speed of first train = $\frac{x}{10} \text{ m/s}$

Similarly, speed of second train = $\frac{x}{12} \text{ m/s}$

Now, required time to cross each other, when the two trains are moving in same direction

$$= \frac{\text{Sum of lengths of two trains}}{\text{Relative speed of two trains}} = \frac{x+x}{\frac{x}{10} - \frac{x}{12}} = 120 \text{ s}$$

According to the formula,

Here, $T_1 = 10 \text{ s}$ and $T_2 = 12 \text{ s}$

$$\text{Required time} = \frac{2 \times 10 \times 12}{12 - 10} = 120 \text{ s}$$

readingSections.title: Example 22
readingSections.content:
After travelling 240 km, a train meets with an accident and

then proceeds at $\frac{3}{4}$ of its former speed and arrives at its destination 35 minutes late. Had the accident occurred 72 km further, it would have reached the destination only 25 minutes late. Find the speed of the train.

### Solution

Let the speed of the train be x km/hr.

According to the question,

Difference between the time when 24 km are travelled with $(3/4)^\text{th}$ of the speed and with usual speed = 10 minutes

$$\frac{72}{\frac{3x}{4}} - \frac{72}{x} = \frac{10}{60}$$

$$72 \times 6 = 3x$$

$$x = 144 \text{ km/hr.}$$

readingSections.title: Example 23
readingSections.content:
An express train and a goods train are running on the parallel tracks in the same direction. The driver of the goods train observes that the express train coming from behind, overtakes and crosses his train completely in 1 min whereas a man on the express train marks that he crosses the goods train in 2/3 minutes. If the speeds of the trains is in the ratio of 1 : 2, then find the ratio of their lengths.

### Solution

**Method 1:** Let the speeds of the two trains be x and 2x and length be $L_1$ and $L_2$, respectively.

**Case – 1:** When driver of goods train observes that passenger train crosses his train, then

$$\frac{L_1 + L_2}{2x - x} = 1 \text{ min} = 60 \text{ seconds} \quad \dots \quad (i)$$

**Case – 2:** When a man on express train observes that he crosses the goods train, then

$$\frac{L_1}{2x - x} = \frac{2}{3} \text{ min} = \frac{2}{3} \times 60 = 40 \text{ seconds} \quad \dots \quad (ii)$$

On dividing eq. (i) by eq. (ii), we get

$$\frac{L_1 + L_2}{L_1} = \frac{60}{40} \Rightarrow \frac{L_2}{L_1} + 1 = \frac{3}{2}$$

$$\frac{L_2}{L_1} = \frac{3}{2} - 1 = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow L_1 : L_2 = 2 : 1$$

**Method 2:** Express train passes goods train = 1 min = 60 s

Express train passes a man = $\frac{2}{3} \text{ min} = 20 \text{ s}$

Because speed is constant

So, Length of goods train : Length of express train = $(60 - 20) : 20 = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1$

BOAT
Boat and Stream
Boat and Stream is a topic in mathematics that deals with the
movement of a boat in a river.
Still water:
The water of a river or any other water body which is not
flowing is known as still water, under this circumstance the
water is considered to be stationary and the speed of the
water is zero.
Stream (or current):
It is the flowing water of a river which is moving at a certain
speed and represented as (s s ).
Speed of Boat:
When a boat moves with its own speed in still water, then this
speed of boat is called as speed of boat in still water (S B ).
Upstream:
When a boat or swimmer is navigating against the current,
it’s referred to as moving upstream i.e. against the flow of
water.
Downstream:
When a boat or a swimmer travels with the direction of the
stream, it is referred to as moving downstream i.e. along the
flow of water.
When the boat or a swimmer is moving along the flow of
water or with the flow of the water, the speed of the movement
(net speed) of the boat depends on the flow of the water [i.e.
speed of the water S s ]
(i) When boat or swimmer is moving in Upstream:
Speed of the boat or swimmer moving against the flow of
the water (i.e. moving in upstream)
