readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
BOAT AND STREAM

Boat and Stream is a topic in mathematics that deals with the movement of a boat in a river.

readingSections.title: Still water
readingSections.content: The water of a river or any other water body which is not flowing is known as still water, under this circumstance the water is considered to be stationary and the speed of the water is zero.

readingSections.title: Stream (or current)
readingSections.content: It is the flowing water of a river which is moving at a certain speed and represented as ($s_s$).

readingSections.title: Speed of Boat
readingSections.content: When a boat moves with its own speed in still water, then this speed of boat is called as speed of boat in still water ($S_B$).

readingSections.title: Upstream
readingSections.content: When a boat or swimmer is navigating against the current, it's referred to as moving upstream i.e. against the flow of water.

readingSections.title: Downstream
readingSections.content:
When a boat or a swimmer travels with the direction of the stream, it is referred to as moving downstream i.e. along the flow of water.

When the boat or a swimmer is moving along the flow of water or with the flow of the water, the speed of the movement (net speed) of the boat depends on the flow of the water [i.e. speed of the water $S_s$]

readingSections.title: (i) When boat or swimmer is moving in Upstream
readingSections.content:
Speed of the boat or swimmer moving against the flow of the water (i.e. moving in upstream)

= Speed of boat in still water – Speed of stream

$$= S_B - S_s$$

readingSections.title: (ii) When boat or swimmer is moving in Downstream
readingSections.content:
Speed of the boat or swimmer moving with the flow of the water (i.e. moving in downstream)

= Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

$$= S_B + S_s$$

Based on above, we can deduce the formulae for the following:

Speed of the boat

$$= \frac{\text{Downstream Speed} + \text{Upstream Speed}}{2}$$

Speed of the stream

$$= \frac{\text{Downstream Speed} - \text{Upstream Speed}}{2}$$

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
The speed of a boat is 10 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 2 km/hr. Find the downstream and upstream speed.

### Solution

Downstream speed = $S_B + S_s = 10 + 2 = 12$ km/hr

Upstream speed = $S_B - S_s = 10 - 2 = 8$ km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
A boatman can row a boat 1 km in 10 minutes along the direction of the stream and 4 km in 1 hour against the direction of the stream. Find the speed of the boat that the boatman can row in still water and the speed of the stream.

### Solution

Downstream speed = $\frac{1}{10} \times 60 = 6$ km/hr

Upstream speed = $\frac{4}{1} = 4$ km/hr

Speed of the boat = $\frac{6+4}{2} = \frac{10}{2} = 5$ km/hr

Speed of the stream = $\frac{6-4}{2} = \frac{2}{2} = 1$ km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
A boatman can row a boat in downstream at 12 km/h and in upstream at 8 km/h. Find the speed of the boat that the man can row in still water and the speed of the stream.

### Solution

Speed of the boat = $$\frac{12+8}{2} = \frac{20}{2} = 10$$ km/hr

Speed of the stream = $$\frac{12-8}{2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2$$ km/hr

Hence speed of boat in still water = 10 km/h.

and speed of stream = 2 km/hr.

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
The speed of a motor boat to that of the stream is 36: 5. The boat goes against the stream in 6 hours 50 minutes, it will take the time to cover the same distance along the stream is

### Solution

Ratio of the speed of the motor boat to that of the current = 36 : 5

Let the speed of the motorboat = 36x

and speed of the stream = 5x

Downstream speed = 36x + 5x = 41x

Upstream speed = 36x - 5x = 31x

Distance = 31x × 6 = $$\frac{50}{60} = 31x \times \frac{41}{6}$$

Now, as we know from the question that Distance in both (upstream and downstream case) is same.

$$T_{\text{Downstream}} = \frac{D}{S_{\text{Downstream}}} = \frac{31x \times \frac{41}{6}}{41x} = \frac{31}{6} = 5 \text{ (1/6)}$$

= 5 hours and 10 minutes

readingSections.title: Concept 2
readingSections.content:
If it takes “(T = T$_{U}$ + T$_{D}$)” hours for a boat to reach a point in still water and comes back to the same point then, the distance between the two points can be calculated by

**Distance (D) = $$\frac{\left\{ (S_b^2 - S_s^2) \times T \right\}}{2S_b}$$**

where S$_{b}$ = Speed of the boat in still water

S$_{s}$ = Speed of the stream

T$_{U}$ = Time taken to cover the distance in upstream by the boat or a swimmer

T$_{D}$ = Time taken to cover the distance in downstream by the boat or a swimmer

T = Total time taken to cover the distance by the boat or a swimmer

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
A boat goes 360 km upstream and returns to the same point in 35 hours. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, how much distance boat will cover in still water in 6 hours?

### Solution

### Method 1

Let speed of boat in still water be ‘x’ km/h

According to question,

$$\frac{360}{x+3} + \frac{360}{x-3} = 35$$

$$360(x-3) + 360(x+3) = 35(x^2 - 3^2)$$

$$360x - 1080 + 360x + 1080 = 35x^2 - 315$$

$$35x^2 - 720x - 315 = 0$$

On Solving above, we get

$$x = 21, -3/7$$

Speed of boat in still water ‘x’ = 21 km/hr

So, distance covered by boat in 6 hours in still water = 21 × 6 = 126 km

### Method 2

Applying the formula above discussed:

$$D = \frac{\left\{ (S_b^2 - S_s^2) \times T \right\}}{2S_b}$$

$$360 = \frac{\left\{ (S_b^2 - 3^2) \times 35 \right\}}{2S_b}$$

$$720 S_b = 35 S_b^2 - 315$$

$$35 S_b^2 - 720 S_b - 315 = 0$$

$$7 S_b^2 - 144 S_b - 63 = 0$$

On Solving above, we get

$$S_b = 21, -3/7$$

$$S_b = 21 \text{ km/hr}$$

Distance covered by boat in 6 hours in still water = 21 × 6 = 126 km

readingSections.title: Concept 3
readingSections.content:
If time taken to cover the distance in Upstream = a × Time taken to cover the same distance in Downstream

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} = a \times \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}}$$

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} : \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}} = a : 1$$

Downstream Speed : Upstream Speed = a : 1

**Speed of Boat : Speed of Current (Stream) = (a + 1) : (a - 1),**
where a is a natural number.

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
Vimal can row at a speed of $4\frac{1}{2}$ km/hr in still water. If he takes 2 times as long to row a distance upstream as to row the same distance in downstream, then, the find the speed of the stream.

### Solution

(Here a = 2 is given)

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} = 2 \times \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}}$$

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} : \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}} = 2 : 1$$

Downstream Speed : Upstream Speed = 2 : 1

Speed of Boat : Speed of Current (Stream) = (2 + 1) : (2 - 1) = 3 : 1

$$3 = 4.5$$

$$\text{then } 1 = 4.5 \div 3 = 1.5 \text{ km/hr}$$

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
Sonu can row at a speed of 8 km/hr in still water. If he takes 3 times as long to row a distance upstream as to row the same distance in downstream, then, find the speed of the stream.

### Solution

(Here a = 3 is given)

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} = 3 \times \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}}$$

$$\text{Time}_{\text{Upstream}} : \text{Time}_{\text{Downstream}} = 3 : 1$$

Downstream Speed : Upstream Speed = 3 : 1

Speed of Boat : Speed of Current (Stream) = (3 + 1) : (3 - 1) = 4 : 2

$$4 = 8$$

$$\text{then } 2 = (8 \div 4) \times 2 = 4 \text{ km/hr}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 4
readingSections.content:
**Relative Speed of two boats-** Let there are two boats having their speeds in still water as x km/hr and y km/hr.

- (i) In case when both are moving in the same direction = (x - y) km/hr
- (ii) In case when both are moving in the opposite direction = (x + y) km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 8
readingSections.content:
Two boats A and B start towards each other from two places, 162 km apart. Speed of the boat A and B in still water are 12

km/hr and 15 km/hr respectively. If boat A moves downstream and boat B moves upstream, they will meet after-

### Solution

Let speed of the stream = x km/hr

Speed of boat A in downstream = (12 + x) km/hr

Speed of boat B in downstream = (15 - x) km/hr

Both the boats are moving in opposite directions, so

Relative speed = 12 + x + 15 - x = 27 km/hr

Time = [Distance/Relative Speed] = 162/27 = 6 hours

readingSections.title: Concept 5
readingSections.content:
If a person or a boat travels a distance downstream in $T_D$ hours and returns the same distance upstream in $T_U$ hours, then the speed of the man in still water will be:

$$\text{Speed of Man or boat in Still Water} = \left[ S_t \times \left\{ \frac{T_D + T_U}{T_D - T_U} \right\} \right] \text{ km/hr,}$$

where $S_t$ is the speed of the stream

readingSections.title: Example 9
readingSections.content:
Prashant can row a certain distance is 16 hours and can return the same distance is 12 hours. If the stream of flows at the rate of 8 km/h, then find the speed of Prashant in still water?

### Solution

### Method 1

Using above formula, Speed of Man or boat in Still Water

$$= \left[ S_t \times \left\{ \frac{T_D + T_U}{T_D - T_U} \right\} \right] \text{ km/hr}$$

Speed of Prashant in still water = $\left[ 8 \times \left\{ \frac{16 + 12}{16 - 12} \right\} \right] \text{ km/hr}$
= 56 km/hr

### Method 2

Let the speed of man in still water = 'x'

According to question,

$$(x - 8) \times 16 = (x + 8) \times 12$$

$$4x - 32 = 3x + 24$$

$$x = 56 \text{ km/h}$$

readingSections.title: Concept 6
readingSections.content:
If the speed of boat in still water is x km/hr and river is flowing with a speed of y km/hr, then average speed in

going to a certain place and coming back to starting point

is given by $\frac{(x + y)(x - y)}{x}$ km/hr.

readingSections.title: Example 10
readingSections.content:
A man can row in still water with a speed of $18\mathrm{km / hr}$ to go to a certain place and to come back. Find the average speed for the whole journey, if the river is flowing with a speed of $6\mathrm{km / hr}$ ?

### Solution

Average speed $= \frac{(18 + 6)(18 - 6)}{18} = 16\mathrm{km / hr}$

readingSections.title: Concept 7
readingSections.content:
If a man or boat can row $\mathrm{U}_1$ km upstream and $\mathrm{D}_1$ km downstream in $\mathrm{T}_1$ hours. Also, if a man or boat can row $\mathrm{U}_2$ km upstream and $\mathrm{D}_2$ km downstream in $\mathrm{T}_2$ hours.

Then, the upstream speed of man or boat

$$
= \left(\frac {\mathrm {U} _ {1} \mathrm {D} _ {2} - \mathrm {U} _ {2} \mathrm {D} _ {1}}{\mathrm {D} _ {2} \mathrm {T} _ {1} - \mathrm {D} _ {1} \mathrm {T} _ {2}}\right) \mathrm {k m / h r}
$$

the downstream speed of man or boat $= \left(\frac{\mathrm{U}_1\mathrm{D}_2 - \mathrm{U}_2\mathrm{D}_1}{\mathrm{U}_1\mathrm{T}_2 - \mathrm{U}_2\mathrm{T}_1}\right)$ km/hr

readingSections.title: Example 11
readingSections.content:
A boats covers $28\mathrm{km}$ upstream and $42\mathrm{km}$ downstream in 7 hours, while it covers $36\mathrm{km}$ upstream and $24\mathrm{km}$ downstream in $6\frac{1}{2}$ hours. What is the speed of the boat and stream?

### Solution

According to concept,

The upstream speed of man or boat $= \left(\frac{\mathrm{U}_1\mathrm{D}_2 - \mathrm{U}_2\mathrm{D}_1}{\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{T}_1 - \mathrm{D}_1\mathrm{T}_2}\right)\mathrm{km / hr}$

$$
= \left(\frac {2 8 \times 2 4 - 3 6 \times 4 2}{2 4 \times 7 - 4 2 \times 6 \frac {1}{2}}\right) \mathrm {k m / h r} = 8 \mathrm {k m / h}
$$

$=$ the downstream speed of man or boat

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \left(\frac {\mathrm {U} _ {1} \mathrm {D} _ {2} - \mathrm {U} _ {2} \mathrm {D} _ {1}}{\mathrm {U} _ {1} \mathrm {T} _ {2} - \mathrm {U} _ {2} \mathrm {T} _ {1}}\right) \mathrm {k m / h r} \\ = \left(\frac {2 8 \times 2 4 - 3 6 \times 4 2}{2 8 \times 6 \frac {1}{2} - 3 6 \times 7}\right) \mathrm {k m / h r} \\ = 1 2 \mathrm {k m} / \mathrm {h} \\ \end{array}
$$

Speed of the boat $= (12 + 8) / 2 = 10\mathrm{km / hr}$

Speed of the stream $= (12 - 8) / 2 = 2\mathrm{km / hr}$

### Method 2

Let the upstream speed $\mathrm{U} = \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}$ and downstream speed $\mathrm{D} = \frac{1}{\mathrm{y}}$

According to question,

$$
\frac {2 8}{\mathrm {U}} + \frac {4 2}{\mathrm {D}} = 7
$$

$$
2 8 \mathrm {x} + 4 2 \mathrm {y} = 7; 4 \mathrm {x} + 6 \mathrm {y} = 1 \quad \dots (\mathrm {I})
$$

$$
\frac {3 6}{\mathrm {U}} + \frac {2 4}{\mathrm {D}} = 6 \frac {1}{2} = \frac {1 3}{2}
$$

$$
3 6 \mathrm {x} + 2 4 \mathrm {y} = \frac {1 3}{2} \quad \dots (\mathrm {I I})
$$

On solving equation (I) and (II), we get

$$
x = \frac {1}{8}, y = \frac {1}{1 2}
$$

$\mathrm{D} = 12\mathrm{km / hr};\mathrm{U} = 8\mathrm{km / hr}$

Speed of the boat $= (12 + 8) / 2 = 10\mathrm{km / hr}$

Speed of the stream $= (12 - 8) / 2 = 2\mathrm{km / hr}$

readingSections.title: Example 12
readingSections.content:
In a swimming championship, a swimmer swims from a point P against a stream for 5 minutes and then swims backwards in favour of the stream for next 5 minutes and come to the point Q. If PQ is 200 metres, find the speed of the stream in $\mathrm{km / hr}$ is -

### Solution

Let the speed of swimmer in still water $= \mathrm{x}$ km/hr and speed of the stream $= \mathrm{y}$ km/hr

![Book diagram, page 172](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p172-img-54.jpeg)

Upstream speed $(\mathrm{x} - \mathrm{y}) = \frac{\mathrm{PR}}{5}\times 60 = 12\times \mathrm{PR}$

Downstream speed $(\mathrm{x} + \mathrm{y}) = \frac{\mathrm{QR}}{5}\times 60 = 12\times \mathrm{QR}$

According to Question,

$$
Q R - P R = 2 0 0
$$

$$
x + y - x + y = 1 2 \times 2 0 0
$$

$$
2 y = 2 4 0 0
$$

$$
y = 1 2 0 0 \mathrm {m} / \mathrm {h r} = 1. 2 \mathrm {k m} / \mathrm {h r}
$$

![Book diagram, page 173](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p173-img-55.jpeg)

chapters.content:
Chapter
20
DATA INTERPRETATION
DATA INTERPRETATION
Data interpretation is a process where you make sense
of information presented in mathematical forms. Here’s
how it works:
1. Understand the Data: Begin by examining the
information presented, which could be in the form
of figures, diagrams, or tabular data. It’s crucial to
comprehend what these data points signify.
2. Identify Key Points: Next, you identify important
points in the data. This could be the highest or lowest
values, trends over time, or significant changes.
3. Analyze Relationships: You then look at how different
parts of the data relate to each other. This could involve
comparing different sets of numbers, looking at how one
variable affects another, or finding patterns in the data.
4. Draw Conclusions: Based on your analysis, you draw
conclusions about what the data means. This could
involve making predictions about future data, explaining
why certain patterns exist, or identifying the cause of
certain trends.
5. Communicate Findings: Finally, you communicate
your findings. This could involve explaining your
conclusions to others, writing a report, or creating a
presentation.
Data interpretation is about understanding and making sense of
data to draw meaningful conclusions. In data interpretation the
information is given in the form of charts that is given below.
TABULAR CHART
A tabular chart is a chart that consists of rows and columns.
To select data, it is necessary to find the intersection point
of two different terms given in the rows and columns.

4.
Savings of Ram = [100 - (20 + 30 + 40 + 5 + 5)]%
= 0% = 0
PIE CHART
A pie chart is a graphical representation that organizes data
into a circular shape. This data can be expressed in both
percentage (%) and angular (°) forms.
a) Pie chart in percentage (%) : In a pie chart represented
in percentages (%), the entire circle is considered to be
100%. If the percentage value of any section is not given,
it can be determined by subtracting the sum of all known
sections from 100%.
For example, if a pie chart has three sections: Section A
is 20%, Section B is 30%, and the percentage value for
Section C is not given, we can calculate it as follows:
Section C = Total percentage of a circle - (Section A +
Section B) = 100% - (20% + 30%) = 50%
So, Section C would be 50%. This way, we can determine
the percentage value of any unknown section in a pie chart.



CASELET DI
A caselet in data interpretation presents data in text form, not
graphs. The text’s length and detail can vary, and the data
could be logical or numerical. To solve these, read the text
carefully, identify key points, and consider creating your own
visual aids for better understanding.

readingSections.title: Introduction
readingSections.content:
Data interpretation is a process where you make sense of information presented in mathematical forms. Here's how it works:

1. **Understand the Data:** Begin by examining the information presented, which could be in the form of figures, diagrams, or tabular data. It's crucial to comprehend what these data points signify.
2. **Identify Key Points:** Next, you identify important points in the data. This could be the highest or lowest values, trends over time, or significant changes.
3. **Analyze Relationships:** You then look at how different parts of the data relate to each other. This could involve comparing different sets of numbers, looking at how one variable affects another, or finding patterns in the data.
4. **Draw Conclusions:** Based on your analysis, you draw conclusions about what the data means. This could involve making predictions about future data, explaining why certain patterns exist, or identifying the cause of certain trends.
5. **Communicate Findings:** Finally, you communicate your findings. This could involve explaining your conclusions to others, writing a report, or creating a presentation.

Data interpretation is about understanding and making sense of data to draw meaningful conclusions. In data interpretation the information is given in the form of charts that is given below.

![Book diagram, page 175](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p175-img-56.jpeg)

readingSections.title: TABULAR CHART
readingSections.content: A tabular chart is a chart that consists of rows and columns. To select data, it is necessary to find the intersection point of two different terms given in the rows and columns.

readingSections.title: Example 1
readingSections.content:
Read the chart carefully in which given % expense of 5 different people in July of a particular year.

|   | Cloths | Food | Rent | Travelling | Entertainment  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  Ram | 20 | 30 | 40 | 5 | 5  |
|  Ranjan | 10 | 12 | 25 | 20 | 15  |
|  Krishna | 18 | 24 | 8 | 10 | 25  |
|  Hanumaan | 10 | 50 | 5 | 5 | 10  |
|  Jitu | 20 | 20 | 20 | 12 | 3  |

1. If Krishna's total savings amount to Rs 45000, what is his salary?
2. What is the average salary of Ram and Hanuman if they spend Rs 4500 and Rs 3200 on clothes respectively?
3. What is the ratio of Jitu's salary to Ranjan's if their respective expenses for traveling and rent are Rs 8000 and Rs 7500?
4. What are Ram's savings if he spends Rs 2145.7 on entertainment?

### Solution

1. Savings of Krishna = [100 - (18 + 24 + 8 + 10 + 25)]% = 15%

$$\text{Salary of Krishna} = \frac{45000}{15\%} \times 100\% = 300,000$$

2. Salary of Ram = $\frac{4500}{20\%} \times 100\% = 22500$

$$\text{Salary of Hanumaan} = \frac{3200}{10\%} \times 100\% = 32000$$

Average salary

$$= \frac{\text{Salary of Ram} + \text{Salary of Hanuman}}{2}$$

$$= \frac{22500 + 32000}{2} = 27250$$

3. Salary of Jitu : Salary of Ranjan

$$= \frac{8000}{12\%} \times 100\% : \frac{7500}{25\%} \times 100\% = 20 : 9$$

4. Savings of Ram = [100 - (20 + 30 + 40 + 5 + 5)]%

$$= 0\% = 0$$

readingSections.title: PIE CHART
readingSections.content:
A pie chart is a graphical representation that organizes data into a circular shape. This data can be expressed in both percentage (%) and angular (°) forms.

a) **Pie chart in percentage (%)** : In a pie chart represented in percentages (%), the entire circle is considered to be 100%. If the percentage value of any section is not given, it can be determined by subtracting the sum of all known sections from 100%.

For example, if a pie chart has three sections: Section A is 20%, Section B is 30%, and the percentage value for Section C is not given, we can calculate it as follows:

Section C = Total percentage of a circle - (Section A + Section B) = 100% - (20% + 30%) = 50%

So, Section C would be 50%. This way, we can determine the percentage value of any unknown section in a pie chart.

readingSections.title: Example 2
readingSections.content:
The given chart illustrates the percentage of the total journey covered by Amit using different vehicles. If Amit's total journey is 900 km, please refer to the questions below for further details.

JOURNEY DETAILS OF DIFFERENT VEHICLE PERCENTAGE WISE

![Book diagram, page 176](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p176-img-57.jpeg)

1. If the speed of the bike and car is 40 km/hr and 60 km/hr respectively, then find the average speed during these sections of the journey.
2. Find the time for which Amit travels by train if the speed of the train is 90 km/hr.
3. Find the speed of the bike in km/hr if Amit took 120 minutes to travel by bike.
4. If the price of an auto ride for the first km is Rs 25 and thereafter it's Rs 5 per km, then find the total fare for the auto ride.

### Solution

1. The distance traveled by bike in percentage is calculated as follows = 100% - (20+12+31+25)% = 12%

Given that the distance traveled by bike and car is the same, we can calculate the average speed as follows

$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times 60}{40 + 60} = 48 \text{ km/hr}$$

2. The time taken by Amit by train is calculated as follows

$$= \frac{\text{Distance travelled}}{\text{Speed of train}} = \frac{25\% \text{ of } 900}{90} = 2.5 \text{ hour}$$
$$= 2 \text{ hours and } 30 \text{ minutes}$$

3. Time taken = $\frac{120 \text{ minute}}{60} = 2 \text{ hour}$

The speed of the bike is calculated as follows

$$= \frac{\text{Distance travelled}}{\text{Time taken}} = \frac{12\% \text{ of } 900}{2} = 54 \text{ km/hr}$$

4. The distance traveled by auto is calculated as follows = 31% of 900 = 279 km

The fare for this distance is calculated as follows = 1 × 25 + (279-1) × 5 = Rs 1415

b) **Pie chart in degree (°)** : In a pie chart represented in degrees (°), the entire circle is considered to be 360°. If the degree value of any section is not given, it can be determined by subtracting the sum of all known sections from 360°.

For example, if a pie chart has three sections: Section A is 120°, Section B is 90°, and the degree value for Section C is not given, we can calculate it as follows:

Section C = Total degrees of a circle - (Section A + Section B) = 360° - (120° + 90°) = 150°

So, Section C would be 150°. This way, we can determine the degree value of any unknown section in a pie chart.

readingSections.title: Conversion between Percentage and degree
readingSections.content:
I. If you're dealing with a value in degrees and you want to convert it to a percentage, you can use this formula:

$$\text{Percentage value} = \frac{\text{Degree value}}{360^\circ} \times 100\%$$

II. Conversely, if you have a value in percentage and you need to convert it to degrees, you can use this formula:

$$\text{Degree value} = \frac{\text{Percentage value}}{100\%} \times 360^\circ$$

readingSections.title: Example 3
readingSections.content:
In an election between 5 candidates four candidates excluding winner they gets 40°, 45°, 60° and 90° votes.

![Book diagram, page 176](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p176-img-58.jpeg)

1. If the total number of votes is 1440, then find the votes for the winning candidate.
2. If \(25\%\) of voters did not cast their votes and Deepak received 4500 votes, then find the total number of voters.
3. What percentage of votes did Akhil receive if all voters cast their vote?
4. If Ram won by 459 votes over Rahul, then find the number of votes received by Isha.

### Solution

1. The number of votes received by Ram in degrees $= 360^{\circ}$ - $(40 + 45 + 60 + 90) = 125^{\circ}$

Therefore, Ram is the winning candidate

Now, The number of votes received by Ram

$$
= 125^{\circ} \text{ of } 1440 = \frac{125}{360} \times 1440 = 500
$$

2. Let's denote the total number of voters as 'x'

The number of votes received by Deepak $= 60^{\circ}$ of (100-25)% of x

$$
\begin{array}{l} 4500 = \frac{60}{360} \times \frac{75}{100} \times x \\ x = 36000 \end{array}
$$

3. The percentage of votes received by Akhil

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \frac{\text{Degree value of votes gets by Akhil}}{360^{\circ}} \times 100\% \\ = \frac{45^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}} \times 100\% = 12.5\% \end{array}
$$

4. The number of votes received by Isha $= \frac{459}{85^{\circ}} \times 90^{\circ} = 486$

readingSections.title: BAR GRAPH
readingSections.content:
A bar diagram is a visual tool that uses bars to depict data. The dimension of the bar, either its height or length, represents the magnitude of the data. Bar diagrams can be arranged in either a vertical or horizontal manner and are effective for contrasting various data categories.

1. Vertical Bar Diagram: This diagram type presents data categories on the x-axis (horizontal axis) and data values on the y-axis (vertical axis). Each bar represents a data category, with the height of the bar corresponding to its data value.
2. Horizontal Bar Diagram: In this format, the data categories are presented on the y-axis and the data values on the x-axis. Each bar represents a data category, with the length of the bar corresponding to its data value.
3. Stacked Bar Diagram: In this diagram type, each bar represents a total, which is divided into segments that represent different sub-categories.
4. Grouped Bar Diagram: In this format, bars are grouped by category, with each bar representing a different subcategory.
5. Percentage or \(100\%\) Stacked Bar Diagram: In this diagram type, each bar represents a total of \(100\%\). It's

useful for comparing proportions or percentages across different categories.

readingSections.title: Example 4
readingSections.content:
Please read the chart carefully. It shows the investment (in lakhs) and the respective selling price percentages of five members who sell their items.

Amount invested (in Lakhs) and Selling Price (%)

![Book diagram, page 177](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p177-img-59.jpeg)

1. Find the profit of Amit in Rupees.
2. Find the total profit or loss by all.
3. Find the ratio of selling price of Amrita and Ajit.

### Solution

1. Profit of Amit \(= (160 - 100)\%\) of 4000000 \(= 2400000\)
2. Loss of Anuj \(= (100 - 70)\%\) of 2500000 \(= 750000\)

Profit of Ajit $= (120 - 100)\%$ of 3000000 $= 600000$

Profit of Amit $= (160 - 100)\%$ of 4000000 $= 2400000$

Profit of Anjali $= (125 - 100)\%$ of 3500000 $= 875000$

Loss of Amrita $= (100 - 80)\%$ of 4500000 $= 900000$

Total Profit $= (-750000 + 600000 + 2400000 + 875000 - 900000) = 2225000$

3. Selling price by Amrita : Selling price by Ajit $= 80\%$ of 4500000 : $120\%$ of 3000000 $= 1:1$

readingSections.title: LINE GRAPH
readingSections.content: A line graph is a chart that uses lines to connect data points representing a quantity at different times. It's useful for showing trends over time and making predictions about future data points.

readingSections.title: Example 5
readingSections.content:
The graph shows the selling of cars of two different companies Tata and Hyundai in different years (in thousands).

![Book diagram, page 177](/content-assets/ssc-cgl/quant-book/ocr-p177-img-60.jpeg)

183

1. If the cost price per unit of Hyundai cars and Tata cars is Rs 1,005,000 and Rs 1,010,000 respectively in all years, then which company's income is higher and by how much in all years?
2. Find the ratio of the average selling price of Hyundai cars in 2020, 2022, and 2023 to that of Tata cars in 2020, 2021, and 2022.
3. If from 2020 to 2023, Tata cars had color issues in 10%, 5%, 20%, and 15% of the units respectively, and the company had to refund 50% of the amount to customers after their claims, then what is the actual profit percentage of the company now (approximately)? Assume that the company had pre-decided to take a 20% profit on each car and that the cost price of each car is Rs 1 million.
4. In how many years did Tata do more business in terms of the number of cars sold?

### Solution

1. Total income of Company = number of car sold × cost of per unit car

$$\text{The Income of Tata} = (16000 + 24000 + 42000 + 32000) \times 1010000 = 1,15,14,00,00,000$$

$$\text{The Income of Hyundai} = (24000 + 36000 + 12000 + 40000) \times 1005000 = 1,12,56,00,00,000$$

$$\text{The Income of Tata is more} = 115140000000 - 112560000000 = \text{Rs } 258,00,00,000$$

2. Average selling of Hyundai in 2020, 2022 and 2023

$$= \frac{24000 + 12000 + 40000}{3} = \frac{76000}{3}$$

Average selling of Tata in 2020, 2021 and 2022

$$= \frac{16000 + 24000 + 42000}{3} = \frac{82000}{3}$$

Ratio of average selling of Hyundai : Ratio of average selling of Tata

$$= \frac{76000}{3} : \frac{82000}{3} = 38 : 41$$

3. Total cars sold by Tata = 16000 + 24000 + 42000 + 32000 = 114000

$$\text{Cost price of Cars} = 114000 \times 10 \text{ Lakh} = 1140000 \text{ Lakh}$$

$$\text{Total selling} = 114000 \times 10 \text{ Lakh} \times \frac{120}{100} = 1368000 \text{ Lakh}$$

$$\text{Color issue in cars} = 10\% \text{ of } 16000 + 5\% \text{ of } 24000 + 20\% \text{ of } 42000 + 15\% \text{ of } 32000 = 16000$$

$$\text{Returned amount} = 16000 \times 5 \text{ Lakh} = 80000 \text{ Lakh}$$

$$\text{So Final Income} = 1368000 \text{ Lakh} - 80000 \text{ Lakh} = 1288000 \text{ Lakh}$$

$$\text{Profit percent} = \frac{1288000 \text{ Lakh} - 1140000 \text{ Lakh}}{1140000 \text{ Lakh}} \times 100\% = 12.98\% \text{ (Approx)}$$

4. 1 year ( In 2022 only)

readingSections.title: CASELET DI
readingSections.content: A caselet in data interpretation presents data in text form, not graphs. The text's length and detail can vary, and the data could be logical or numerical. To solve these, read the text carefully, identify key points, and consider creating your own visual aids for better understanding.

readingSections.title: Example 6
readingSections.content:
In a garden, 30% of the plants are fruit-bearing, 50% are flowers, and the remaining are vegetables. Among the fruit plants, 20% are Pineapples, 16.66% are Grapes, and the remaining 361 plants are Blackberry. The flower plants consist of four types: Sunflowers, Dahlia, Tulipes, and Daisys, which are in the ratio of 1:2:3:4 respectively. The vegetable section comprises three types of vegetables: Onion, Brinjal, and Pumpkin. The quantity of Onion is 60% more than that of Brinjal, and Pumpkin is 12.5% less than Onion.

1. What is the ratio of the sum of Dahlia and Brinjals to the difference between Dahlia and Grapes?
2. Find the total number of plants in the garden, excluding Pineapples and Pumpkins.
3. If 1100 more fruit plants are added to the garden, what is the percentage of Sunflower plants now?
4. By what percentage is Onion more or less than Tulip?
5. If 216 more plants are added to the garden, what is the percentage of Blackberry plants now?

### Solution

Total plants in the garden = 100%

|  Total plants 100%  |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  Fruits 30% |   |   | Flowers 50% |   |   |   | Vegetable 20%  |   |   |
|  Pineapple | Grapes | Blackberry | Sunflower | Dahlia | Tulip | Daisy | Onion | Brinjal | Pumpkin  |
|  6% | 5% | 19% | 5% | 10% | 15% | 20% | 8% | 5% | 7%  |

1. (Dahlia + Brinjal) : (Dahlia - Grapes) = (10% + 5%) : (10% - 5%) = 15 : 5 = 3 : 1

2. Blackberry = 19% = 361, so 1% = 19

$$\text{Total plants excluding Pineapple and Pumpkin} = 100\% - (6\% + 7\%) = 87\% = 87 \times 19 = 1653$$

3. Total number of plants after increase = 19 × 100 + 1100 = 3000

$$\text{Total number of Sunflowers} = 19 \times 5 = 95$$

$$\text{Percentage of Sunflowers} = \frac{95}{3000} \times 100\% = 3.16\%$$

4. Onion % = 8%, Tulip % = 15%

$$\text{Required \%} = \frac{7}{15} \times 100 = 46.66\%$$

5. Since it is not specified whether the new plants include Blackberry, we cannot calculate the percentage of Blackberry plants if an additional 216 plants are added to the garden.

readingSections.title: Example 7
readingSections.content:
The given pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the population of Town A, Town B, Town C, Town D and Town E and the table chart shows the ratio of male and female in each town, read it carefully and solve the questions below. If the total population of all towns is 5,00,000.

1. Find the number of males in town C.
2. What is the difference between number of males in town C and number of females in town E?
3. If the population of Town D is increased by 23% in next year and the ratio of males and females is inverse then what is the population of males in Town D now.
4. Find the difference between the population of highest population and lowest population in town.

### Solution

1. Population of Town C = 13% of 5,00,000 = 65000

$$\text{Number of males in town C} = \frac{65000}{10} \times 9 = 58500$$

2. Number of males in Town C = 58500

3. Population of males in Town D = 500000 × $\frac{14}{100}$ × $\frac{123}{100}$ × $\frac{8}{15}$ = 45920

4. Difference between the population of highest population and lowest population in town = 500000 × $\frac{(30-13)}{100} = 85000$
